revision.text:
{{日本の古墳 |名称=西山古墳 |画像=[[画像:NisiyamaKofun-01.jpg|250px|]]
後方部の西側より |所在地=[[奈良県]][[天理市]]杣之内町 |位置={{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|34|35|33|N|135|50|36|E|scale:10000}} |形状=[[前方後方墳]] |規模=全長183m 高さ13m |埋葬施設=[[竪穴式石室]] |築造年代=古墳時代前期 |被葬者= |出土品=鏡・石鏃・鉄製刀剣類の破片、管玉、埴輪ほか |史跡指定=国史跡（1927年4月8日指定） |特記事項= }} '''西山古墳'''（にしやまこふん）は、[[奈良県]][[天理市]]杣之内（そまのうち）町にある[[古墳]]で、国の[[史跡]]に指定されている。 == 概要 == 築造時期は[[古墳時代]]前期（4世紀）と見られており、同古墳が属する[[杣之内古墳群]]の中でも最も古い時期に造られた古墳である。墳丘は前方部を西に向けた3段構築の[[前方後方墳]]で、全長183メートル、後円部の幅94メートル 高さ16メートル、前方部の幅72メートル。これは全国にある前方後方墳の中でもっとも規模の大きいものである。墳丘は1段目のみが前方後方墳の形で、その上に[[前方後円墳]]がのっているというきわめて特異な形をしており、当初からこの形であったことは間違いないとみられている『大和の古墳I』泉森皎編 人文書院（2003年）。 後方部中心には[[竪穴式石室]]があるが、すでに盗掘を受けているとみられている。第2次世界大戦中には旧日本軍により対空砲の陣地がおかれ、このさいに竪穴式石室の石材（[[柏原市]]芝山産）が堀りだされたとされる天理教育委員会による現地説明板による。 == 現状 == 墳丘の保存状態は良く、樹木が生えていないため段築をはっきりと観察することができる。 == アクセス == 天理駅より徒歩約20分。[[天理参考館]]の南約500メートル、[[天理中学校]]すぐ北。 == 脚注 == {{reflist}} == 参考資料 == * 天理市教育委員会設置現地説明板 * 天理市ホームページ 古墳ガイド == 関連項目 == * [[杣之内古墳群]] * [[日本の古墳一覧#奈良県|奈良県の古墳一覧]] * [[近畿の史跡一覧#奈良県|奈良県の史跡一覧]] == 外部リンク == *[http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html 天理市ホームページ|古墳ガイド] [[Category:天理市]] [[Category:奈良県の古墳]] [[Category:奈良県にある日本の史跡]]

revision.comment: 双方中方墳、副葬品等
revision.text:
{{日本の古墳 |名称=西山古墳 |画像=[[画像:NisiyamaKofun-01.jpg|250px|]]
後方部の西側より |所在地=[[奈良県]][[天理市]]杣之内町 |位置={{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|34|35|33|N|135|50|36|E|scale:10000}} |形状=[[前方後方墳]] |規模=全長183m 高さ13m |埋葬施設=[[竪穴式石室]] |築造年代=古墳時代前期 |被葬者= |出土品=鏡・石鏃・鉄製刀剣類の破片、管玉、埴輪ほか |史跡指定=国の史跡（1927年4月8日指定） |特記事項= }} '''西山古墳'''（にしやまこふん）は、[[奈良県]][[天理市]]御経野町・勾田町・杣之内（そまのうち）町にある[[古墳]]で、1927年（昭和2年）国の[[史跡]]に指定されている。別称はナガリヤマ（勾山[まがりやま]）。 == 概要 == 築造時期は[[古墳時代]]前期（4世紀）と見られており、同古墳が属する[[杣之内古墳群]]の中でも最も古い時期に造られた古墳である。 後方部中心には[[竪穴式石室]]があるが、すでに盗掘を受けているとみられている。 第2次世界大戦中には旧日本軍により対空砲の陣地がおかれ、このさいに竪穴式石室の石材（[[柏原市]]芝山産）が堀り出されたとされる天理教育委員会による現地説明板による。 == 規模・形状 == 墳丘は前方部を西に向けた3段構築の[[前方後方墳]]で、全長183メートル、後円部の幅94メートル 高さ16メートル、前方部の幅72メートル。 下段が前方後方形で、中段から上は前方後円形となる特殊な墳形をもつ。下段の後方部は一辺90メートルの正方形で、これに同じ長さの前方部が付いている。中段は前方後円型をしていて、後円丘径72メートル、前方丘全長90メートル。墳頂部は径30メートルが平坦で、前方部先端は主軸に直交する横長形となっている。後方部高さ15～10メートル。 緩やかな傾斜地に立地し、三本の尾根の中央部を墳丘に、北と南の尾根を外堤として、自然地形を有効に利用しているため濠幅は一定しないが、全長200メートル以上の双方中方墳とも考えられる。濠は現在埋め立てられているが、階段状の方形の濠が巡らされていたと考えられる。現状では前方後方形の墳丘と見られるが、地形改変が進んでいることなどを考慮して、双方中方墳の可能性もある泉森皎「西山古墳」文化庁文化財保護部史跡研究会監修『図説　日本の史跡　第3巻　原始3』同朋舎出版　1991年　36ページ。 これは日本にある前方後方墳の中でもっとも規模の大きいものである。墳丘は1段目のみが前方後方墳の形で、その上に[[前方後円墳]]が乗るというきわめて特異な形をしており、当初からこの形であったことは間違いないとみられている『大和の古墳I』泉森皎編 人文書院（2003年）。 == 副葬品・出土品 == 後方部からは、銅鏡片、碧玉製鏃、管玉、鉄剣・鉄刀片が出土している。前方部南側濠内から碧玉製車輪石1が検出されている。傾斜斜面には葺き石が、埴輪片がみられ、円筒埴輪、鰭付（ひれつき）円筒埴輪、家形埴輪が見つかっている。 == 現状 == 墳丘の保存状態は良く、樹木が生えていないため段築をはっきりと観察することができる。 == アクセス == 天理駅より徒歩約20分。[[天理参考館]]の南約500メートル、[[天理中学校]]すぐ北。 == 脚注 == {{reflist}} == 参考資料 == * 天理市教育委員会設置現地説明板 * 天理市ホームページ 古墳ガイド == 関連項目 == * [[杣之内古墳群]] * [[日本の古墳一覧#奈良県|奈良県の古墳一覧]] * [[近畿の史跡一覧#奈良県|奈良県の史跡一覧]] == 外部リンク == *[http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html 天理市ホームページ|古墳ガイド] {{DEFAULTSORT:にしやま こふん}} [[Category:天理市]] [[Category:奈良県の古墳]] [[Category:奈良県にある国指定の史跡]]

{{日本の古墳 |名称=西山古墳 |画像=[[画像:NisiyamaKofun-01.jpg|250px|]]
後方部の西側より |所在地=[[奈良県]][[天理市]]杣之内町 |位置={{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|34|35|33|N|135|50|36|E|scale:10000}} |形状=[[前方後方墳]] |規模=全長183m 高さ13m |埋葬施設=[[竪穴式石室]] |築造年代=古墳時代前期 |被葬者= |出土品=鏡・石鏃・鉄製刀剣類の破片、管玉、埴輪ほか |史跡指定=国の史跡（1927年4月8日指定） |特記事項= }} '''西山古墳'''（にしやまこふん）は、[[奈良県]][[天理市]]御経野町・勾田町・杣之内（そまのうち）町にある[[古墳]]で、1927年（昭和2年）国の[[史跡]]に指定されている。別称はナガリヤマ（勾山[まがりやま]）。 == 概要 == 築造時期は[[古墳時代]]前期（4世紀）と見られており、同古墳が属する[[杣之内古墳群]]の中でも最も古い時期に造られた古墳である。 後方部中心には[[竪穴式石室]]があるが、すでに盗掘を受けているとみられている。 第2次世界大戦中には旧日本軍により対空砲の陣地がおかれ、このさいに竪穴式石室の石材（[[柏原市]]芝山産）が堀り出されたとされる天理教育委員会による現地説明板による。 == 規模・形状 == [[画像:Tenri-nishiyama_stereo.jpg|thumb|350px|西山古墳の[[ステレオグラム|ステレオ]]空中写真（1985年） {{国土航空写真}}]] 墳丘は前方部を西に向けた3段構築の[[前方後方墳]]で、全長183メートル、後円部の幅94メートル 高さ16メートル、前方部の幅72メートル。 下段が前方後方形で、中段から上は前方後円形となる特殊な墳形をもつ。下段の後方部は一辺90メートルの正方形で、これに同じ長さの前方部が付いている。中段は前方後円型をしていて、後円丘径72メートル、前方丘全長90メートル。墳頂部は径30メートルが平坦で、前方部先端は主軸に直交する横長形となっている。後方部高さ15～10メートル。 緩やかな傾斜地に立地し、三本の尾根の中央部を墳丘に、北と南の尾根を外堤として、自然地形を有効に利用しているため濠幅は一定しないが、全長200メートル以上の双方中方墳とも考えられる。濠は現在埋め立てられているが、階段状の方形の濠が巡らされていたと考えられる。現状では前方後方形の墳丘と見られるが、地形改変が進んでいることなどを考慮して、双方中方墳の可能性もある泉森皎「西山古墳」文化庁文化財保護部史跡研究会監修『図説　日本の史跡　第3巻　原始3』同朋舎出版　1991年　36ページ。 これは日本にある前方後方墳の中でもっとも規模の大きいものである。墳丘は1段目のみが前方後方墳の形で、その上に[[前方後円墳]]が乗るというきわめて特異な形をしており、当初からこの形であったことは間違いないとみられている『大和の古墳I』泉森皎編 人文書院（2003年）。 == 副葬品・出土品 == 後方部からは、銅鏡片、碧玉製鏃、管玉、鉄剣・鉄刀片が出土している。前方部南側濠内から碧玉製車輪石1が検出されている。傾斜斜面には葺き石が、埴輪片がみられ、円筒埴輪、鰭付（ひれつき）円筒埴輪、家形埴輪が見つかっている。 == 現状 == 墳丘の保存状態は良く、樹木が生えていないため段築をはっきりと観察することができる。 == アクセス == 天理駅より徒歩約20分。[[天理参考館]]の南約500メートル、[[天理中学校]]すぐ北。 == 脚注 == {{reflist}} == 参考資料 == * 天理市教育委員会設置現地説明板 * 天理市ホームページ 古墳ガイド == 関連項目 == * [[杣之内古墳群]] * [[日本の古墳一覧#奈良県|奈良県の古墳一覧]] * [[近畿の史跡一覧#奈良県|奈良県の史跡一覧]] == 外部リンク == *[http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html 天理市ホームページ|古墳ガイド] {{DEFAULTSORT:にしやま こふん}} [[Category:天理市]] [[Category:奈良県の古墳]] [[Category:奈良県にある国指定の史跡]]

*[http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html 天理市ホームページ|古墳ガイド] {{DEFAULTSORT:にしやまこふん}} [[Category:奈良県の古墳]] [[Category:天理市の歴史]] [[Category:奈良県にある国指定の史跡]] [[Category:前方後方墳]]

{{日本の古墳 |名称=西山古墳 |画像=[[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px|]]
墳丘全景（左に前方部、右奥に後方部） |所在地=[[奈良県]][[天理市]]杣之内町 |緯度度 = 34|緯度分 = 35|緯度秒 = 33 |経度度 =135|経度分 = 50|経度秒 = 36 |ISO = JP-29 |形状=[[前方後方墳]] |規模=全長183m 高さ13m |埋葬施設=[[竪穴式石室]] |築造年代=古墳時代前期 |被葬者=[[物部氏]]一族？ |出土品=鏡・石鏃・鉄製刀剣類の破片、管玉、埴輪ほか |史跡指定=国の史跡（1927年4月8日指定） |特記事項= |地図 = Japan Nara |アイコン = 前方後方墳-西 }} '''西山古墳'''（にしやまこふん）は、[[奈良県]][[天理市]]御経野町・勾田町・杣之内（そまのうち）町にある[[古墳]]で、1927年（昭和2年）国の[[史跡]]に指定{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}されている。別称はナガリヤマ（勾山[まがりやま]）。 == 概要 == 築造時期は[[古墳時代]]前期（4世紀）と見られており、同古墳が属する[[杣之内古墳群]]の中でも最も古い時期に造られた古墳である。 後方部中心には[[竪穴式石室]]があるが、すでに盗掘を受けているとみられている。 第2次世界大戦中には旧日本軍により対空砲の陣地がおかれ、このさいに竪穴式石室の石材（[[柏原市]]芝山産）が掘り出されたとされる天理教育委員会による現地説明板による。 == 規模・形状 == [[画像:Tenri-nishiyama_stereo.jpg|thumb|350px|西山古墳の[[ステレオグラム|ステレオ]]空中写真（1985年） {{国土航空写真}}]] 墳丘は前方部を西に向けた3段構築の[[前方後方墳]]で、全長183メートル、後円部の幅94メートル 高さ16メートル、前方部の幅72メートル。 下段が前方後方形で、中段から上は前方後円形となる特殊な墳形をもつ。下段の後方部は一辺90メートルの正方形で、これに同じ長さの前方部が付いている。中段は前方後円型をしていて、後円丘径72メートル、前方丘全長90メートル。墳頂部は径30メートルが平坦で、前方部方向に7メートル下がって細長い前方部が続き、、前方部先端はくびれ部より2メートル高く主軸に直交する横長形となっている。後方部高さは南側で15メートルで、前方部の高さも南側で10メートル。 後方部頂上が盗掘されている。その時の記録から[[竪穴式石室]]であったと推定されている。 緩やかな傾斜地に立地し、三本の尾根の中央部を墳丘に、北と南の尾根を外堤として、自然地形を有効に利用しているため濠幅は一定しないが、全長200メートル以上の双方中方墳とも考えられる。濠は現在埋め立てられているが、階段状の方形の濠階段状の濠は「伝崇神天皇陵」古墳でもみられる。が巡らされていたと考えられる。現状では前方後方形の墳丘と見られるが、地形改変が進んでいることなどを考慮して、双方中方墳の可能性もある泉森皎「西山古墳」文化庁文化財保護部史跡研究会監修『図説　日本の史跡　第3巻　原始3』同朋舎出版　1991年　36ページ。 これは日本にある前方後方墳の中でもっとも規模の大きいものである。墳丘は1段目のみが前方後方墳の形で、その上に[[前方後円墳]]が乗るというきわめて特異な形をしており、当初からこの形であったことは間違いないとみられている『大和の古墳I』泉森皎編 人文書院（2003年）。 == 副葬品・出土品 == 後方部からは、銅鏡片、碧玉製鏃、管玉、鉄剣・鉄刀片が出土している。前方部南側濠内から碧玉製車輪石1が検出されている。傾斜斜面には葺き石が、埴輪片がみられ、円筒埴輪、鰭付（ひれつき）円筒埴輪、家形埴輪が見つかっている。 == 現状 == 墳丘の保存状態は良く、樹木が生えていないため段築をはっきりと観察することができる。 == アクセス == 天理駅より徒歩約20分。[[天理大学附属天理参考館]]の南約500メートル、[[天理中学校]]すぐ北。 == 脚注 == {{reflist}} == 参考資料 == * 天理市教育委員会設置現地説明板 * 天理市ホームページ 古墳ガイド == 関連項目 == * [[杣之内古墳群]] == 外部リンク == {{Commonscat|Nishiyama Kofun}} *[http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html 天理市ホームページ|古墳ガイド] {{DEFAULTSORT:にしやまこふん}} [[Category:奈良県の古墳]] [[Category:天理市の歴史]] [[Category:奈良県にある国指定の史跡]] [[Category:前方後方墳]]

== [[画像:Tenri-nishiyama_stereo.jpg|thumb|350px|西山古墳の[[ステレオグラム|ステレオ]]空中写真（1985年） {{国土航空写真}}]] 墳丘は前方部を西に向けた3段構築の[[前方後方墳]]で、全長183メートル、後円部の幅94メートル 高さ16メートル、前方部の幅72メートル。 下段が前方後方形で、中段から上は前方後円形となる特殊な墳形をもつ。下段の後方部は一辺90メートルの正方形で、これに同じ長さの前方部が付いている。中段は前方後円型をしていて、後円丘径72メートル、前方丘全長90メートル。墳頂部は径30メートルが平坦で、前方部方向に7メートル下がって細長い前方部が続き、、前方部先端はくびれ部より2メートル高く主軸に直交する横長形となっている。後方部高さは南側で15メートルで、前方部の高さも南側で10メートル。 後方部頂上が盗掘されている。その時の記録から[[竪穴式石室]]であったと推定されている。 緩やかな傾斜地に立地し、三本の尾根の中央部を墳丘に、北と南の尾根を外堤として、自然地形を有効に利用しているため濠幅は一定しないが、全長200メートル以上の双方中方墳とも考えられる。濠は現在埋め立てられているが、階段状の方形の濠階段状の濠は「伝崇神天皇陵」古墳でもみられる。が巡らされていたと考えられる。現状では前方後方形の墳丘と見られるが、地形改変が進んでいることなどを考慮して、双方中方墳の可能性もある泉森皎「西山古墳」文化庁文化財保護部史跡研究会監修『図説　日本の史跡　第3巻　原始3』同朋舎出版　1991年　36ページ。 これは日本にある前方後方墳の中でもっとも規模の大きいものである。墳丘は1段目のみが前方後方墳の形で、その上に[[前方後円墳]]が乗るというきわめて特異な形をしており、当初からこの形であったことは間違いないとみられている『大和の古墳I』泉森皎編 人文書院（2003年）。 == 副葬品・出土品 == 後方部からは、銅鏡片、碧玉製鏃、管玉、鉄剣・鉄刀片が出土している。前方部南側濠内から碧玉製車輪石1が検出されている。傾斜斜面には葺き石が、埴輪片がみられ、円筒埴輪、鰭付（ひれつき）円筒埴輪、家形埴輪が見つかっている。 == 現状 == 墳丘の保存状態は良く、樹木が生えていないため段築をはっきりと観察することができる。 == アクセス == 天理駅より徒歩約20分。[[天理大学附属天理参考館]]の南約500メートル、[[天理中学校]]すぐ北。 == 文化財 == === 国の史跡 === * 西山古墳（史跡「杣之内古墳群」のうち） *: 1927年（昭和2年）4月8日指定{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}。 *: 2018年（平成30年）2月13日、既指定の史跡「西山古墳」に西乗鞍古墳を追加指定、「杣之内古墳群」に名称変更平成30年2月13日文部科学省告示第19号。。 == 脚注 == {{reflist}} == 参考資料 == * 天理市教育委員会設置現地説明板 * 天理市ホームページ 古墳ガイド == 関連項目 == * [[杣之内古墳群]] == 外部リンク == {{Commonscat|Nishiyama Kofun}} * {{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}} *[http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html 天理市ホームページ|古墳ガイド] {{DEFAULTSORT:にしやまこふん}} [[Category:杣之内古墳群]] [[:File:Tenri-nishiyama_stereo.jpg|ステレオ写真はこちら]]]] 墳丘は前方部を西に向けた3段構築の[[前方後方墳]]で、全長183メートル、後円部の幅94メートル 高さ16メートル、前方部の幅72メートル。 下段が前方後方形で、中段から上は前方後円形となる特殊な墳形をもつ。下段の後方部は一辺90メートルの正方形で、これに同じ長さの前方部が付いている。中段は前方後円型をしていて、後円丘径72メートル、前方丘全長90メートル。墳頂部は径30メートルが平坦で、前方部方向に7メートル下がって細長い前方部が続き、前方部先端はくびれ部より2メートル高く主軸に直交する横長形となっている。後方部高さは南側で15メートルで、前方部の高さも南側で10メートル。 後方部頂上が盗掘されている。その時の記録から[[竪穴式石室]]であったと推定されている。 緩やかな傾斜地に立地し、三本の尾根の中央部を墳丘に、北と南の尾根を外堤として、自然地形を有効に利用しているため濠幅は一定しないが、全長200メートル以上の双方中方墳とも考えられる。濠は現在埋め立てられているが、階段状の方形の濠階段状の濠は「伝崇神天皇陵」古墳でもみられる。が巡らされていたと考えられる。現状では前方後方形の墳丘と見られるが、地形改変が進んでいることなどを考慮して、双方中方墳の可能性もある泉森皎「西山古墳」文化庁文化財保護部史跡研究会監修『図説　日本の史跡　第3巻　原始3』同朋舎出版　1991年　36ページ。 これは日本にある前方後方墳の中でもっとも規模の大きいものである。墳丘は1段目のみが前方後方墳の形で、その上に[[前方後円墳]]が乗るというきわめて特異な形をしており、当初からこの形であったことは間違いないとみられている『大和の古墳I』泉森皎編 人文書院（2003年）。 == 副葬品・出土品 == 後方部からは、銅鏡片、碧玉製鏃、管玉、鉄剣・鉄刀片が出土している。前方部南側濠内から碧玉製車輪石1が検出されている。傾斜斜面には葺き石が、埴輪片がみられ、円筒埴輪、鰭付（ひれつき）円筒埴輪、家形埴輪が見つかっている。 == 現状 == 墳丘の保存状態は良く、樹木が生えていないため段築をはっきりと観察することができる。 == アクセス == 天理駅より徒歩約20分。[[天理大学附属天理参考館]]の南約500メートル、[[天理中学校]]すぐ北。 == 文化財 == === 国の史跡 === * 西山古墳（史跡「杣之内古墳群」のうち） *: 1927年（昭和2年）4月8日指定。 *: 2018年（平成30年）2月13日、既指定の史跡「西山古墳」に西乗鞍古墳を追加指定、「杣之内古墳群」に名称変更平成30年2月13日文部科学省告示第19号。。 == 脚注 == {{reflist}} == 参考資料 == * 天理市教育委員会設置現地説明板 * 天理市ホームページ 古墳ガイド == 関連項目 == * [[杣之内古墳群]] == 外部リンク == {{Commonscat|Nishiyama Kofun}} * {{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}} *[http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html 天理市ホームページ|古墳ガイド] {{DEFAULTSORT:にしやまこふん}} [[Category:杣之内古墳群]] [[Category:奈良県の古墳]] [[Category:天理市の歴史]] [[Category:奈良県にある国指定の史跡]] [[Category:前方後方墳]]

{{国土航空写真}}
[[:File:Tenri-nishiyama_stereo.jpg|ステレオ写真はこちら]]]] 墳丘は前方部を西に向けた3段構築の[[前方後方墳]]で、全長183メートル、後円部の幅94メートル 高さ16メートル、前方部の幅72メートル。 下段が前方後方形で、中段から上は前方後円形となる特殊な墳形をもつ。下段の後方部は一辺90メートルの正方形で、これに同じ長さの前方部が付いている。中段は前方後円型をしていて、後円丘径72メートル、前方丘全長90メートル。墳頂部は径30メートルが平坦で、前方部方向に7メートル下がって細長い前方部が続き、前方部先端はくびれ部より2メートル高く主軸に直交する横長形となっている。後方部高さは南側で15メートルで、前方部の高さも南側で10メートル。 後方部頂上が盗掘されている。その時の記録から[[竪穴式石室]]であったと推定されている。 緩やかな傾斜地に立地し、三本の尾根の中央部を墳丘に、北と南の尾根を外堤として、自然地形を有効に利用しているため濠幅は一定しないが、全長200メートル以上の双方中方墳とも考えられる。濠は現在埋め立てられているが、階段状の方形の濠階段状の濠は「伝崇神天皇陵」古墳でもみられる。が巡らされていたと考えられる。現状では前方後方形の墳丘と見られるが、地形改変が進んでいることなどを考慮して、双方中方墳の可能性もある泉森皎「西山古墳」文化庁文化財保護部史跡研究会監修『図説　日本の史跡　第3巻　原始3』同朋舎出版　1991年　36ページ。 これは日本にある前方後方墳の中でもっとも規模の大きいものである。墳丘は1段目のみが前方後方墳の形で、その上に[[前方後円墳]]が乗るというきわめて特異な形をしており、当初からこの形であったことは間違いないとみられている『大和の古墳I』泉森皎編 人文書院（2003年）。 == 副葬品・出土品 == 後方部からは、銅鏡片、碧玉製鏃、管玉、鉄剣・鉄刀片が出土している。前方部南側濠内から碧玉製車輪石1が検出されている。傾斜斜面には葺き石が、埴輪片がみられ、円筒埴輪、鰭付（ひれつき）円筒埴輪、家形埴輪が見つかっている。 == 現状 == 墳丘の保存状態は良く、樹木が生えていないため段築をはっきりと観察することができる。 == アクセス == 天理駅より徒歩約20分。[[天理大学附属天理参考館]]の南約500メートル、[[天理中学校]]すぐ北。 == 文化財 == === 国の史跡 === * 西山古墳（史跡「杣之内古墳群」のうち） *: 1927年（昭和2年）4月8日指定。 *: 2018年（平成30年）2月13日、既指定の史跡「西山古墳」に西乗鞍古墳を追加指定、「杣之内古墳群」に名称変更平成30年2月13日文部科学省告示第19号。。 == 脚注 == {{reflist}} == 参考資料 == * 天理市教育委員会設置現地説明板 * 天理市ホームページ 古墳ガイド == 関連項目 == * [[杣之内古墳群]] == 外部リンク == {{Commonscat|Nishiyama Kofun}} * {{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}} *[http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html 天理市ホームページ|古墳ガイド] {{DEFAULTSORT:にしやまこふん}} [[Category:杣之内古墳群]] [[Category:奈良県の古墳]] [[Category:天理市の歴史]] [[Category:奈良県にある国指定の史跡]] [[Category:前方後方墳]]

[[ja:西山古墳]] {{Kofun of Japan |Name = Nishiyama Kofun |Image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px|]] |Caption = Mound overview (left: anterior, right back: posterior) |Location = {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}} {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}} Somanouchi Town |Coordinates = {{coord|34|35|33|N|135|50|36|E|region:JP-29_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Nishiyama Kofun}} |Type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳}} |Size = Total length: 183m, height: 13m |Burial = {{ill|Pit-style stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室}} |Era = Early Kofun period |Interred = (Theory) A member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏}} |Artifacts = Mirror fragments, stone arrowheads, iron sword fragments, magatama, and haniwa |Historic Designation = National Historic Site (designated April 8, 1927) |Map = Japan Nara |Icon = Zenpō-kōhō-fun-W }}
'''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in Somanouchi Town, {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}, Japan. It is designated as a National Historic Site and is part of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群}}.
== Overview == Constructed during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} (4th century), Nishiyama Kofun is the oldest of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群}}. The burial mound features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳}} at its base to a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} at its upper levels.
The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day {{ill|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市}}), was targeted.
== Dimensions and Structure == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * **Rear mound (posterior):** 94m width, 16m height * **Anterior mound:** 72m width, 13m height
The lower tier forms a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in.
Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design.
== Artifacts == Excavations have yielded: * **Posterior mound:** * Mirror fragments * Greenstone arrowheads * Magatama beads * Iron sword fragments * **Moat (south side):** * Greenstone wheel stones * **Surface artifacts:** * Stone paving (fukiishi) * Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)
== Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure.
== Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School.
== Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927<ref name="National Historic Site">{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}</ref>. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the designated area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."<ref>Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018.</ref>
== References == {{reflist}}
== See Also == * {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群}}

[[Category:Original page]] [[ja:西山古墳]] {{Kofun of Japan |Name = Nishiyama Kofun |image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px|]] |Caption = Mound overview (left: anterior, right back: posterior) |location = {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}} {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}} Somanouchi Town |coordinates = {{coord|34|35|33|N|135|50|36|E|region:JP-29_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Nishiyama Kofun}} |Type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳}} |Size = Total length: 183m, height: 13m |Burial = {{ill|Pit-style stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室}} |Era = Early Kofun period |Interred = (Theory) A member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏}} |Artifacts = Mirror fragments, stone arrowheads, iron sword fragments, magatama, and haniwa |Historic Designation = National Historic Site (designated April 8, 1927) |Map = Japan Nara |Icon = Zenpō-kōhō-fun-W }}
'''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in Somanouchi Town, {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}, Japan. It is designated as a National Historic Site and is part of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}.
== Overview == Constructed during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} (4th century), Nishiyama Kofun is the oldest of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}. The burial mound features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳}} at its base to a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} at its upper levels.
The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day {{ill|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市}}), was targeted.
== Dimensions and Structure == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * **Rear mound (posterior):** 94m width, 16m height * **Anterior mound:** 72m width, 13m height
The lower tier forms a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in.
Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design.
== Artifacts == Excavations have yielded: * **Posterior mound:** * Mirror fragments * Greenstone arrowheads * Magatama beads * Iron sword fragments * **Moat (south side):** * Greenstone wheel stones * **Surface artifacts:** * Stone paving (fukiishi) * Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)
== Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure.
== Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School.
== Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927<ref name="National Historic Site">{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}</ref>. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the designated area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."<ref>Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018.</ref>
== References == {{reflist}}
== See Also == * {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}
== External Links == * {{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}} * [http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html Tenri City Kofun Guide]

'''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in Somanouchi Town, {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}, Japan. It is designated as a National Historic Site and is part of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}.
== Overview == Constructed during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} (4th century), Nishiyama Kofun is the oldest of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}. The burial mound features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳}} at its base to a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} at its upper levels.
The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day {{ill|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市}}), was targeted.
== Dimensions and Structure == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * **Rear mound (posterior):** 94m width, 16m height * **Anterior mound:** 72m width, 13m height
The lower tier forms a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in.
Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design.
== Artifacts == Excavations have yielded: * **Posterior mound:** ** Mirror fragments ** Greenstone arrowheads ** Magatama beads ** Iron sword fragments * **Moat (south side):** ** Greenstone wheel stones * **Surface artifacts:** ** Stone paving (fukiishi) ** Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)
== Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure.
== Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School.
== Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927<ref name="National Historic Site">{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}</ref>. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the designated area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."<ref>Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018.</ref>
== References == {{reflist}}
== See Also == * {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}
== External Links == * {{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}} * [http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html Tenri City Kofun Guide]

'''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in Somanouchi Town, {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}, Japan. It is designated as a National Historic Site and is part of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}.
== Overview == Constructed during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} (4th century), Nishiyama Kofun is the oldest of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}. The burial mound features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳}} at its base to a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} at its upper levels.
The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day {{ill|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市}}), was targeted.
== Dimensions and Structure == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * **Rear mound (posterior):** 94m width, 16m height * **Anterior mound:** 72m width, 13m height
The lower tier forms a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in.
Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design.
== Artifacts == Excavations have yielded: * **Posterior mound:** ** Mirror fragments ** Greenstone arrowheads ** Magatama beads ** Iron sword fragments * **Moat (south side):** ** Greenstone wheel stones * **Surface artifacts:** ** Stone paving (fukiishi) ** Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)
== Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure.
== Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School.
== Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927<ref name="National Historic Site">{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}</ref>. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the designated area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."<ref>Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018.</ref>
== References == {{reflist}}
== See Also == * {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}
== External Links == * {{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}} * [http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html Tenri City Kofun Guide]

'''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in Somanouchi Town, {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}, Japan. It is designated as a National Historic Site and is part of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}.
== Overview == Constructed during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} (4th century), Nishiyama Kofun is the oldest of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}. The burial mound features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳}} at its base to a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} at its upper levels.
The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day {{ill|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市}}), was targeted.
== Dimensions and Structure == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * **Rear mound (posterior):** 94m width, 16m height * **Anterior mound:** 72m width, 13m height
The lower tier forms a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in.
Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design.
== Artifacts == Excavations have yielded: * **Posterior mound:** ** Mirror fragments ** Greenstone arrowheads ** Magatama beads ** Iron sword fragments * **Moat (south side):** ** Greenstone wheel stones * **Surface artifacts:** ** Stone paving (fukiishi) ** Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)
== Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure.
== Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School.
== Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927<ref name="National Historic Site">{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}</ref>. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the designated area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."<ref>Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018.</ref>
== References == {{reflist}}
== See Also == * {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}

'''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in Somanouchi Town, {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}, Japan. It is designated as a National Historic Site and is part of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}.
== Overview == Constructed during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} (4th century), Nishiyama Kofun is the oldest of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}. The burial mound features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳}} at its base to a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} at its upper levels.
The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day {{ill|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市}}), was targeted.
== Dimensions and Structure == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * '''Rear mound (posterior):''' 94m width, 16m height * '''Anterior mound:''' 72m width, 13m height
The lower tier forms a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in.
Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design.
== Artifacts == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments'''
* '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones'''
* '''Surface artifacts:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure.
== Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School.
== Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927<ref name="National Historic Site">{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}</ref>. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the designated area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."<ref>Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018.</ref>
== References == {{reflist}}
== See Also == * {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}
== External Links == * {{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}} * [http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html Tenri City Kofun Guide]

[[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Nishiyama Kofun-qq]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Nishiyama Kofun]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[ja:西山古墳]] {{Infobox ancient site |name = Nishiyama Kofun |image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px|]] |Caption = Mound overview (left: anterior, right back: posterior) |location = {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}} {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}} Somanouchi Town |coordinates = {{coord|34|35|33|N|135|50|36|E|region:JP-29_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Nishiyama Kofun}} |Type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳}} |Size = Total length: 183m, height: 13m |Burial = {{ill|Pit-style stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber}} |Era = Early Kofun period |Interred = (Theory) A member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏}} |Artifacts = Mirror fragments, stone arrowheads, iron sword fragments, magatama, and haniwa |Historic Designation = National Historic Site (designated April 8, 1927) |Map = Japan Nara |Icon = Zenpō-kōhō-fun-W }}
'''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in Somanouchi Town, {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}, Japan. It is designated as a National Historic Site and is part of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}.
== Overview == Constructed during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} (4th century), Nishiyama Kofun is the oldest of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}. The burial mound features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳}} at its base to a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} at its upper levels.
The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day {{ill|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市}}), was targeted.
== Dimensions and Structure == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * '''Rear mound (posterior):''' 94m width, 16m height * '''Anterior mound:''' 72m width, 13m height
The lower tier forms a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in.
Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design.
== Artifacts == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments'''
* '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones'''
* '''Surface artifacts:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure.
== Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School.
== Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927<ref name="National Historic Site">{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}</ref>. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the designated area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."<ref>Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018.</ref>
== References == {{reflist}}
== See Also == * {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}
== External Links == * {{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}} * [http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html Tenri City Kofun Guide]

'''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in Somanouchi Town, {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}, Japan. It is designated as a National Historic Site and is part of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}.
== Overview == Constructed during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} (4th century), Nishiyama Kofun is the oldest of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}. The burial mound features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳}} at its base to a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} at its upper levels.
The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day {{ill|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市}}), was targeted.
== Dimensions and Structure == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * '''Rear mound (posterior):''' 94m width, 16m height * '''Anterior mound:''' 72m width, 13m height
The lower tier forms a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in.
Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design.
== Artifacts == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments'''
* '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones'''
* '''Surface artifacts:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure.
== Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School.
== Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927<ref name="National Historic Site">{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}</ref>. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the designated area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."<ref>Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018.</ref>
== References == {{reflist}}

* '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones'''
* '''Surface artifacts:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure.

[[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Nishiyama Kofun-qq]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Nishiyama Kofun]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[ja:西山古墳]] {{Infobox ancient site |name = Nishiyama Kofun |image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px|]] |Caption = Mound overview (left: anterior, right back: posterior) |location = {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}} {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}} Somanouchi Town |coordinates = {{coord|34|35|33|N|135|50|36|E|region:JP-29_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Nishiyama Kofun}} |Type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳}} |Size = Total length: 183m, height: 13m |Burial = {{ill|Pit-style stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber}} |Era = Early Kofun period |Interred = (Theory) A member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏}} |Artifacts = Mirror fragments, stone arrowheads, iron sword fragments, magatama, and haniwa |Historic Designation = National Historic Site (designated April 8, 1927) |Map = Japan Nara |Icon = Zenpō-kōhō-fun-W }}
'''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in Somanouchi Town, {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}, Japan. It is designated as a National Historic Site and is part of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}.
== Overview == Constructed during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} (4th century), Nishiyama Kofun is the oldest of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}. The burial mound features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳}} at its base to a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} at its upper levels.
The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day {{ill|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市}}), was targeted.
== Dimensions and Structure == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * '''Rear mound (posterior):''' 94m width, 16m height * '''Anterior mound:''' 72m width, 13m height
The lower tier forms a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in.
Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design.
== Artifacts == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments'''
* '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones'''
* '''Surface artifacts:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure.
== Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School.
== Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927<ref name="National Historic Site">{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}</ref>. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the designated area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."<ref>Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018.</ref>
== References == {{reflist}}
== See Also == * {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}
== External Links == * {{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}} * [http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html Tenri City Kofun Guide]

[[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Nishiyama Kofun-qq]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Nishiyama Kofun]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[ja:西山古墳]] {{Infobox ancient site |name = Nishiyama Kofun |image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px|]] |Caption = Mound overview (left: anterior, right back: posterior) |location = {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}} {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}} Somanouchi Town |coordinates = {{coord|34|35|33|N|135|50|36|E|region:JP-29_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Nishiyama Kofun}} |Type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳}} |Size = Total length: 183m, height: 13m |Burial = {{ill|Pit-style stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber}} |Era = Early Kofun period |Interred = (Theory) A member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏}} |Artifacts = Mirror fragments, stone arrowheads, iron sword fragments, magatama, and haniwa |Historic Designation = National Historic Site (designated April 8, 1927) |Map = Japan Nara |Icon = Zenpō-kōhō-fun-W }}
'''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in Somanouchi Town, {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}, Japan. It is designated as a National Historic Site and is part of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}.
== Overview == Constructed during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} (4th century), Nishiyama Kofun is the oldest of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}. The burial mound features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳}} at its base to a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} at its upper levels.
The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day {{ill|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市}}), was targeted.
== Dimensions and Structure == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * '''Rear mound (posterior):''' 94m width, 16m height * '''Anterior mound:''' 72m width, 13m height
The lower tier forms a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in.
Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design.
== Artifacts == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments'''
* '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones'''
* '''Surface artifacts:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure.
== Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School.
== Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927<ref name="National Historic Site">{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}</ref>. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the designated area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."<ref>Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018.</ref>
== References == {{reflist}}
== See Also == * {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}
== External Links == * {{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}} * [http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html Tenri City Kofun Guide]

== Overview == Constructed during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} (4th century), Nishiyama Kofun is the oldest of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}. The burial mound features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} at its base to a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} at its upper levels.
The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day {{ill|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市}}), was targeted.
== Dimensions and Structure == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * '''Rear mound (posterior):''' 94m width, 16m height * '''Anterior mound:''' 72m width, 13m height
The lower tier forms a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in.
Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design.
== Artifacts == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments'''
* '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones'''
* '''Surface artifacts:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure.
== Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School.
== Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927<ref name="National Historic Site">{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}</ref>. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the designated area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."<ref>Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018.</ref>
== References == {{reflist}}
== See Also == * {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}
== External Links == * {{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}} * [http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html Tenri City Kofun Guide]

[[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Nishiyama Kofun-qq]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Nishiyama Kofun]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[ja:西山古墳]] {{Infobox ancient site |name = Nishiyama Kofun |image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px|]] |Caption = Mound overview (left: anterior, right back: posterior) |location = {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}} {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}} Somanouchi Town |coordinates = {{coord|34|35|33|N|135|50|36|E|region:JP-29_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Nishiyama Kofun}} |Type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} |Size = Total length: 183m, height: 13m |Burial = {{ill|Pit-style stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber}} |Era = Early Kofun period |Interred = (Theory) A member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏}} |Artifacts = Mirror fragments, stone arrowheads, iron sword fragments, magatama, and haniwa |Historic Designation = National Historic Site (designated April 8, 1927) |Map = Japan Nara |Icon = Zenpō-kōhō-fun-W }}
'''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in Somanouchi Town, {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}, Japan. It is designated as a National Historic Site and is part of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}.
== Overview == Constructed during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} (4th century), Nishiyama Kofun is the oldest of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}. The burial mound features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} at its base to a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} at its upper levels.
The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day {{ill|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市}}), was targeted.
== Dimensions and Structure == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * '''Rear mound (posterior):''' 94m width, 16m height * '''Anterior mound:''' 72m width, 13m height
The lower tier forms a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in.
Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design.
== Artifacts == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments'''
* '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones'''
* '''Surface artifacts:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure.
== Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School.
== Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927<ref name="National Historic Site">{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}</ref>. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the designated area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."<ref>Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018.</ref>
== References == {{reflist}}
== See Also == * {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}
== External Links == * {{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}} * [http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html Tenri City Kofun Guide]

[[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Nishiyama Kofun-qq]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Nishiyama Kofun]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[ja:西山古墳]] {{Infobox ancient site |name = Nishiyama Kofun |image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px|]] |Caption = Mound overview (left: anterior, right back: posterior) |location = {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}} {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}} Somanouchi Town |coordinates = {{coord|34|35|33|N|135|50|36|E|region:JP-29_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Nishiyama Kofun}} |Type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} |Size = Total length: 183m, height: 13m |Burial = {{ill|Pit-style stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber}} |Era = Early Kofun period |Interred = (Theory) A member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏}} |Artifacts = Mirror fragments, stone arrowheads, iron sword fragments, magatama, and haniwa |Historic Designation = National Historic Site (designated April 8, 1927) |Map = Japan Nara |Icon = Zenpō-kōhō-fun-W }}
'''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in Somanouchi Town, {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}, Japan. It is designated as a National Historic Site and is part of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}.
== Overview == Constructed during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} (4th century), Nishiyama Kofun is the oldest of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}. The burial mound features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} at its base to a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} at its upper levels.
The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day {{ill|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市}}), was targeted.
== Dimensions and Structure == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * '''Rear mound (posterior):''' 94m width, 16m height * '''Anterior mound:''' 72m width, 13m height
The lower tier forms a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in.
Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design.
== Artifacts == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments'''
* '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones'''
* '''Surface artifacts:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure.
== Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School.
== Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927<ref name="National Historic Site">{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}</ref>. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the designated area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."<ref>Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018.</ref>
== References == {{reflist}}
== See Also == * {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}
== External Links == * {{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}} * [http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html Tenri City Kofun Guide]

[[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Nishiyama Kofun-qq]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Nishiyama Kofun]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[ja:西山古墳]] {{Infobox ancient site |name = Nishiyama Kofun |image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px|]] |Caption = Mound overview (left: anterior, right back: posterior) |location = {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}} {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}} Somanouchi Town |coordinates = {{coord|34|35|33|N|135|50|36|E|region:JP-29_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Nishiyama Kofun}} |Type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} |Size = Total length: 183m, height: 13m |Burial = {{ill|Pit-style stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber}} |Era = Early Kofun period |Interred = (Theory) A member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏}} |Artifacts = Mirror fragments, stone arrowheads, iron sword fragments, magatama, and haniwa |Historic Designation = National Historic Site (designated April 8, 1927) |Map = Japan Nara |Icon = Zenpō-kōhō-fun-W }}
'''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in Somanouchi Town, {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}, Japan. It is designated as a National Historic Site and is part of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}.
== Overview == Constructed during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} (4th century), Nishiyama Kofun is the oldest of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}. The burial mound features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} at its base to a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} at its upper levels.
The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day {{ill|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市}}), was targeted.
== Dimensions and Structure == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * '''Rear mound (posterior):''' 94m width, 16m height * '''Anterior mound:''' 72m width, 13m height
The lower tier forms a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in.
Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design.
== Artifacts == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments'''
* '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones'''
* '''Surface artifacts:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure.
== Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School.
== Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927<ref name="National Historic Site">{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}</ref>. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the designated area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."<ref>Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018.</ref>

The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day {{ill|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市}}), was targeted.
== Dimensions and Structure == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * '''Rear mound (posterior):''' 94m width, 16m height * '''Anterior mound:''' 72m width, 13m height
The lower tier forms a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in.
Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design.
== Artifacts == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments'''
* '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones'''
* '''Surface artifacts:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure.
== Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School.
== Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927<ref name="National Historic Site">{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}</ref>. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the designated area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."<ref>Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018.</ref>

[[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Nishiyama Kofun-qq]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Nishiyama Kofun]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[ja:西山古墳]] {{Infobox ancient site |name = Nishiyama Kofun |image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px|]] |Caption = Mound overview (left: anterior, right back: posterior) |location = {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}} {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}} Somanouchi Town |coordinates = {{coord|34|35|33|N|135|50|36|E|region:JP-29_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Nishiyama Kofun}} |Type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} |Size = Total length: 183m, height: 13m |Burial = {{ill|Pit-style stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber}} |Era = Early Kofun period |Interred = (Theory) A member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏}} |Artifacts = Mirror fragments, stone arrowheads, iron sword fragments, magatama, and haniwa |Historic Designation = National Historic Site (designated April 8, 1927) |Map = Japan Nara |Icon = Zenpō-kōhō-fun-W }}
'''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in Somanouchi Town, {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}, Japan. It is designated as a National Historic Site and is part of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}.
== Overview == Constructed during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} (4th century), Nishiyama Kofun is the oldest of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}. The burial mound features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} at its base to a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} at its upper levels.
The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day {{ill|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市}}), was targeted.
== Dimensions and Structure == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * '''Rear mound (posterior):''' 94m width, 16m height * '''Anterior mound:''' 72m width, 13m height
The lower tier forms a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in.
Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design.
== Artifacts == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments'''
* '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones'''
* '''Surface artifacts:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure.
== Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School.
== Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927<ref name="National Historic Site">{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}</ref>. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the designated area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."<ref>Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018.</ref>
== References == {{reflist}}
== See Also == * {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}
== External Links == * {{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}} * [http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html Tenri City Kofun Guide]

[[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Nishiyama Kofun-qq]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Nishiyama Kofun]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[ja:西山古墳]] {{Infobox ancient site |name = Nishiyama Kofun |image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px|]] |Caption = Mound overview (left: anterior, right back: posterior) |location = {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}} {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}} Somanouchi Town |coordinates = {{coord|34|35|33|N|135|50|36|E|region:JP-29_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Nishiyama Kofun}} |Type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} |Size = Total length: 183m, height: 13m |Burial = {{ill|Pit-style stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber}} |Era = Early Kofun period |Interred = (Theory) A member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏}} |Artifacts = Mirror fragments, stone arrowheads, iron sword fragments, magatama, and haniwa |Historic Designation = National Historic Site (designated April 8, 1927) |Map = Japan Nara |Icon = Zenpō-kōhō-fun-W }}
'''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in Somanouchi Town, {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}, Japan. It is designated as a National Historic Site and is part of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}.
== Overview == Constructed during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} (4th century), Nishiyama Kofun is the oldest of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}. The burial mound features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} at its base to a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} at its upper levels.
The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day {{ill|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市}}), was targeted.
== Dimensions and Structure == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * '''Rear mound (posterior):''' 94m width, 16m height * '''Anterior mound:''' 72m width, 13m height
The lower tier forms a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in.
Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design.
== Artifacts == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments'''
* '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones'''
* '''Surface artifacts:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure.
== Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School.
== Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927<ref name="National Historic Site">{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}</ref>. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the designated area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."<ref>Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018.</ref>
== References == {{reflist}}
== See Also == * {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}

[[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Nishiyama Kofun-qq]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Nishiyama Kofun]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[ja:西山古墳]] {{Infobox ancient site |name = Nishiyama Kofun |image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px|]] |Caption = Mound overview (left: anterior, right back: posterior) |location = {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}} {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}} Somanouchi Town |coordinates = {{coord|34|35|33|N|135|50|36|E|region:JP-29_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Nishiyama Kofun}} |Type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} |Size = Total length: 183m, height: 13m |Burial = {{ill|Pit-style stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber}} |Era = Early Kofun period |Interred = (Theory) A member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏}} |Artifacts = Mirror fragments, stone arrowheads, iron sword fragments, magatama, and haniwa |Historic Designation = National Historic Site (designated April 8, 1927) |Map = Japan Nara |Icon = Zenpō-kōhō-fun-W }}
'''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in Somanouchi Town, {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}, Japan. It is designated as a National Historic Site and is part of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}.
== Overview == Constructed during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} (4th century), Nishiyama Kofun is the oldest of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}. The burial mound features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} at its base to a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} at its upper levels.
The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day {{ill|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市}}), was targeted.
== Dimensions and Structure == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * '''Rear mound (posterior):''' 94m width, 16m height * '''Anterior mound:''' 72m width, 13m height
The lower tier forms a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in.
Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design.
== Artifacts == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments'''
* '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones'''
* '''Surface artifacts:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure.
== Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School.
== Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927<ref name="National Historic Site">{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}</ref>. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the designated area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."<ref>Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018.</ref>
== References == {{reflist}}
== See Also == * {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}
== External Links == * {{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}} * [http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html Tenri City Kofun Guide]
