[[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Nishiyama Kofun-qq]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Nishiyama Kofun]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[ja:西山古墳]] {{Infobox ancient site |name = Nishiyama Kofun |image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px|]] |Caption = Mound overview (left: anterior, right back: posterior) |location = {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}} {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}} Somanouchi Town |coordinates = {{coord|34|35|33|N|135|50|36|E|region:JP-29_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Nishiyama Kofun}} |Type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} |Size = Total length: 183m, height: 13m |Burial = {{ill|Pit-style stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber}} |Era = Early Kofun period |Interred = (Theory) A member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏}} |Artifacts = Mirror fragments, stone arrowheads, iron sword fragments, magatama, and haniwa |Historic Designation = National Historic Site (designated April 8, 1927) |Map = Japan Nara |Icon = Zenpō-kōhō-fun-W }}
'''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in Somanouchi Town, {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}, Japan. It is designated as a National Historic Site and is part of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}.
== Overview == Constructed during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} (4th century), Nishiyama Kofun is the oldest of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}. The burial mound features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} at its base to a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} at its upper levels.
The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day {{ill|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市}}), was targeted.
== Dimensions and Structure == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * '''Rear mound (posterior):''' 94m width, 16m height * '''Anterior mound:''' 72m width, 13m height
The lower tier forms a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in.
Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design.
== Artifacts == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments'''
* '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones'''
* '''Surface artifacts:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure.
== Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School.
== Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927<ref name="National Historic Site">{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}</ref>. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the designated area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."<ref>Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018.</ref>
== References == {{reflist}}
== See Also == * {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}
== External Links == * {{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}} * [http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html Tenri City Kofun Guide]

[[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Nishiyama Kofun-qq]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Nishiyama Kofun]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[ja:西山古墳]] {{Infobox ancient site |name = Nishiyama Kofun |image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px|]] |Caption = Mound overview (left: anterior, right back: posterior) |location = {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}} {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}} Somanouchi Town |coordinates = {{coord|34|35|33|N|135|50|36|E|region:JP-29_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Nishiyama Kofun}} |Type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} |Size = Total length: 183m, height: 13m |Burial = {{ill|Pit-style stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber}} |Era = Early Kofun period |Interred = (Theory) A member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏}} |Artifacts = Mirror fragments, stone arrowheads, iron sword fragments, magatama, and haniwa |Historic Designation = National Historic Site (designated April 8, 1927) |Map = Japan Nara |Icon = Zenpō-kōhō-fun-W }}
'''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in Somanouchi Town, {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}, Japan. It is designated as a National Historic Site and is part of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}.
== Overview == Constructed during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} (4th century), Nishiyama Kofun is the oldest of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}. The burial mound features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} at its base to a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} at its upper levels.
The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day {{ill|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市}}), was targeted.
== Dimensions and Structure == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * '''Rear mound (posterior):''' 94m width, 16m height * '''Anterior mound:''' 72m width, 13m height
The lower tier forms a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in.
Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design.
== Artifacts == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments'''
* '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones'''
* '''Surface artifacts:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure.
== Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School.
== Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927<ref name="National Historic Site">{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}</ref>. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the designated area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."<ref>Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018.</ref>
== References == {{reflist}}
== See Also == * {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}
== External Links == * {{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}} * [http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html Tenri City Kofun Guide]

'''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in Somanouchi Town, {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}, Japan. It is designated as a National Historic Site and is part of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}.
== Overview == Constructed during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} (4th century), Nishiyama Kofun is the oldest of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}. The burial mound features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} at its base to a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} at its upper levels.
The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day {{ill|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市}}), was targeted.
== Dimensions and Structure == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * '''Rear mound (posterior):''' 94m width, 16m height * '''Anterior mound:''' 72m width, 13m height
The lower tier forms a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in.
Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design.
== Artifacts == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments'''
* '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones'''
* '''Surface artifacts:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure.
== Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School.
== Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927<ref name="National Historic Site">{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}</ref>. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the designated area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."<ref>Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018.</ref>
== References == {{reflist}}
== See Also == * {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}
== External Links == * {{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}} * [http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html Tenri City Kofun Guide]

[[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Nishiyama Kofun-qq]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Nishiyama Kofun]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[ja:西山古墳]] {{Infobox ancient site |name = Nishiyama Kofun |image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px|]] |Caption = Mound overview (left: anterior, right back: posterior) |location = {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}} {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}} Somanouchi Town |coordinates = {{coord|34|35|33|N|135|50|36|E|region:JP-29_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Nishiyama Kofun}} |type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} |Size = Total length: 183m, height: 13m |Burial = {{ill|Pit-style stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber}} |Era = Early Kofun period |Interred = (Theory) A member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏}} |Artifacts = Mirror fragments, stone arrowheads, iron sword fragments, magatama, and haniwa |Historic Designation = National Historic Site (designated April 8, 1927) |Map = Japan Nara |Icon = Zenpō-kōhō-fun-W }}
'''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in Somanouchi Town, {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}, Japan. It is designated as a National Historic Site and is part of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}.
== Overview == Constructed during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} (4th century), Nishiyama Kofun is the oldest of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}. The burial mound features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} at its base to a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} at its upper levels.
The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day {{ill|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市}}), was targeted.
== Dimensions and Structure == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * '''Rear mound (posterior):''' 94m width, 16m height * '''Anterior mound:''' 72m width, 13m height
The lower tier forms a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in.
Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design.
== Artifacts == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments'''
* '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones'''
* '''Surface artifacts:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure.
== Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School.
== Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927<ref name="National Historic Site">{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}</ref>. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the designated area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."<ref>Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018.</ref>
== References == {{reflist}}
== See Also == * {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}
== External Links == * {{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}} * [http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html Tenri City Kofun Guide]

[[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq-Nishiyama Kofun-qq]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Nishiyama Kofun]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[ja:西山古墳]] {{Infobox ancient site |name = Nishiyama Kofun |image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px|]] |Caption = Mound overview (left: anterior, right back: posterior) |location = {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}} {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}} Somanouchi Town |coordinates = {{coord|34|35|33|N|135|50|36|E|region:JP-29_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Nishiyama Kofun}} |type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} |Size = Total length: 183m, height: 13m |Burial = {{ill|Pit-style stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber}} |Era = Early Kofun period |Interred = (Theory) A member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏}} |Artifacts = Mirror fragments, stone arrowheads, iron sword fragments, magatama, and haniwa |Historic Designation = National Historic Site (designated April 8, 1927) |Map = Japan Nara |Icon = Zenpō-kōhō-fun-W }}
'''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in Somanouchi Town, {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}, Japan. It is designated as a National Historic Site and is part of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}.
== Overview == Constructed during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} (4th century), Nishiyama Kofun is the oldest of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}. The burial mound features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} at its base to a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} at its upper levels.
The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day {{ill|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市}}), was targeted.
== Dimensions and Structure == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * '''Rear mound (posterior):''' 94m width, 16m height * '''Anterior mound:''' 72m width, 13m height
The lower tier forms a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in.
Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design.
== Artifacts == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments'''
* '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones'''
* '''Surface artifacts:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure.
== Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School.
== Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927<ref name="National Historic Site">{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}</ref>. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the designated area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."<ref>Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018.</ref>
== References == {{reflist}}
== See Also == * {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}
== External Links == * {{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}} * [http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html Tenri City Kofun Guide]

'''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in Somanouchi Town, {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}, Japan. It is designated as a National Historic Site and is part of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}.
== Overview == Constructed during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} (4th century), Nishiyama Kofun is the oldest of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}. The burial mound features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} at its base to a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} at its upper levels.
The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day {{ill|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市}}), was targeted.
== Dimensions and Structure == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * '''Rear mound (posterior):''' 94m width, 16m height * '''Anterior mound:''' 72m width, 13m height
The lower tier forms a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in.
Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design.
== Artifacts == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments'''
* '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones'''
* '''Surface artifacts:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure.
== Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School.
== Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927<ref name="National Historic Site">{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}</ref>. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the designated area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."<ref>Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018.</ref>
== References == {{reflist}}
== See Also == * {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}
== External Links == * {{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}} * [http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html Tenri City Kofun Guide]

* '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones'''
* '''Surface artifacts:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure.

[[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq deprecated start]]<!--Nishiyama Kofun-->[[Category:qq deprecated close]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Nishiyama Kofun]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[ja:西山古墳]] {{Infobox ancient site |name = Nishiyama Kofun |image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px|]] |Caption = Mound overview (left: anterior, right back: posterior) |location = {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}} {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}} Somanouchi Town |coordinates = {{coord|34|35|33|N|135|50|36|E|region:JP-29_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Nishiyama Kofun}} |type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} |Size = Total length: 183m, height: 13m |Burial = {{ill|Pit-style stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber}} |Era = Early Kofun period |Interred = (Theory) A member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏}} |Artifacts = Mirror fragments, stone arrowheads, iron sword fragments, magatama, and haniwa |Historic Designation = National Historic Site (designated April 8, 1927) |Map = Japan Nara |Icon = Zenpō-kōhō-fun-W }}
'''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in Somanouchi Town, {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}, Japan. It is designated as a National Historic Site and is part of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}.
== Overview == Constructed during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} (4th century), Nishiyama Kofun is the oldest of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}. The burial mound features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} at its base to a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} at its upper levels.
The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day {{ill|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市}}), was targeted.
== Dimensions and Structure == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * '''Rear mound (posterior):''' 94m width, 16m height * '''Anterior mound:''' 72m width, 13m height
The lower tier forms a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in.
Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design.
== Artifacts == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments'''
* '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones'''
* '''Surface artifacts:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure.
== Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School.
== Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927<ref name="National Historic Site">{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}</ref>. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the designated area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."<ref>Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018.</ref>
== References == {{reflist}}
== See Also == * {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}
== External Links == * {{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}} * [http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html Tenri City Kofun Guide]

'''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in Somanouchi Town, {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}, Japan. It is designated as a National Historic Site and is part of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}.
== Overview == Constructed during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} (4th century), Nishiyama Kofun is the oldest of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}. The burial mound features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} at its base to a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} at its upper levels.
The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day {{ill|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市}}), was targeted.
== Dimensions and Structure == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * '''Rear mound (posterior):''' 94m width, 16m height * '''Anterior mound:''' 72m width, 13m height
The lower tier forms a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in.
Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design.
== Artifacts == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments'''
* '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones'''
* '''Surface artifacts:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure.
== Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School.
== Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927<ref name="National Historic Site">{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}</ref>. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the designated area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."<ref>Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018.</ref>

[[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Nishiyama Kofun]][[Category:qq]] <!--Nishiyama Kofun-->[[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Nishiyama Kofun]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[ja:西山古墳]] {{Infobox ancient site |name = Nishiyama Kofun |image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px|]] |Caption = Mound overview (left: anterior, right back: posterior) |location = {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}} {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}} Somanouchi Town |coordinates = {{coord|34|35|33|N|135|50|36|E|region:JP-29_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Nishiyama Kofun}} |type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} |Size = Total length: 183m, height: 13m |Burial = {{ill|Pit-style stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber}} |Era = Early Kofun period |Interred = (Theory) A member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏}} |Artifacts = Mirror fragments, stone arrowheads, iron sword fragments, magatama, and haniwa |Historic Designation = National Historic Site (designated April 8, 1927) |Map = Japan Nara |Icon = Zenpō-kōhō-fun-W }}
'''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in Somanouchi Town, {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}, Japan. It is designated as a National Historic Site and is part of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}.
== Overview == Constructed during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} (4th century), Nishiyama Kofun is the oldest of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}. The burial mound features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} at its base to a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} at its upper levels.
The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day {{ill|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市}}), was targeted.
== Dimensions and Structure == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * '''Rear mound (posterior):''' 94m width, 16m height * '''Anterior mound:''' 72m width, 13m height
The lower tier forms a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in.
Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design.
== Artifacts == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments'''
* '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones'''
* '''Surface artifacts:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure.
== Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School.
== Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927<ref name="National Historic Site">{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}</ref>. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the designated area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."<ref>Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018.</ref>

== Dimensions and Structure == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * '''Rear mound (posterior):''' 94m width, 16m height * '''Anterior mound:''' 72m width, 13m height
The lower tier forms a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in.
Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design.
== Artifacts == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments'''
* '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones'''
* '''Surface artifacts:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure.
== Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School.
== Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927<ref name="National Historic Site">{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}</ref>. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the designated area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."<ref>Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018.</ref>

'''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in Somanouchi Town, {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}, Japan. It is designated as a National Historic Site and is part of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}.
== Overview == Constructed during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} (4th century), Nishiyama Kofun is the oldest of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}. The burial mound features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} at its base to a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} at its upper levels.
The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day {{ill|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市}}), was targeted.
== Dimensions and Structure == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * '''Rear mound (posterior):''' 94m width, 16m height * '''Anterior mound:''' 72m width, 13m height
The lower tier forms a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in.
Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design.
== Artifacts == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments'''
* '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones'''
* '''Surface artifacts:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure.
== Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School.
== Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927<ref name="National Historic Site">{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}</ref>. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the designated area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."<ref>Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018.</ref>

[[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Ugoodbye $1 completion categories]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Nishiyama Kofun]][[Category:qq]] <!--Nishiyama Kofun-->[[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Nishiyama Kofun]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[ja:西山古墳]] {{Infobox ancient site |name = Nishiyama Kofun |image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px|]] |Caption = Mound overview (left: anterior, right back: posterior) |location = {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}} {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}} Somanouchi Town |coordinates = {{coord|34|35|33|N|135|50|36|E|region:JP-29_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Nishiyama Kofun}} |type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} |Size = Total length: 183m, height: 13m |Burial = {{ill|Pit-style stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber}} |Era = Early Kofun period |Interred = (Theory) A member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏}} |Artifacts = Mirror fragments, stone arrowheads, iron sword fragments, magatama, and haniwa |Historic Designation = National Historic Site (designated April 8, 1927) |Map = Japan Nara |Icon = Zenpō-kōhō-fun-W }}
'''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in Somanouchi Town, {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}, Japan. It is designated as a National Historic Site and is part of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}.
== Overview == Constructed during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} (4th century), Nishiyama Kofun is the oldest of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}. The burial mound features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} at its base to a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} at its upper levels.
The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day {{ill|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市}}), was targeted.
== Dimensions and Structure == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * '''Rear mound (posterior):''' 94m width, 16m height * '''Anterior mound:''' 72m width, 13m height
The lower tier forms a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in.
Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design.
== Artifacts == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments'''
* '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones'''
* '''Surface artifacts:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure.
== Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School.
== Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927<ref name="National Historic Site">{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}</ref>. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the designated area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."<ref>Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018.</ref>
== References == {{reflist}}
== See Also == * {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}
== External Links == * {{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}} * [http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html Tenri City Kofun Guide]

[[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:qq]][[sn:Nishiyama Kofun]][[Category:qq]]{{DEFAULTSORT:Nishiyama Kofun}}[[Category:qq]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Nishiyama Kofun]][[Category:qq]] <!--Nishiyama Kofun-->[[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Nishiyama Kofun]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[ja:西山古墳]] {{Infobox ancient site |name = Nishiyama Kofun |image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px|]] |Caption = Mound overview (left: anterior, right back: posterior) |location = {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}} {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}} Somanouchi Town |coordinates = {{coord|34|35|33|N|135|50|36|E|region:JP-29_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Nishiyama Kofun}} |type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} |Size = Total length: 183m, height: 13m |Burial = {{ill|Pit-style stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber}} |Era = Early Kofun period |Interred = (Theory) A member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏}} |Artifacts = Mirror fragments, stone arrowheads, iron sword fragments, magatama, and haniwa |Historic Designation = National Historic Site (designated April 8, 1927) |Map = Japan Nara |Icon = Zenpō-kōhō-fun-W }}
'''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in Somanouchi Town, {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}, Japan. It is designated as a National Historic Site and is part of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}.
== Overview == Constructed during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} (4th century), Nishiyama Kofun is the oldest of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}. The burial mound features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} at its base to a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} at its upper levels.
The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day {{ill|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市}}), was targeted.
== Dimensions and Structure == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * '''Rear mound (posterior):''' 94m width, 16m height * '''Anterior mound:''' 72m width, 13m height
The lower tier forms a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in.
Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design.
== Artifacts == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments'''
* '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones'''
* '''Surface artifacts:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure.
== Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School.
== Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927<ref name="National Historic Site">{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}</ref>. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the designated area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."<ref>Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018.</ref>

The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day {{ill|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市}}), was targeted.
== Dimensions and Structure == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * '''Rear mound (posterior):''' 94m width, 16m height * '''Anterior mound:''' 72m width, 13m height
The lower tier forms a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in.
Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design.
== Artifacts == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments'''
* '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones'''
* '''Surface artifacts:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure.
== Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School.
== Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927<ref name="National Historic Site">{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}</ref>. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the designated area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."<ref>Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018.</ref>

'''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in Somanouchi Town, {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}, Japan. It is designated as a National Historic Site and is part of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}.
== Overview == Constructed during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} (4th century), Nishiyama Kofun is the oldest of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群}}. The burial mound features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} at its base to a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} at its upper levels.
The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day {{ill|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市}}), was targeted.
== Dimensions and Structure == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * '''Rear mound (posterior):''' 94m width, 16m height * '''Anterior mound:''' 72m width, 13m height
The lower tier forms a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in.
Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design.
== Artifacts == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments'''
* '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones'''
* '''Surface artifacts:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure.
== Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School.
== Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927<ref name="National Historic Site">{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}</ref>. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the designated area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."<ref>Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018.</ref>

[[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:qq]][[sn:Nishiyama Kofun]][[Category:qq]]{{DEFAULTSORT:Nishiyama Kofun}}[[Category:qq]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Nishiyama Kofun]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Nishiyama Kofun]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[ja:西山古墳]] {{Infobox ancient site |name = Nishiyama Kofun |image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px|]] |Caption = Mound overview (left: anterior, right back: posterior) |location = {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}} {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}} Somanouchi Town |coordinates = {{coord|34|35|33|N|135|50|36|E|region:JP-29_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Nishiyama Kofun}} |type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} |Size = Total length: 183m, height: 13m |Burial = {{ill|Pit-style stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber}} |Era = Early Kofun period |Interred = (Theory) A member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏}} |Artifacts = Mirror fragments, stone arrowheads, iron sword fragments, magatama, and haniwa |Historic Designation = National Historic Site (designated April 8, 1927) |Map = Japan Nara |Icon = Zenpō-kōhō-fun-W }} '''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in Somanouchi Town, {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}, Japan. It is designated as a National Historic Site and is part of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster}}. == Overview == Constructed during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} (4th century), Nishiyama Kofun is the oldest of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster}}. The burial mound features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} at its base to a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} at its upper levels. The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day {{ill|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市}}), was targeted. == Dimensions and Structure == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * '''Rear mound (posterior):''' 94m width, 16m height * '''Anterior mound:''' 72m width, 13m height The lower tier forms a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in. Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design. == Artifacts == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments''' * '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones''' * '''Surface artifacts:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure. == Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School. == Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the designated area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster}} == External Links == * {{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}} * [http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html Tenri Ota, Gunma|Nishiyama Kofun (Ota)}} {{Infobox Kofun | name = Nishiyama Kofun | native_name = 西山古墳 | image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px]]
Mound overview (left: front section, back right: rear section) | location = {{ill|Tenri, Nara|ja|天理市}}, Nara Prefecture, Japan | latitude = 34.5925 | longitude = 135.8433 | region = Japan | type = {{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} (rectangular keyhole-shaped tumulus) | length = 183m, Height: 13m | burial = {{ill|Tateana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber}} (pit-style stone chamber) | built = Early Kofun period (4th century) | person = Possibly a member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏}} | artifacts = Mirrors, stone arrowheads, iron swords and blades, magatama beads, haniwa clay figures | designated = National Historic Site of Japan (designated April 8, 1927) }} '''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a '''large [[Zenpō-kōhō-fun|rectangular keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後方墳, zenpō-kōhō-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Tenri, Nara|ja|天理市}}, Nara Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''{{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster}}''' and is the '''largest kofun of its type in Japan'''. In '''1927 (Showa 2)''', it was '''designated as a National Historic Site''' of Japan.{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/1958|title=Nishiyama Kofun - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}} It is also known by the '''alternate name "Nagariyama" (勾山, Magariyama).''' == Overview == The kofun was '''constructed during the early [[Kofun period]] (4th century)''' and is one of the '''earliest tumuli''' in the '''{{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster}}'''. The mound originally had a '''[[Vertical pit stone chamber|pit-style stone chamber]] (竪穴式石室, tateana-shiki sekishitsu)''', but it was likely '''looted in antiquity'''.Izumimori, Ko. *Ancient Tombs of Yamato I* (『大和の古墳I』), Jinbun Shoin, 2003. During '''World War II''', the Japanese Imperial Army '''stationed an anti-aircraft gun battery''' at the site. At that time, stones from the '''burial chamber (originally quarried in Kashiwara, Osaka)''' were reportedly '''removed''' and repurposed.On-site information board by the Tenri City Board of Education. == Structure & Dimensions == [[File:080515 Nishiyama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|Aerial view of Nishiyama Kofun.
{{National Aerial Photography}}.
[[:File:Tenri-nishiyama_stereo.jpg|Stereo image here]]]] The tumulus is a '''three-tiered, [[Zenpō-kōhō-fun|rectangular keyhole-shaped mound]] (前方後方墳, [[zenpō-kōhō-fun]])''' with the front section '''oriented westward'''. Its dimensions are: - '''Total length''': 183 meters - '''Rear section''' (square): 94m wide × 16m high - '''Front section''': 72m wide The '''lower level''' is '''rectangular''', while the '''middle and upper levels''' are '''rounder''', creating a hybrid '''keyhole-shaped mound (前方後円形, zenpō-kōenkei)'''. The '''central burial chamber''' is estimated to be a '''[[Vertical pit stone chamber|pit-style stone chamber]]''' based on '''historical records'''. The mound is positioned '''along three natural ridges''', with the '''central ridge forming the main mound''', while the '''north and south ridges serve as outer embankments'''. A '''moat once surrounded the mound''', but it has since been '''filled in'''. This kofun is '''the largest of its kind in Japan'''. The '''unique construction''', with a '''rectangular lower tier supporting a rounder upper structure''', is believed to be '''original to its design'''. == Artifacts & Burial Goods == Excavations have uncovered: - '''Copper mirrors (fragments)''' - '''Green jasper arrowheads''' - '''Magatama beads''' - '''Iron swords and blades''' - '''Wheel-shaped stone object (碧玉製車輪石, hekigyoku-sei sharinseki)''' - '''Haniwa clay figures''', including: - '''[[Cylindrical Haniwa|Cylindrical haniwa]] (円筒埴輪)''' - '''Fin-shaped haniwa (鰭付円筒埴輪)''' - '''[[Figural Haniwa|House-shaped haniwa]] (家形埴輪)''' == Current Condition == The '''mound is well preserved''', and due to '''lack of tree cover''', the '''three-tiered structure is clearly visible'''. == Access == - '''20-minute walk from [[Tenri Station]]''' - Located '''500 meters south''' of the '''Tenri University Reference Museum''' - '''Just north''' of '''Tenri Middle School''' == Cultural Heritage Status == === '''National Historic Site of Japan''' === - '''Original designation (1927)''': Nishiyama Kofun was designated a '''National Historic Site'''. - '''Expansion (2018)''': The designation was '''expanded''' to include '''Nishinorikura Kofun (西乗鞍古墳)''', renaming the site as the '''Somanochi Kofun Group (杣之内古墳群)'''.Ministry of Education, Science and Culture Announcement No. 19 (February 13, 2018). == References == {{Reflist}} == Additional Resources == - '''On-site information board''' (Tenri City Board of Education) - '''Tenri City Website: Kofun Guide''' == Related Articles == * {{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:qq]][[sn:Nishiyama Kofun]][[Category:qq]]{{DEFAULTSORT:Nishiyama Kofun}}[[Category:qq]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Nishiyama Kofun]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Nishiyama Kofun]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[ja:西山古墳]] {{Infobox ancient site |name = Nishiyama Kofun |image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px|]] |Caption = Mound overview (left: anterior, right back: posterior) |location = {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}} {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}} Somanouchi Town |coordinates = {{coord|34|35|33|N|135|50|36|E|region:JP-29_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Nishiyama Kofun}} |type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} |Size = Total length: 183m, height: 13m |Burial = {{ill|Pit-style stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber}} |Era = Early Kofun period |Interred = (Theory) A member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏}} |Artifacts = Mirror fragments, stone arrowheads, iron sword fragments, magatama, and haniwa |Historic Designation = National Historic Site (designated April 8, 1927) |Map = Japan Nara |Icon = Zenpō-kōhō-fun-W }} '''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in Somanouchi Town, {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}, Japan. It is designated as a National Historic Site and is part of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster}}. == Overview == Constructed during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} (4th century), Nishiyama Kofun is the oldest of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster}}. The burial mound features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} at its base to a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} at its upper levels. The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day {{ill|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市}}), was targeted. == Dimensions and Structure == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * '''Rear mound (posterior):''' 94m width, 16m height * '''Anterior mound:''' 72m width, 13m height The lower tier forms a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in. Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design. == Artifacts == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments''' * '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones''' * '''Surface artifacts:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure. == Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School. == Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the designated area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == Ota, Gunma|Nishiyama Kofun (Ota)}} {{Infobox Kofun | name = Nishiyama Kofun | native_name = 西山古墳 | image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px]]
Mound overview (left: front section, back right: rear section) | location = {{ill|Tenri, Nara|ja|天理市}}, Nara Prefecture, Japan | latitude = 34.5925 | longitude = 135.8433 | region = Japan | type = {{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} (rectangular keyhole-shaped tumulus) | length = 183m, Height: 13m | burial = {{ill|Tateana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber}} (pit-style stone chamber) | built = Early Kofun period (4th century) | person = Possibly a member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏}} | artifacts = Mirrors, stone arrowheads, iron swords and blades, magatama beads, haniwa clay figures | designated = National Historic Site of Japan (designated April 8, 1927) }} '''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a '''large [[Zenpō-kōhō-fun|rectangular keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後方墳, zenpō-kōhō-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Tenri, Nara|ja|天理市}}, Nara Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''{{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster}}''' and is the '''largest kofun of its type in Japan'''. In '''1927 (Showa 2)''', it was '''designated as a National Historic Site''' of Japan.{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/1958|title=Nishiyama Kofun - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}} It is also known by the '''alternate name "Nagariyama" (勾山, Magariyama).''' == Overview == The kofun was '''constructed during the early [[Kofun period]] (4th century)''' and is one of the '''earliest tumuli''' in the '''{{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster}}'''. The mound originally had a '''[[Vertical pit stone chamber|pit-style stone chamber]] (竪穴式石室, tateana-shiki sekishitsu)''', but it was likely '''looted in antiquity'''.Izumimori, Ko. *Ancient Tombs of Yamato I* (『大和の古墳I』), Jinbun Shoin, 2003. During '''World War II''', the Japanese Imperial Army '''stationed an anti-aircraft gun battery''' at the site. At that time, stones from the '''burial chamber (originally quarried in Kashiwara, Osaka)''' were reportedly '''removed''' and repurposed.On-site information board by the Tenri City Board of Education. == Structure & Dimensions == [[File:080515 Nishiyama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|Aerial view of Nishiyama Kofun.
{{National Aerial Photography}}.
[[:File:Tenri-nishiyama_stereo.jpg|Stereo image here]]]] The tumulus is a '''three-tiered, [[Zenpō-kōhō-fun|rectangular keyhole-shaped mound]] (前方後方墳, [[zenpō-kōhō-fun]])''' with the front section '''oriented westward'''. Its dimensions are: - '''Total length''': 183 meters - '''Rear section''' (square): 94m wide × 16m high - '''Front section''': 72m wide The '''lower level''' is '''rectangular''', while the '''middle and upper levels''' are '''rounder''', creating a hybrid '''keyhole-shaped mound (前方後円形, zenpō-kōenkei)'''. The '''central burial chamber''' is estimated to be a '''[[Vertical pit stone chamber|pit-style stone chamber]]''' based on '''historical records'''. The mound is positioned '''along three natural ridges''', with the '''central ridge forming the main mound''', while the '''north and south ridges serve as outer embankments'''. A '''moat once surrounded the mound''', but it has since been '''filled in'''. This kofun is '''the largest of its kind in Japan'''. The '''unique construction''', with a '''rectangular lower tier supporting a rounder upper structure''', is believed to be '''original to its design'''. == Artifacts & Burial Goods == Excavations have uncovered: - '''Copper mirrors (fragments)''' - '''Green jasper arrowheads''' - '''Magatama beads''' - '''Iron swords and blades''' - '''Wheel-shaped stone object (碧玉製車輪石, hekigyoku-sei sharinseki)''' - '''Haniwa clay figures''', including: - '''[[Cylindrical Haniwa|Cylindrical haniwa]] (円筒埴輪)''' - '''Fin-shaped haniwa (鰭付円筒埴輪)''' - '''[[Figural Haniwa|House-shaped haniwa]] (家形埴輪)''' == Current Condition == The '''mound is well preserved''', and due to '''lack of tree cover''', the '''three-tiered structure is clearly visible'''. == Access == - '''20-minute walk from [[Tenri Station]]''' - Located '''500 meters south''' of the '''Tenri University Reference Museum''' - '''Just north''' of '''Tenri Middle School''' == Cultural Heritage Status == === '''National Historic Site of Japan''' === - '''Original designation (1927)''': Nishiyama Kofun was designated a '''National Historic Site'''. - '''Expansion (2018)''': The designation was '''expanded''' to include '''Nishinorikura Kofun (西乗鞍古墳)''', renaming the site as the '''Somanochi Kofun Group (杣之内古墳群)'''.Ministry of Education, Science and Culture Announcement No. 19 (February 13, 2018). == References == {{Reflist}} == Additional Resources == - '''On-site information board''' (Tenri City Board of Education) - '''Tenri City Website: Kofun Guide''' == Related Articles == * {{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun Ota, Gunma|Nishiyama Kofun (Ota)}} {{Infobox Kofun | name = Nishiyama Kofun | native_name = 西山古墳 | image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px]]
Mound overview (left: front section, back right: rear section) | location = {{ill|Tenri, Nara|ja|天理市}}, Nara Prefecture, Japan | latitude = 34.5925 | longitude = 135.8433 | region = Japan | type = {{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} (rectangular keyhole-shaped tumulus) | length = 183m, Height: 13m | burial = {{ill|Tateana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber}} (pit-style stone chamber) | built = Early Kofun period (4th century) | person = Possibly a member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏}} | artifacts = Mirrors, stone arrowheads, iron swords and blades, magatama beads, haniwa clay figures | designated = National Historic Site of Japan (designated April 8, 1927) }} '''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a '''large [[Zenpō-kōhō-fun|rectangular keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後方墳, zenpō-kōhō-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Tenri, Nara|ja|天理市}}, Nara Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''{{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster}}''' and is the '''largest kofun of its type in Japan'''. In '''1927 (Showa 2)''', it was '''designated as a National Historic Site''' of Japan.{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/1958|title=Nishiyama Kofun - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}} It is also known by the '''alternate name "Nagariyama" (勾山, Magariyama).''' == Overview == The kofun was '''constructed during the early [[Kofun period]] (4th century)''' and is one of the '''earliest tumuli''' in the '''{{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster}}'''. The mound originally had a '''[[Vertical pit stone chamber|pit-style stone chamber]] (竪穴式石室, tateana-shiki sekishitsu)''', but it was likely '''looted in antiquity'''.Izumimori, Ko. *Ancient Tombs of Yamato I* (『大和の古墳I』), Jinbun Shoin, 2003. During '''World War II''', the Japanese Imperial Army '''stationed an anti-aircraft gun battery''' at the site. At that time, stones from the '''burial chamber (originally quarried in Kashiwara, Osaka)''' were reportedly '''removed''' and repurposed.On-site information board by the Tenri City Board of Education. == Structure & Dimensions == [[File:080515 Nishiyama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|Aerial view of Nishiyama Kofun.
{{National Aerial Photography}}.
[[:File:Tenri-nishiyama_stereo.jpg|Stereo image here]]]] The tumulus is a '''three-tiered, [[Zenpō-kōhō-fun|rectangular keyhole-shaped mound]] (前方後方墳, [[zenpō-kōhō-fun]])''' with the front section '''oriented westward'''. Its dimensions are: - '''Total length''': 183 meters - '''Rear section''' (square): 94m wide × 16m high - '''Front section''': 72m wide The '''lower level''' is '''rectangular''', while the '''middle and upper levels''' are '''rounder''', creating a hybrid '''keyhole-shaped mound (前方後円形, zenpō-kōenkei)'''. The '''central burial chamber''' is estimated to be a '''[[Vertical pit stone chamber|pit-style stone chamber]]''' based on '''historical records'''. The mound is positioned '''along three natural ridges''', with the '''central ridge forming the main mound''', while the '''north and south ridges serve as outer embankments'''. A '''moat once surrounded the mound''', but it has since been '''filled in'''. This kofun is '''the largest of its kind in Japan'''. The '''unique construction''', with a '''rectangular lower tier supporting a rounder upper structure''', is believed to be '''original to its design'''. == Artifacts & Burial Goods == Excavations have uncovered: - '''Copper mirrors (fragments)''' - '''Green jasper arrowheads''' - '''Magatama beads''' - '''Iron swords and blades''' - '''Wheel-shaped stone object (碧玉製車輪石, hekigyoku-sei sharinseki)''' - '''Haniwa clay figures''', including: - '''[[Cylindrical Haniwa|Cylindrical haniwa]] (円筒埴輪)''' - '''Fin-shaped haniwa (鰭付円筒埴輪)''' - '''[[Figural Haniwa|House-shaped haniwa]] (家形埴輪)''' == Current Condition == The '''mound is well preserved''', and due to '''lack of tree cover''', the '''three-tiered structure is clearly visible'''. == Access == - '''20-minute walk from [[Tenri Station]]''' - Located '''500 meters south''' of the '''Tenri University Reference Museum''' - '''Just north''' of '''Tenri Middle School''' == Cultural Heritage Status == === '''National Historic Site of Japan''' === - '''Original designation (1927)''': Nishiyama Kofun was designated a '''National Historic Site'''. - '''Expansion (2018)''': The designation was '''expanded''' to include '''Nishinorikura Kofun (西乗鞍古墳)''', renaming the site as the '''Somanochi Kofun Group (杣之内古墳群)'''.Ministry of Education, Science and Culture Announcement No. 19 (February 13, 2018). == References == {{Reflist}} == Additional Resources == - '''On-site information board''' (Tenri City Board of Education) - '''Tenri City Website: Kofun Guide''' == Related Articles == * {{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun
