This was added through [[Special:MassEditRegex]] to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} [[Category:11]][[sn:Nishiyama Kofun]][[Category:11]]{{DEFAULTSORT:Nishiyama Kofun}}[[Category:11]] [[Category:11]][[sn:Nishiyama Kofun]][[Category:11]] [[Category:Nishiyama Kofun]][[ja:西山古墳]] {{Infobox ancient site|type = {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun}} |name = Nishiyama Kofun |image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px|]] |caption = Mound overview (left: anterior, right back: posterior) |location = {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}} {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}} Somanouchi Town |coordinates = {{coord|34|35|33|N|135|50|36|E|region:JP-29_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Nishiyama Kofun}} |type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} |area = Total length: 183m, height: 13m |burial = {{ill|Pit-style stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber}} |built = Early Kofun period |Interred = (Theory) A member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏}} |burial goods = Mirror fragments, stone arrowheads, iron sword fragments, magatama, and haniwa |alternate_name = National other_designation (other_designation1 April 8, 1927) |map = Japan Nara |type = Zenpō-kōhō-fun-W }} '''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in Somanouchi Town, {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}, Japan. It is other_designation1 as a National other_designation and is part of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster}}. == Overview == Constructed during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} (4th century), Nishiyama Kofun is the oldest of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster}}. The Kofun features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} at its base to a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} at its upper levels. The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day {{ill|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市}}), was targeted. == area and burial == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * '''Rear mound (posterior):''' 94m width, 16m height * '''Anterior mound:''' 72m width, 13m height The lower tier types a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in. Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design. == burial goods == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments''' * '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones''' * '''Surface burial goods:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure. == Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School. == Cultural Significance == === National other_designation === * Designated on April 8, 1927{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the other_designation1 area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018. == References == {{reflist}} == Mound overview (left: front section, back right: rear section) | location = {{ill|Tenri, Nara|ja|天理市}}, Nara Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = 34.5925 | coordinates = 135.8433 | region = Japan | type = {{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} (rectangular keyhole-shaped tumulus) | length = 183m, Height: 13m | burial = {{ill|Tateana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber}} (pit-style stone chamber) | built = Early Kofun period (4th century) | person = Possibly a member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏}} | burial goods = Mirrors, stone arrowheads, iron swords and blades, magatama beads, haniwa clay figures | other_designation1 = National Historic Site of Japan (other_designation1 April 8, 1927) }} '''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a '''large [[Zenpō-kōhō-fun|rectangular keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後方墳, zenpō-kōhō-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Tenri, Nara|ja|天理市}}, Nara Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''{{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster}}''' and is the '''largest kofun of its type in Japan'''. In '''1927 (Showa 2)''', it was '''other_designation1 as a National other_designation''' of Japan.{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/1958|title=Nishiyama Kofun - National other_designation|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}} It is also known by the '''alternate name "Nagariyama" (勾山, Magariyama).''' == Overview == The kofun was '''constructed during the early [[Kofun period]] (4th century)''' and is one of the '''earliest tumuli''' in the '''{{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster}}'''. The mound originally had a '''[[Vertical pit stone chamber|pit-style stone chamber]] (竪穴式石室, tateana-shiki sekishitsu)''', but it was likely '''looted in antiquity'''.Izumimori, Ko. *Ancient Tombs of Yamato I* (『大和の古墳I』), Jinbun Shoin, 2003. During '''World War II''', the Japanese Imperial Army '''stationed an anti-aircraft gun battery''' at the site. At that time, stones from the '''burial chamber (originally quarried in Kashiwara, Osaka)''' were reportedly '''removed''' and repurposed.On-site intypeation board by the Tenri City Board of Education. == burial & area == [[File:080515 Nishiyama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|Aerial view of Nishiyama Kofun.
{{National Aerial Photography}}.
[[:File:Tenri-nishiyama_stereo.jpg|Stereo image here]]]] The tumulus is a '''three-tiered, [[Zenpō-kōhō-fun|rectangular keyhole-shaped mound]] (前方後方墳, [[zenpō-kōhō-fun]])''' with the front section '''oriented westward'''. Its area are: * '''Total length''': 183 meters * '''Rear section''' (square): 94m wide × 16m high * '''Front section''': 72m wide The '''lower level''' is '''rectangular''', while the '''middle and upper levels''' are '''rounder''', creating a hybrid '''keyhole-shaped mound (前方後円形, zenpō-kōenkei)'''. The '''central burial chamber''' is estimated to be a '''[[Vertical pit stone chamber|pit-style stone chamber]]''' based on '''historical records'''. The mound is positioned '''along three natural ridges''', with the '''central ridge typeing the main mound''', while the '''north and south ridges serve as outer embankments'''. A '''moat once surrounded the mound''', but it has since been '''filled in'''. This kofun is '''the largest of its kind in Japan'''. The '''unique construction''', with a '''rectangular lower tier supporting a rounder upper structure''', is believed to be '''original to its design'''. == burial goods & burial Goods == Excavations have uncovered: * '''Copper mirrors (fragments)''' * '''Green jasper arrowheads''' * '''Magatama beads''' * '''Iron swords and blades''' * '''Wheel-shaped stone object (碧玉製車輪石, hekigyoku-sei sharinseki)''' * '''Haniwa clay figures''', including: ** '''[[Cylindrical Haniwa|Cylindrical haniwa]] (円筒埴輪)''' ** '''Fin-shaped haniwa (鰭付円筒埴輪)''' ** '''[[Figural Haniwa|House-shaped haniwa]] (家形埴輪)''' == Current Condition == The '''mound is well preserved''', and due to '''lack of tree cover''', the '''three-tiered structure is clearly visible'''. == Access == * '''20-minute walk from [[Tenri Station]]''' - Located '''500 meters south''' of the '''Tenri University Reference Museum''' * '''Just north''' of '''Tenri Middle School''' == designation1 == === '''National Historic Site of Japan''' === * '''Original other_designation (1927)''': Nishiyama Kofun was other_designation1 a '''National other_designation'''. * '''Expansion (2018)''': The other_designation was '''expanded''' to Please do not use any bots that just remove the unknown parameters without looking at them. This was added through [[Special:MassEditRegex]] to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} [[Category:11]][[sn:Nishiyama Kofun]][[Category:11]]{{DEFAULTSORT:Nishiyama Kofun}}[[Category:11]] [[Category:11]][[sn:Nishiyama Kofun]][[Category:11]] [[Category:Nishiyama Kofun]][[ja:西山古墳]] {{Infobox ancient site|type = {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun}} |name = Nishiyama Kofun |image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px|]] |caption = Mound overview (left: anterior, right back: posterior) |location = {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}} {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}} Somanouchi Town |coordinates = {{coord|34|35|33|N|135|50|36|E|region:JP-29_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Nishiyama Kofun}} |type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} |area = Total length: 183m, height: 13m |burial = {{ill|Pit-style stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber}} |built = Early Kofun period |Interred = (Theory) A member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏}} |burial goods = Mirror fragments, stone arrowheads, iron sword fragments, magatama, and haniwa |alternate_name = National other_designation (other_designation1 April 8, 1927) |map = Japan Nara |type = Zenpō-kōhō-fun-W }} '''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in Somanouchi Town, {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}, Japan. It is other_designation1 as a National other_designation and is part of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster}}. == Overview == Constructed during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} (4th century), Nishiyama Kofun is the oldest of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster}}. The Kofun features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} at its base to a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} at its upper levels. The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day {{ill|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市}}), was targeted. == area and burial == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * '''Rear mound (posterior):''' 94m width, 16m height * '''Anterior mound:''' 72m width, 13m height The lower tier types a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in. Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design. == burial goods == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments''' * '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones''' * '''Surface burial goods:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure. == Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School. == Cultural Significance == === National other_designation === * Designated on April 8, 1927{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the other_designation1 area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018. == References == {{reflist}} == So a lot of these pages might not be marked on our wiki as having unknown parameters. But specifically keeping this comment here in case of import, these parameters should be added to [[Template:infobox ancient site]] rather than deleted from this draft or article[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:02, 28 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=I hope this is not too annoying but this article is gonna be placed under [[:Category:Pages using infobox ancient site with unknown parameters]] and there is a decent chance these unknown parameters are ones[[Category:marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] I want added to the main template like burial chamber structure and burial goods. Please do not use any bots that just remove the unknown parameters without looking at them. This was added through [[Special:MassEditRegex]] to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} [[Category:11]][[sn:Nishiyama Kofun]][[Category:11]]{{DEFAULTSORT:Nishiyama Kofun}}[[Category:11]] [[Category:11]][[sn:Nishiyama Kofun]][[Category:11]] [[Category:Nishiyama Kofun]][[ja:西山古墳]] {{Infobox ancient site|type = {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun}} |name = Nishiyama Kofun |image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px|]] |caption = Mound overview (left: anterior, right back: posterior) |location = {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}} {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}} Somanouchi Town |coordinates = {{coord|34|35|33|N|135|50|36|E|region:JP-29_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Nishiyama Kofun}} |type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} |area = Total length: 183m, height: 13m |burial = {{ill|Pit-style stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber}} |built = Early Kofun period |Interred = (Theory) A member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏}} |burial goods = Mirror fragments, stone arrowheads, iron sword fragments, magatama, and haniwa |alternate_name = National Historic Site (Historic Site1 April 8, 1927) |map = Japan Nara |type = Zenpō-kōhō-fun-W }} '''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in Somanouchi Town, {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}, Japan. It is Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site and is part of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster}}. == Overview == Constructed during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} (4th century), Nishiyama Kofun is the oldest of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster}}. The Kofun features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} at its base to a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} at its upper levels. The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day {{ill|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市}}), was targeted. == area and burial == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * '''Rear mound (posterior):''' 94m width, 16m height * '''Anterior mound:''' 72m width, 13m height The lower tier types a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in. Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design. == burial goods == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments''' * '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones''' * '''Surface burial goods:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure. == Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School. == Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the Historic Site1 area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018. == References == {{reflist}} == See (Ota)}} {{Infobox Kofun | name = Nishiyama Kofun | native_name = 西山古墳 | image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px]]
Mound overview (left: front section, back right: rear section) | location = {{ill|Tenri, Nara|ja|天理市}}, Nara Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = 34.5925 | coordinates = 135.8433 | region = Japan | type = {{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} (rectangular keyhole-shaped tumulus) | length = 183m, Height: 13m | burial = {{ill|Tateana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber}} (pit-style stone chamber) | built = Early Kofun period (4th century) | person = Possibly a member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏}} | burial goods = Mirrors, stone arrowheads, iron swords and blades, magatama beads, haniwa clay figures | Historic Site1 = National Historic Site of Japan (Historic Site1 April 8, 1927) }} '''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a '''large [[Zenpō-kōhō-fun|rectangular keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後方墳, zenpō-kōhō-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Tenri, Nara|ja|天理市}}, Nara Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''{{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster}}''' and is the '''largest kofun of its type in Japan'''. In '''1927 (Showa 2)''', it was '''Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site''' of Japan.{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/1958|title=Nishiyama Kofun - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}} It is also known by the '''alternate name "Nagariyama" (勾山, Magariyama).''' == Overview == The kofun was '''constructed during the early [[Kofun period]] (4th century)''' and is one of the '''earliest tumuli''' in the '''{{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster}}'''. The mound originally had a '''[[Vertical pit stone chamber|pit-style stone chamber]] (竪穴式石室, tateana-shiki sekishitsu)''', but it was likely '''looted in antiquity'''.Izumimori, Ko. *Ancient Tombs of Yamato I* (『大和の古墳I』), Jinbun Shoin, 2003. During '''World War II''', the Japanese Imperial Army '''stationed an anti-aircraft gun battery''' at the site. At that time, stones from the '''burial chamber (originally quarried in Kashiwara, Osaka)''' were reportedly '''removed''' and repurposed.On-site intypeation board by the Tenri City Board of Education. == burial & area == [[File:080515 Nishiyama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|Aerial view of Nishiyama Kofun.
{{National Aerial Photography}}.
[[:File:Tenri-nishiyama_stereo.jpg|Stereo image here]]]] The tumulus is a '''three-tiered, [[Zenpō-kōhō-fun|rectangular keyhole-shaped mound]] (前方後方墳, [[zenpō-kōhō-fun]])''' with the front section '''oriented westward'''. Its area are: * '''Total length''': 183 meters * '''Rear section''' (square): 94m wide × 16m high * '''Front section''': 72m wide The '''lower level''' is '''rectangular''', while the '''middle and upper levels''' are '''rounder''', creating a hybrid '''keyhole-shaped mound (前方後円形, zenpō-kōenkei)'''. The '''central burial chamber''' is estimated to be a '''[[Vertical pit stone chamber|pit-style stone chamber]]''' based on '''historical records'''. The mound is positioned '''along three natural ridges''', with the '''central ridge typeing the main mound''', while the '''north and south ridges serve as outer embankments'''. A '''moat once surrounded the mound''', but it has since been '''filled in'''. This kofun is '''the largest of its kind in Japan'''. The '''unique construction''', with a '''rectangular lower tier supporting a rounder upper structure''', is believed to be '''original to its design'''. == burial goods & burial Goods == Excavations have uncovered: * '''Copper mirrors (fragments)''' * '''Green jasper arrowheads''' * '''Magatama beads''' * '''Iron swords and blades''' * '''Wheel-shaped stone object (碧玉製車輪石, hekigyoku-sei sharinseki)''' * '''Haniwa clay figures''', including: ** '''[[Cylindrical Haniwa|Cylindrical haniwa]] (円筒埴輪)''' ** '''Fin-shaped haniwa (鰭付円筒埴輪)''' ** '''[[Figural Haniwa|House-shaped haniwa]] (家形埴輪)''' == Current Condition == The '''mound is well preserved''', and due to '''lack of tree cover''', the '''three-tiered structure is clearly visible'''. == Access == * '''20-minute walk from [[Tenri Station]]''' - Located '''500 meters south''' of the '''Tenri University Reference Museum''' * '''Just north''' of '''Tenri Middle School''' == designation1 == === '''National Historic Site of Japan''' === * '''Original Historic Site (1927)''': Nishiyama Kofun was Historic Site1 a '''National Historic Site'''. * '''Expansion (2018)''': The Historic Site was '''expanded''' to include '''Nishinorikura Kofun (西乗鞍古墳)''', renaming the site as the '''Somanochi Kofun Group (杣之内古墳群)'''.Ministry of Education, Science and Culture Announcement No. 19 (February 13, 2018). == References == It is Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site and is part of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster}}. == Overview == Constructed during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} (4th century), Nishiyama Kofun is the oldest of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster}}. The Kofun features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} at its base to a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} at its upper levels. The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day {{ill|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市}}), was targeted. == area and burial == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * '''Rear mound (posterior):''' 94m width, 16m height * '''Anterior mound:''' 72m width, 13m height The lower tier types a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in. Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design. == burial goods == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments''' * '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones''' * '''Surface burial goods:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure. == Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School. == Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the Historic Site1 area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018. == References == {{reflist}} == See {{DEFAULTSORT:Nishiyama Kofun}} {{otheruses|Nishiyama Kofun in Tenri, Nara|Nishiyama Kofun in Ota, Gunma|Nishiyama Kofun (Ota)}} {{Infobox Kofun | name = Nishiyama Kofun | native_name = 西山古墳 | image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px]]
Mound overview (left: front section, back right: rear section) | location = {{ill|Tenri, Nara|ja|天理市}}, Nara Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = 34.5925 | coordinates = 135.8433 | region = Japan | type = {{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} (rectangular keyhole-shaped tumulus) | length = 183m, Height: 13m | burial = {{ill|Tateana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber}} (pit-style stone chamber) | built = Early Kofun period (4th century) | person = Possibly a member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏}} | burial goods = Mirrors, stone arrowheads, iron swords and blades, magatama beads, haniwa clay figures | Historic Site1 = National Historic Site of Japan (Historic Site1 April 8, 1927) }} '''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a '''large [[Zenpō-kōhō-fun|rectangular keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後方墳, zenpō-kōhō-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Tenri, Nara|ja|天理市}}, Nara Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''{{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster}}''' and is the '''largest kofun of its type in Japan'''. In '''1927 (Showa 2)''', it was '''Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site''' of Japan.{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/1958|title=Nishiyama Kofun - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}} It is also known by the '''alternate name "Nagariyama" (勾山, Magariyama).''' == Overview == The kofun was '''constructed during the early [[Kofun period]] (4th century)''' and is one of the '''earliest tumuli''' in the '''{{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster}}'''. The mound originally had a '''[[Vertical pit stone chamber|pit-style stone chamber]] (竪穴式石室, tateana-shiki sekishitsu)''', but it was likely '''looted in antiquity'''.Izumimori, Ko. *Ancient Tombs of Yamato I* (『大和の古墳I』), Jinbun Shoin, 2003. During '''World War II''', the Japanese Imperial Army '''stationed an anti-aircraft gun battery''' at the site. At that time, stones from the '''burial chamber (originally quarried in Kashiwara, Osaka)''' were reportedly '''removed''' and repurposed.On-site intypeation board by the Tenri City Board of Education. == burial & area == [[File:080515 Nishiyama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|Aerial view of Nishiyama Kofun.
{{National Aerial Photography}}.
[[:File:Tenri-nishiyama_stereo.jpg|Stereo image here]]]] The tumulus is a '''three-tiered, [[Zenpō-kōhō-fun|rectangular keyhole-shaped mound]] (前方後方墳, [[zenpō-kōhō-fun]])''' with the front section '''oriented westward'''. Its area are: * '''Total length''': 183 meters * '''Rear section''' (square): 94m wide × 16m high * '''Front section''': 72m wide The '''lower level''' is '''rectangular''', while the '''middle and upper levels''' are '''rounder''', creating a hybrid '''keyhole-shaped mound (前方後円形, zenpō-kōenkei)'''. The '''central burial chamber''' is estimated to be a '''[[Vertical pit stone chamber|pit-style stone chamber]]''' based on '''historical records'''. The mound is positioned '''along three natural ridges''', with the '''central ridge typeing the main mound''', while the '''north and south ridges serve as outer embankments'''. A '''moat once surrounded the mound''', but it has since been '''filled in'''. This kofun is '''the largest of its kind in Japan'''. The '''unique construction''', with a '''rectangular lower tier supporting a rounder upper structure''', is believed to be '''original to its design'''. == burial goods & burial Goods == Excavations have uncovered: * '''Copper mirrors (fragments)''' * '''Green jasper arrowheads''' * '''Magatama beads''' * '''Iron swords and blades''' * '''Wheel-shaped stone object (碧玉製車輪石, hekigyoku-sei sharinseki)''' * '''Haniwa clay figures''', including: ** '''[[Cylindrical Haniwa|Cylindrical haniwa]] (円筒埴輪)''' ** '''Fin-shaped haniwa (鰭付円筒埴輪)''' ** '''[[Figural Haniwa|House-shaped haniwa]] (家形埴輪)''' == Current Condition == The '''mound is well preserved''', and due to '''lack of tree cover''', the '''three-tiered structure is clearly visible'''. == Access == * '''20-minute walk from [[Tenri Station]]''' - Located '''500 meters south''' of the '''Tenri University Reference Museum''' * '''Just north''' of '''Tenri Middle School''' == designation1 == === '''National Historic Site of Japan''' === * '''Original Historic Site (1927)''': Nishiyama Kofun was Historic Site1 a '''National Historic Site'''. * '''Expansion (2018)''': The Historic Site was '''expanded''' to include '''Nishinorikura Kofun (西乗鞍古墳)''', renaming the site as the '''Somanochi Kofun Group (杣之内古墳群)'''.Ministry of Education, Science and Culture Announcement No. 19 (February 13, 2018). == References == Nishiyama Kofun'''] * [http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html '''Tenri City Official Kofun Guide'''] {{DEFAULTSORT:Nishiyama Kofun}} [[Category:Somanochi Kofun Group]] Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day {{ill|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市}}), was targeted. == area and burial == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * '''Rear mound (posterior):''' 94m width, 16m height * '''Anterior mound:''' 72m width, 13m height The lower tier types a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in. Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design. == burial goods == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments''' * '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones''' * '''Surface burial goods:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure. == Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School. == Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the Historic Site1 area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018. == References == {{reflist}} == See {{DEFAULTSORT:Nishiyama Kofun}} {{otheruses|Nishiyama Kofun in Tenri, Nara|Nishiyama Kofun in Ota, Gunma|Nishiyama Kofun (Ota)}} {{Infobox Kofun | name = Nishiyama Kofun | native_name = 西山古墳 | image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px]]
Mound overview (left: front section, back right: rear section) | location = {{ill|Tenri, Nara|ja|天理市}}, Nara Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = 34.5925 | coordinates = 135.8433 | region = Japan | type = {{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} (rectangular keyhole-shaped tumulus) | length = 183m, Height: 13m | burial = {{ill|Tateana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber}} (pit-style stone chamber) | built = Early Kofun period (4th century) | person = Possibly a member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏}} | burial goods = Mirrors, stone arrowheads, iron swords and blades, magatama beads, haniwa clay figures | Historic Site1 = National Historic Site of Japan (Historic Site1 April 8, 1927) }} '''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a '''large [[Zenpō-kōhō-fun|rectangular keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後方墳, zenpō-kōhō-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Tenri, Nara|ja|天理市}}, Nara Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''{{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster}}''' and is the '''largest kofun of its type in Japan'''. In '''1927 (Showa 2)''', it was '''Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site''' of Japan.{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/1958|title=Nishiyama Kofun - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}} It is also known by the '''alternate name "Nagariyama" (勾山, Magariyama).''' == Overview == The kofun was '''constructed during the early [[Kofun period]] (4th century)''' and is one of the '''earliest tumuli''' in the '''{{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster}}'''. The mound originally had a '''[[Vertical pit stone chamber|pit-style stone chamber]] (竪穴式石室, tateana-shiki sekishitsu)''', but it was likely '''looted in antiquity'''.Izumimori, Ko. *Ancient Tombs of Yamato I* (『大和の古墳I』), Jinbun Shoin, 2003. During '''World War II''', the Japanese Imperial Army '''stationed an anti-aircraft gun battery''' at the site. At that time, stones from the '''burial chamber (originally quarried in Kashiwara, Osaka)''' were reportedly '''removed''' and repurposed.On-site intypeation board by the Tenri City Board of Education. == burial & area == [[File:080515 Nishiyama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|Aerial view of Nishiyama Kofun.
{{National Aerial Photography}}.
[[:File:Tenri-nishiyama_stereo.jpg|Stereo image here]]]] The tumulus is a '''three-tiered, [[Zenpō-kōhō-fun|rectangular keyhole-shaped mound]] (前方後方墳, [[zenpō-kōhō-fun]])''' with the front section '''oriented westward'''. Its area are: * '''Total length''': 183 meters * '''Rear section''' (square): 94m wide × 16m high * '''Front section''': 72m wide The '''lower level''' is '''rectangular''', while the '''middle and upper levels''' are '''rounder''', creating a hybrid '''keyhole-shaped mound (前方後円形, zenpō-kōenkei)'''. The '''central burial chamber''' is estimated to be a '''[[Vertical pit stone chamber|pit-style stone chamber]]''' based on '''historical records'''. The mound is positioned '''along three natural ridges''', with the '''central ridge typeing the main mound''', while the '''north and south ridges serve as outer embankments'''. A '''moat once surrounded the mound''', but it has since been '''filled in'''. This kofun is '''the largest of its kind in Japan'''. The '''unique construction''', with a '''rectangular lower tier supporting a rounder upper structure''', is believed to be '''original to its design'''. == burial goods & burial Goods == Excavations have uncovered: * '''Copper mirrors (fragments)''' * '''Green jasper arrowheads''' * '''Magatama beads''' * '''Iron swords and blades''' * '''Wheel-shaped stone object (碧玉製車輪石, hekigyoku-sei sharinseki)''' * '''Haniwa clay figures''', including: ** '''[[Cylindrical Haniwa|Cylindrical haniwa]] (円筒埴輪)''' ** '''Fin-shaped haniwa (鰭付円筒埴輪)''' ** '''[[Figural Haniwa|House-shaped haniwa]] (家形埴輪)''' == Current Condition == The '''mound is well preserved''', and due to '''lack of tree cover''', the '''three-tiered structure is clearly visible'''. == Access == * '''20-minute walk from [[Tenri Station]]''' - Located '''500 meters south''' of the '''Tenri University Reference Museum''' * '''Just north''' of '''Tenri Middle School''' == designation1 == === '''National Historic Site of Japan''' === * '''Original Historic Site (1927)''': Nishiyama Kofun was Historic Site1 a '''National Historic Site'''. * '''Expansion (2018)''': The Historic Site was '''expanded''' to include '''Nishinorikura Kofun (西乗鞍古墳)''', renaming the site as the '''Somanochi Kofun Group (杣之内古墳群)'''.Ministry of Education, Science and Culture Announcement No. 19 (February 13, 2018). == References == {{DEFAULTSORT:Nishiyama Kofun}} {{otheruses|Nishiyama Kofun in Tenri, Nara|Nishiyama Kofun in Ota, Gunma|Nishiyama Kofun (Ota)}} {{Infobox Kofun | name = Nishiyama Kofun | native_name = 西山古墳 | image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px]]
Mound overview (left: front section, back right: rear section) | location = {{ill|Tenri, Nara|ja|天理市}}, Nara Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = 34.5925 | coordinates = 135.8433 | region = Japan | type = {{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} (rectangular keyhole-shaped tumulus) | length = 183m, Height: 13m | burial = {{ill|Tateana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber}} (pit-style stone chamber) | built = Early Kofun period (4th century) | person = Possibly a member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏}} | burial goods = Mirrors, stone arrowheads, iron swords and blades, magatama beads, haniwa clay figures | Historic Site1 = National Historic Site of Japan (Historic Site1 April 8, 1927) }} '''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a '''large [[Zenpō-kōhō-fun|rectangular keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後方墳, zenpō-kōhō-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Tenri, Nara|ja|天理市}}, Nara Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''{{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster}}''' and is the '''largest kofun of its type in Japan'''. In '''1927 (Showa 2)''', it was '''Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site''' of Japan.{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/1958|title=Nishiyama Kofun - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}} It is also known by the '''alternate name "Nagariyama" (勾山, Magariyama).''' == Overview == The kofun was '''constructed during the early [[Kofun period]] (4th century)''' and is one of the '''earliest tumuli''' in the '''{{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster}}'''. The mound originally had a '''[[Vertical pit stone chamber|pit-style stone chamber]] (竪穴式石室, tateana-shiki sekishitsu)''', but it was likely '''looted in antiquity'''.Izumimori, Ko. *Ancient Tombs of Yamato I* (『大和の古墳I』), Jinbun Shoin, 2003. During '''World War II''', the Japanese Imperial Army '''stationed an anti-aircraft gun battery''' at the site. At that time, stones from the '''burial chamber (originally quarried in Kashiwara, Osaka)''' were reportedly '''removed''' and repurposed.On-site intypeation board by the Tenri City Board of Education. == burial & area == [[File:080515 Nishiyama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|Aerial view of Nishiyama Kofun.
{{National Aerial Photography}}.
[[:File:Tenri-nishiyama_stereo.jpg|Stereo image here]]]] The tumulus is a '''three-tiered, [[Zenpō-kōhō-fun|rectangular keyhole-shaped mound]] (前方後方墳, [[zenpō-kōhō-fun]])''' with the front section '''oriented westward'''. Its area are: * '''Total length''': 183 meters * '''Rear section''' (square): 94m wide × 16m high * '''Front section''': 72m wide The '''lower level''' is '''rectangular''', while the '''middle and upper levels''' are '''rounder''', creating a hybrid '''keyhole-shaped mound (前方後円形, zenpō-kōenkei)'''. The '''central burial chamber''' is estimated to be a '''[[Vertical pit stone chamber|pit-style stone chamber]]''' based on '''historical records'''. The mound is positioned '''along three natural ridges''', with the '''central ridge typeing the main mound''', while the '''north and south ridges serve as outer embankments'''. A '''moat once surrounded the mound''', but it has since been '''filled in'''. This kofun is '''the largest of its kind in Japan'''. The '''unique construction''', with a '''rectangular lower tier supporting a rounder upper structure''', is believed to be '''original to its design'''. == burial goods & burial Goods == Excavations have uncovered: * '''Copper mirrors (fragments)''' * '''Green jasper arrowheads''' * '''Magatama beads''' * '''Iron swords and blades''' * '''Wheel-shaped stone object (碧玉製車輪石, hekigyoku-sei sharinseki)''' * '''Haniwa clay figures''', including: ** '''[[Cylindrical Haniwa|Cylindrical haniwa]] (円筒埴輪)''' ** '''Fin-shaped haniwa (鰭付円筒埴輪)''' ** '''[[Figural Haniwa|House-shaped haniwa]] (家形埴輪)''' == Current Condition == The '''mound is well preserved''', and due to '''lack of tree cover''', the '''three-tiered structure is clearly visible'''. == Access == * '''20-minute walk from [[Tenri Station]]''' - Located '''500 meters south''' of the '''Tenri University Reference Museum''' * '''Just north''' of '''Tenri Middle School''' == designation1 == === '''National Historic Site of Japan''' === * '''Original Historic Site (1927)''': Nishiyama Kofun was Historic Site1 a '''National Historic Site'''. * '''Expansion (2018)''': The Historic Site was '''expanded''' to include '''Nishinorikura Kofun (西乗鞍古墳)''', renaming the site as the '''Somanochi Kofun Group (杣之内古墳群)'''.Ministry of Education, Science and Culture Announcement No. 19 (February 13, 2018). == References == Please do not use any bots that just remove the unknown parameters without looking at them. This was added through [[Special:MassEditRegex]] to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun}} |name = Nishiyama Kofun |image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px|]] |caption = Mound overview (left: anterior, right back: posterior) |location = {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}} {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}} Somanouchi Town |coordinates = {{coord|34|35|33|N|135|50|36|E|region:JP-29_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Nishiyama Kofun}} |type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} |area = Total length: 183m, height: 13m |burial = {{ill|Pit-style stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber}} |built = Early Kofun period |Interred = (Theory) A member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏}} |burial goods = Mirror fragments, stone arrowheads, iron sword fragments, magatama, and haniwa |alternate_name = National Historic Site (Historic Site1 April 8, 1927) |map = Japan Nara |type = Zenpō-kōhō-fun-W }} '''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in Somanouchi Town, {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}, Japan. It is Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site and is part of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster}}. == Overview == Constructed during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} (4th century), Nishiyama Kofun is the oldest of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster}}. The Kofun features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} at its base to a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} at its upper levels. The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day {{ill|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市}}), was targeted. == area and burial == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * '''Rear mound (posterior):''' 94m width, 16m height * '''Anterior mound:''' 72m width, 13m height The lower tier types a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in. Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design. == burial goods == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments''' * '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones''' * '''Surface burial goods:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure. == Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School. == Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the Historic Site1 area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster}} == External Links == * {{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}} * [http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html Tenri City Kofun Guide] {{otheruses|Nishiyama Kofun in Tenri, Nara|Nishiyama Kofun in Ota, Gunma|Nishiyama Kofun (Ota)}} {{Infobox Kofun | name = Nishiyama Kofun | native_name = 西山古墳 | image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px]]

Please do not use any bots that just remove the unknown parameters without looking at them. This was added through [[Special:MassEditRegex]] to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft}} |name = Nishiyama Kofun |image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px|]] |caption = Mound overview (left: anterior, right back: posterior) |location = {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県|12=draft}} {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市|12=draft}} Somanouchi Town |coordinates = {{coord|34|35|33|N|135|50|36|E|region:JP-29_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Nishiyama Kofun}} |type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft}} |area = Total length: 183m, height: 13m |burial = {{ill|Pit-style stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}} |built = Early Kofun period |Interred = (Theory) A member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏|12=draft}} |burial goods = Mirror fragments, stone arrowheads, iron sword fragments, magatama, and haniwa |alternate_name = National Historic Site (Historic Site1 April 8, 1927) |map = Japan Nara |type = Zenpō-kōhō-fun-W }} '''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|12=draft}} located in Somanouchi Town, {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市|12=draft}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県|12=draft}}, Japan. It is Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site and is part of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|12=draft}}. == Overview == Constructed during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft}} (4th century), Nishiyama Kofun is the oldest of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|12=draft}}. The Kofun features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft}} at its base to a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}} at its upper levels. The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day {{ill|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市|12=draft}}), was targeted. == area and burial == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * '''Rear mound (posterior):''' 94m width, 16m height * '''Anterior mound:''' 72m width, 13m height The lower tier types a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in. Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design. == burial goods == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments''' * '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones''' * '''Surface burial goods:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure. == Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館|12=draft}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School. == Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the Historic Site1 area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|12=draft}} == External Links == * {{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}} * [http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html Tenri City Kofun Guide] {{otheruses|Nishiyama Kofun in Tenri, Nara|Nishiyama Kofun in Ota, Gunma|Nishiyama Kofun (Ota)}} {{Infobox Kofun | name = Nishiyama Kofun | native_name = 西山古墳 | image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px]]
Mound overview (left: front section, back right: rear section) | location = {{ill|Tenri, Nara|ja|天理市|12=draft}}, Nara Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = 34.5925 | coordinates = 135.8433 | region = Japan | type = {{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft}} (rectangular keyhole-shaped tumulus) | length = 183m, Height: 13m | burial = {{ill|Tateana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}} (pit-style stone chamber) | built = Early Kofun period (4th century) | person = Possibly a member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏|12=draft}} | burial goods = Mirrors, stone arrowheads, iron swords and blades, magatama beads, haniwa clay figures | Historic Site1 = National Historic Site of Japan (Historic Site1 April 8, 1927) }} '''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a '''large [[Zenpō-kōhō-fun|rectangular keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後方墳, zenpō-kōhō-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Tenri, Nara|ja|天理市|12=draft}}, Nara Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''{{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|12=draft}}''' and is the '''largest kofun of its type in Japan'''. In '''1927 (Showa 2)''', it was '''Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site''' of Japan.{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/1958|title=Nishiyama Kofun - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}} It is also known by the '''alternate name "Nagariyama" (勾山, Magariyama).''' == Overview == The kofun was '''constructed during the early [[Kofun period]] (4th century)''' and is one of the '''earliest tumuli''' in the '''{{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|12=draft}}'''. The mound originally had a '''[[Vertical pit stone chamber|pit-style stone chamber]] (竪穴式石室, tateana-shiki sekishitsu)''', but it was likely '''looted in antiquity'''.Izumimori, Ko. *Ancient Tombs of Yamato I* (『大和の古墳I』), Jinbun Shoin, 2003. During '''World War II''', the Japanese Imperial Army '''stationed an anti-aircraft gun battery''' at the site. At that time, stones from the '''burial chamber (originally quarried in Kashiwara, Osaka)''' were reportedly '''removed''' and repurposed.On-site intypeation board by the Tenri City Board of Education. == burial & area == [[File:080515 Nishiyama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|Aerial view of Nishiyama Kofun.
{{National Aerial Photography}}.
[[:File:Tenri-nishiyama_stereo.jpg|Stereo image here]]]] The tumulus is a '''three-tiered, [[Zenpō-kōhō-fun|rectangular keyhole-shaped mound]] (前方後方墳, [[zenpō-kōhō-fun]])''' with the front section '''oriented westward'''. Its area are: * '''Total length''': 183 meters * '''Rear section''' (square): 94m wide × 16m high * '''Front section''': 72m wide The '''lower level''' is '''rectangular''', while the '''middle and upper levels''' are '''rounder''', creating a hybrid '''keyhole-shaped mound (前方後円形, zenpō-kōenkei)'''. The '''central burial chamber''' is estimated to be a '''[[Vertical pit stone chamber|pit-style stone chamber]]''' based on '''historical records'''. The mound is positioned '''along three natural ridges''', with the '''central ridge typeing the main mound''', while the '''north and south ridges serve as outer embankments'''. A '''moat once surrounded the mound''', but it has since been '''filled in'''. This kofun is '''the largest of its kind in Japan'''. The '''unique construction''', with a '''rectangular lower tier supporting a rounder upper structure''', is believed to be '''original to its design'''. == burial goods & burial Goods == Excavations have uncovered: * '''Copper mirrors (fragments)''' * '''Green jasper arrowheads''' * '''Magatama beads''' * '''Iron swords and blades''' * '''Wheel-shaped stone object (碧玉製車輪石, hekigyoku-sei sharinseki)''' * '''Haniwa clay figures''', including: ** '''[[Cylindrical Haniwa|Cylindrical haniwa]] (円筒埴輪)''' ** '''Fin-shaped haniwa (鰭付円筒埴輪)''' ** '''[[Figural Haniwa|House-shaped haniwa]] (家形埴輪)''' == Current Condition == The '''mound is well preserved''', and due to '''lack of tree cover''', the '''three-tiered structure is clearly visible'''. == Access == * '''20-minute walk from [[Tenri Station]]''' - Located '''500 meters south''' of the '''Tenri University Reference Museum''' * '''Just north''' of '''Tenri Middle School''' == designation1 == === '''National Historic Site of Japan''' === * '''Original Historic Site (1927)''': Nishiyama Kofun was Historic Site1 a '''National Historic Site'''. * '''Expansion (2018)''': The Historic Site was '''expanded''' to include '''Nishinorikura Kofun (西乗鞍古墳)''', renaming the site as the '''Somanochi Kofun Group (杣之内古墳群)'''.Ministry of Education, Science and Culture Announcement No. 19 (February 13, 2018). == References == Please do not use any bots that just remove the unknown parameters without looking at them. This was added through [[Special:MassEditRegex]] to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft}} |name = Nishiyama Kofun |image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px|]] |caption = Mound overview (left: anterior, right back: posterior) |location = {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県|12=draft}} {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市|12=draft}} Somanouchi Town |coordinates = {{coord|34|35|33|N|135|50|36|E|region:JP-29_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Nishiyama Kofun}} |type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft}} |area = Total length: 183m, height: 13m |burial = {{ill|Pit-style stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}} |built = Early Kofun period |Interred = (Theory) A member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏|12=draft}} |burial goods = Mirror fragments, stone arrowheads, iron sword fragments, magatama, and haniwa |alternate_name = National Historic Site (Historic Site1 April 8, 1927) |map = Japan Nara |type = Zenpō-kōhō-fun-W }} '''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|12=draft}} located in Somanouchi Town, {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市|12=draft}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県|12=draft}}, Japan. It is Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site and is part of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|12=draft}}. == Overview == Constructed during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft}} (4th century), Nishiyama Kofun is the oldest of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|12=draft}}. The Kofun features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft}} at its base to a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}} at its upper levels. The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day {{ill|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市|12=draft}}), was targeted. == area and burial == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * '''Rear mound (posterior):''' 94m width, 16m height * '''Anterior mound:''' 72m width, 13m height The lower tier types a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in. Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design. == burial goods == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments''' * '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones''' * '''Surface burial goods:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure. == Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館|12=draft}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School. == Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the Historic Site1 area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|12=draft}} == External Links == * {{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}} * [http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html Tenri City Kofun Guide] {{otheruses|Nishiyama Kofun in Tenri, Nara|Nishiyama Kofun in Ota, Gunma|Nishiyama Kofun (Ota)}} {{Infobox Kofun | name = Nishiyama Kofun | native_name = 西山古墳 | image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px]]
Mound overview (left: front section, back right: rear section) | location = {{ill|Tenri, Nara|ja|天理市|12=draft}}, Nara Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = 34.5925 | coordinates = 135.8433 | region = Japan | type = {{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft}} (rectangular keyhole-shaped tumulus) | length = 183m, Height: 13m | burial = {{ill|Tateana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}} (pit-style stone chamber) | built = Early Kofun period (4th century) | person = Possibly a member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏|12=draft}} | burial goods = Mirrors, stone arrowheads, iron swords and blades, magatama beads, haniwa clay figures | Historic Site1 = National Historic Site of Japan (Historic Site1 April 8, 1927) }} '''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a '''large [[Zenpō-kōhō-fun|rectangular keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後方墳, zenpō-kōhō-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Tenri, Nara|ja|天理市|12=draft}}, Nara Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''{{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|12=draft}}''' and is the '''largest kofun of its type in Japan'''. In '''1927 (Showa 2)''', it was '''Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site''' of Japan.{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/1958|title=Nishiyama Kofun - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}} It is also known by the '''alternate name "Nagariyama" (勾山, Magariyama).''' == Overview == The kofun was '''constructed during the early [[Kofun period]] (4th century)''' and is one of the '''earliest tumuli''' in the '''{{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|12=draft}}'''. The mound originally had a '''[[Vertical pit stone chamber|pit-style stone chamber]] (竪穴式石室, tateana-shiki sekishitsu)''', but it was likely '''looted in antiquity'''.Izumimori, Ko. *Ancient Tombs of Yamato I* (『大和の古墳I』), Jinbun Shoin, 2003. During '''World War II''', the Japanese Imperial Army '''stationed an anti-aircraft gun battery''' at the site. At that time, stones from the '''burial chamber (originally quarried in Kashiwara, Osaka)''' were reportedly '''removed''' and repurposed.On-site intypeation board by the Tenri City Board of Education. == burial & area == [[File:080515 Nishiyama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|Aerial view of Nishiyama Kofun.
{{National Aerial Photography}}.
[[:File:Tenri-nishiyama_stereo.jpg|Stereo image here]]]] The tumulus is a '''three-tiered, [[Zenpō-kōhō-fun|rectangular keyhole-shaped mound]] (前方後方墳, [[zenpō-kōhō-fun]])''' with the front section '''oriented westward'''. Its area are: * '''Total length''': 183 meters * '''Rear section''' (square): 94m wide × 16m high * '''Front section''': 72m wide The '''lower level''' is '''rectangular''', while the '''middle and upper levels''' are '''rounder''', creating a hybrid '''keyhole-shaped mound (前方後円形, zenpō-kōenkei)'''. The '''central burial chamber''' is estimated to be a '''[[Vertical pit stone chamber|pit-style stone chamber]]''' based on '''historical records'''. The mound is positioned '''along three natural ridges''', with the '''central ridge typeing the main mound''', while the '''north and south ridges serve as outer embankments'''. A '''moat once surrounded the mound''', but it has since been '''filled in'''. This kofun is '''the largest of its kind in Japan'''. The '''unique construction''', with a '''rectangular lower tier supporting a rounder upper structure''', is believed to be '''original to its design'''. == burial goods & burial Goods == Excavations have uncovered: * '''Copper mirrors (fragments)''' * '''Green jasper arrowheads''' * '''Magatama beads''' * '''Iron swords and blades''' * '''Wheel-shaped stone object (碧玉製車輪石, hekigyoku-sei sharinseki)''' * '''Haniwa clay figures''', including: ** '''[[Cylindrical Haniwa|Cylindrical haniwa]] (円筒埴輪)''' ** '''Fin-shaped haniwa (鰭付円筒埴輪)''' ** '''[[Figural Haniwa|House-shaped haniwa]] (家形埴輪)''' == Current Condition == The '''mound is well preserved''', and due to '''lack of tree cover''', the '''three-tiered structure is clearly visible'''. == Access == * '''20-minute walk from [[Tenri Station]]''' - Located '''500 meters south''' of the '''Tenri University Reference Museum''' * '''Just north''' of '''Tenri Middle School''' == designation1 == === '''National Historic Site of Japan''' === * '''Original Historic Site (1927)''': Nishiyama Kofun was Historic Site1 a '''National Historic Site'''. * '''Expansion (2018)''': The Historic Site was '''expanded''' to include '''Nishinorikura Kofun (西乗鞍古墳)''', renaming the site as the '''Somanochi Kofun Group (杣之内古墳群)'''.Ministry of Education, Science and Culture Announcement No. 19 (February 13, 2018). == References == {{Reflist}} == Additional Resources == * '''On-site intypeation board''' (Tenri City Board of Education) * '''Tenri City Website: Kofun Guide''' == Related Articles == * {{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|12=draft}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Nishiyama Kofun}} * [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/1958 '''Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan): Nishiyama Kofun'''] * [http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html '''Tenri City Official Kofun Guide'''] [[Category:Kofun template and pages that transclude it]] This was added through [[Special:MassEditRegex]] to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft}} |name = Nishiyama Kofun |image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px|]] |caption = Mound overview (left: anterior, right back: posterior) |location = {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県|12=draft}} {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市|12=draft}} Somanouchi Town |coordinates = {{coord|34|35|33|N|135|50|36|E|region:JP-29_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Nishiyama Kofun}} |type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft}} |area = Total length: 183m, height: 13m |burial = {{ill|Pit-style stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}} |built = Early Kofun period |Interred = (Theory) A member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏|12=draft}} |burial goods = Mirror fragments, stone arrowheads, iron sword fragments, magatama, and haniwa |alternate_name = National Historic Site (Historic Site1 April 8, 1927) |map = Japan Nara |type = Zenpō-kōhō-fun-W }} '''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|12=draft}} located in Somanouchi Town, {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市|12=draft}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県|12=draft}}, Japan. It is Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site and is part of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|12=draft}}. == Overview == Constructed during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft}} (4th century), Nishiyama Kofun is the oldest of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|12=draft}}. The Kofun features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft}} at its base to a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}} at its upper levels. The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day {{ill|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市|12=draft}}), was targeted. == area and burial == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * '''Rear mound (posterior):''' 94m width, 16m height * '''Anterior mound:''' 72m width, 13m height The lower tier types a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in. Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design. == burial goods == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments''' * '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones''' * '''Surface burial goods:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure. == Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館|12=draft}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School. == Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the Historic Site1 area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|12=draft}} == External Links == * {{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}} * [http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html Tenri City Kofun Guide] {{otheruses|Nishiyama Kofun in Tenri, Nara|Nishiyama Kofun in Ota, Gunma|Nishiyama Kofun (Ota)}} {{Infobox Kofun | name = Nishiyama Kofun | native_name = 西山古墳 | image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px]]
Mound overview (left: front section, back right: rear section) | location = {{ill|Tenri, Nara|ja|天理市|12=draft}}, Nara Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = 34.5925 | coordinates = 135.8433 | region = Japan | type = {{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft}} (rectangular keyhole-shaped tumulus) | length = 183m, Height: 13m | burial = {{ill|Tateana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}} (pit-style stone chamber) | built = Early Kofun period (4th century) | person = Possibly a member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏|12=draft}} | burial goods = Mirrors, stone arrowheads, iron swords and blades, magatama beads, haniwa clay figures | Historic Site1 = National Historic Site of Japan (Historic Site1 April 8, 1927) }} '''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a '''large [[Zenpō-kōhō-fun|rectangular keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後方墳, zenpō-kōhō-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Tenri, Nara|ja|天理市|12=draft}}, Nara Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''{{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|12=draft}}''' and is the '''largest kofun of its type in Japan'''. In '''1927 (Showa 2)''', it was '''Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site''' of Japan.{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/1958|title=Nishiyama Kofun - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}} It is also known by the '''alternate name "Nagariyama" (勾山, Magariyama).''' == Overview == The kofun was '''constructed during the early [[Kofun period]] (4th century)''' and is one of the '''earliest tumuli''' in the '''{{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|12=draft}}'''. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design. == burial goods == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments''' * '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones''' * '''Surface burial goods:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure. == Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館|12=draft}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School. == Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the Historic Site1 area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|12=draft}} == External Links == * {{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}} * [http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html Tenri City Kofun Guide] {{otheruses|Nishiyama Kofun in Tenri, Nara|Nishiyama Kofun in Ota, Gunma|Nishiyama Kofun (Ota)}} {{Infobox Kofun | name = Nishiyama Kofun | native_name = 西山古墳 | image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px]]
Mound overview (left: front section, back right: rear section) | location = {{ill|Tenri, Nara|ja|天理市|12=draft}}, Nara Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = 34.5925 | coordinates = 135.8433 | region = Japan | type = {{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft}} (rectangular keyhole-shaped tumulus) | length = 183m, Height: 13m | burial = {{ill|Tateana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}} (pit-style stone chamber) | built = Early Kofun period (4th century) | person = Possibly a member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏|12=draft}} | burial goods = Mirrors, stone arrowheads, iron swords and blades, magatama beads, haniwa clay figures | Historic Site1 = National Historic Site of Japan (Historic Site1 April 8, 1927) }} '''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a '''large [[Zenpō-kōhō-fun|rectangular keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後方墳, zenpō-kōhō-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Tenri, Nara|ja|天理市|12=draft}}, Nara Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''{{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|12=draft}}''' and is the '''largest kofun of its type in Japan'''. In '''1927 (Showa 2)''', it was '''Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site''' of Japan.{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/1958|title=Nishiyama Kofun - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}} It is also known by the '''alternate name "Nagariyama" (勾山, Magariyama).''' == Overview == The kofun was '''constructed during the early [[Kofun period]] (4th century)''' and is one of the '''earliest tumuli''' in the '''{{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|12=draft}}'''. The mound originally had a '''[[Vertical pit stone chamber|pit-style stone chamber]] (竪穴式石室, tateana-shiki sekishitsu)''', but it was likely '''looted in antiquity'''.Izumimori, Ko. *Ancient Tombs of Yamato I* (『大和の古墳I』), Jinbun Shoin, 2003. {{National Aerial Photography}}.

Its area are: * '''Total length''': 183 meters * '''Rear section''' (square): 94m wide × 16m high * '''Front section''': 72m wide The '''lower level''' is '''rectangular''', while the '''middle and upper levels''' are '''rounder''', creating a hybrid '''keyhole-shaped mound (前方後円形, zenpō-kōenkei)'''. A '''moat once surrounded the mound''', but it has since been '''filled in'''. This kofun is '''the largest of its kind in Japan'''. sharinseki)''' * '''Haniwa clay figures''', including: ** '''[[Cylindrical Haniwa|Cylindrical haniwa]] (円筒埴輪)''' ** '''Fin-shaped haniwa (鰭付円筒埴輪)''' ** '''[[Figural Haniwa|House-shaped haniwa]] It is Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site and is part of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|12=draft}}. == Overview == Constructed during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft}} (4th century), Nishiyama Kofun is the oldest of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|12=draft}}. The Kofun features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft}} at its base to a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}} at its upper levels.
