It is Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site and is part of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|12=draft|12=draft}}. == Overview == Constructed during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft|12=draft}} (4th century), Nishiyama Kofun is the oldest of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|12=draft|12=draft}}. The Kofun features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft|12=draft}} at its base to a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft|12=draft}} at its upper levels. The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day {{ill|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市|12=draft|12=draft}}), was targeted. == area and burial == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * '''Rear mound (posterior):''' 94m width, 16m height * '''Anterior mound:''' 72m width, 13m height The lower tier types a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft|12=draft}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft|12=draft}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in. Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design. == burial goods == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments''' * '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones''' * '''Surface burial goods:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure. == Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館|12=draft|12=draft}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School. == Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927{{国cultural property等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the Historic Site1 area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|12=draft|12=draft}} == External Links == * {{国cultural property等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}} * [http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html Tenri City Kofun Guide] {{otheruses|Nishiyama Kofun in Tenri, Nara|Nishiyama Kofun in Ota, Gunma|Nishiyama Kofun (Ota)}} {{Infobox Kofun | name = Nishiyama Kofun | native_name = 西山古墳 | image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px]]
Mound overview (left: front section, back right: rear section) | location = {{ill|Tenri, Nara|ja|天理市|12=draft|12=draft}}, Nara Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = 34.5925 | coordinates = 135.8433 | region = Japan | type = {{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft|12=draft}} (rectangular keyhole-shaped tumulus) | length = 183m, Height: 13m | burial = {{ill|Tateana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft|12=draft}} (pit-style stone chamber) | built = Early Kofun period (4th century) | person = Possibly a member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏|12=draft|12=draft}} | burial goods = Mirrors, stone arrowheads, iron swords and blades, magatama beads, haniwa clay figures | Historic Site1 = National Historic Site of Japan (Historic Site1 April 8, 1927) }} '''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a '''large [[Zenpō-kōhō-fun|rectangular keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後方墳, zenpō-kōhō-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Tenri, Nara|ja|天理市|12=draft|12=draft}}, Nara Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''{{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|12=draft|12=draft}}''' and is the '''largest kofun of its type in Japan'''. In '''1927 (Showa 2)''', it was '''Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site''' of Japan.{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/1958|title=Nishiyama Kofun - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}} It is also known by the '''alternate name "Nagariyama" (勾山, Magariyama).''' == Overview == The kofun was '''constructed during the early [[Kofun period]] (4th century)''' and is one of the '''earliest tumuli''' in the '''{{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|12=draft|12=draft}}'''. The mound originally had a '''[[Vertical pit stone chamber|pit-style stone chamber]] (竪穴式石室, tateana-shiki sekishitsu)''', but it was likely '''looted in antiquity'''.Izumimori, Ko. *Ancient Tombs of Yamato I* (『大和の古墳I』), Jinbun Shoin, 2003. During '''World War II''', the Japanese Imperial Army '''stationed an anti-aircraft gun battery''' at the site. At that time, stones from the '''burial chamber (originally quarried in Kashiwara, Osaka)''' were reportedly '''removed''' and repurposed.On-site intypeation board by the Tenri City Board of Education. == burial & area == [[File:080515 Nishiyama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|Aerial view of Nishiyama Kofun.
{{National Aerial Photography}}.
[[:File:Tenri-nishiyama_stereo.jpg|Stereo image here]]]] The tumulus is a '''three-tiered, [[Zenpō-kōhō-fun|rectangular keyhole-shaped mound]] (前方後方墳, [[zenpō-kōhō-fun]])''' with the front section '''oriented westward'''. Its area are: * '''Total length''': 183 meters * '''Rear section''' (square): 94m wide × 16m high * '''Front section''': 72m wide The '''lower level''' is '''rectangular''', while the '''middle and upper levels''' are '''rounder''', creating a hybrid '''keyhole-shaped mound (前方後円形, zenpō-kōenkei)'''. The '''central burial chamber''' is estimated to be a '''[[Vertical pit stone chamber|pit-style stone chamber]]''' based on '''historical records'''. The mound is positioned '''along three natural ridges''', with the '''central ridge typeing the main mound''', while the '''north and south ridges serve as outer embankments'''. A '''moat once surrounded the mound''', but it has since been '''filled in'''. This kofun is '''the largest of its kind in Japan'''. The '''unique construction''', with a '''rectangular lower tier supporting a rounder upper structure''', is believed to be '''original to its design'''. == burial goods & burial Goods == Excavations have uncovered: * '''Copper mirrors (fragments)''' * '''Green jasper arrowheads''' * '''Magatama beads''' * '''Iron swords and blades''' * '''Wheel-shaped stone object (碧玉製車輪石, hekigyoku-sei sharinseki)''' * '''Haniwa clay figures''', including: ** '''[[Cylindrical Haniwa|Cylindrical haniwa]] (円筒埴輪)''' ** '''Fin-shaped haniwa (鰭付円筒埴輪)''' ** '''[[Figural Haniwa|House-shaped haniwa]] (家形埴輪)''' == Current Condition == The '''mound is well preserved''', and due to '''lack of tree cover''', the '''three-tiered structure is clearly visible'''. == Access == * '''20-minute walk from [[Tenri Station]]''' - Located '''500 meters south''' of the '''Tenri University Reference Museum''' * '''Just north''' of '''Tenri Middle School''' == designation1 == === '''National Historic Site of Japan''' === * '''Original Historic Site (1927)''': Nishiyama Kofun was Historic Site1 a '''National Historic Site'''. * '''Expansion (2018)''': The Historic Site was '''expanded''' to include '''Nishinorikura Kofun (西乗鞍古墳)''', renaming the site as the '''Somanochi Kofun Group (杣之内古墳群)'''.Ministry of Education, Science and Culture Announcement No. 19 (February 13, 2018). == References == So a lot of these pages might not be marked on our wiki as having unknown parameters. But specifically keeping this comment here in case of import, these parameters should be added to [[Template:infobox ancient site]] rather than deleted from this draft or article[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:02, 28 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=I hope this is not too annoying but this article is gonna be placed under [[:Category:Pages using infobox ancient site with unknown parameters]] and there is a decent chance these unknown parameters are ones I want added to the main template like burial chamber structure and burial goods. Please do not use any bots that just remove the unknown parameters without looking at them. This was added through [[Special:MassEditRegex]] to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft|12=draft}} |name = Nishiyama Kofun |image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px|]] |caption = Mound overview (left: anterior, right back: posterior) |location = {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県|12=draft|12=draft}} {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市|12=draft|12=draft}} Somanouchi Town |coordinates = {{coord|34|35|33|N|135|50|36|E|region:JP-29_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Nishiyama Kofun}} |type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft|12=draft}} |area = Total length: 183m, height: 13m |burial = {{ill|Pit-style stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft|12=draft}} |built = Early Kofun period |Interred = (Theory) A member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏|12=draft|12=draft}} |burial goods = Mirror fragments, stone arrowheads, iron sword fragments, magatama, and haniwa |alternate_name = National Historic Site (Historic Site1 April 8, 1927) |map = Japan Nara |type = Zenpō-kōhō-fun-W }} '''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} located in Somanouchi Town, {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県|12=draft|12=draft}}, Japan. It is Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site and is part of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|12=draft|12=draft}}. == Overview == Constructed during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft|12=draft}} (4th century), Nishiyama Kofun is the oldest of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|12=draft|12=draft}}. The Kofun features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft|12=draft}} at its base to a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft|12=draft}} at its upper levels. The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day {{ill|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市|12=draft|12=draft}}), was targeted. == area and burial == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * '''Rear mound (posterior):''' 94m width, 16m height * '''Anterior mound:''' 72m width, 13m height The lower tier types a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft|12=draft}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft|12=draft}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in. Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design. == burial goods == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments''' * '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones''' * '''Surface burial goods:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure. == Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館|12=draft|12=draft}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School. == Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927{{国cultural property等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the Historic Site1 area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|12=draft|12=draft}} == External Links == * {{国cultural property等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}} * [http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html Tenri City Kofun Guide] {{otheruses|Nishiyama Kofun in Tenri, Nara|Nishiyama Kofun in Ota, Gunma|Nishiyama Kofun (Ota)}} {{Infobox Kofun | name = Nishiyama Kofun | native_name = 西山古墳 | image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px]]
Mound overview (left: front section, back right: rear section) | location = {{ill|Tenri, Nara|ja|天理市|12=draft|12=draft}}, Nara Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = 34.5925 | coordinates = 135.8433 | region = Japan | type = {{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft|12=draft}} (rectangular keyhole-shaped tumulus) | length = 183m, Height: 13m | burial = {{ill|Tateana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft|12=draft}} (pit-style stone chamber) | built = Early Kofun period (4th century) | person = Possibly a member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏|12=draft|12=draft}} | burial goods = Mirrors, stone arrowheads, iron swords and blades, magatama beads, haniwa clay figures | Historic Site1 = National Historic Site of Japan (Historic Site1 April 8, 1927) }} '''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a '''large [[Zenpō-kōhō-fun|rectangular keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後方墳, zenpō-kōhō-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Tenri, Nara|ja|天理市|12=draft|12=draft}}, Nara Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''{{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|12=draft|12=draft}}''' and is the '''largest kofun of its type in Japan'''. In '''1927 (Showa 2)''', it was '''Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site''' of Japan.{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/1958|title=Nishiyama Kofun - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}} It is also known by the '''alternate name "Nagariyama" (勾山, Magariyama).''' == Overview == The kofun was '''constructed during the early [[Kofun period]] (4th century)''' and is one of the '''earliest tumuli''' in the '''{{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|12=draft|12=draft}}'''. The mound originally had a '''[[Vertical pit stone chamber|pit-style stone chamber]] (竪穴式石室, tateana-shiki sekishitsu)''', but it was likely '''looted in antiquity'''.Izumimori, Ko. *Ancient Tombs of Yamato I* (『大和の古墳I』), Jinbun Shoin, 2003. During '''World War II''', the Japanese Imperial Army '''stationed an anti-aircraft gun battery''' at the site. At that time, stones from the '''burial chamber (originally quarried in Kashiwara, Osaka)''' were reportedly '''removed''' and repurposed.On-site intypeation board by the Tenri City Board of Education. == burial & area == [[File:080515 Nishiyama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|Aerial view of Nishiyama Kofun.
{{National Aerial Photography}}.
[[:File:Tenri-nishiyama_stereo.jpg|Stereo image here]]]] The tumulus is a '''three-tiered, [[Zenpō-kōhō-fun|rectangular keyhole-shaped mound]] (前方後方墳, [[zenpō-kōhō-fun]])''' with the front section '''oriented westward'''. Its area are: * '''Total length''': 183 meters * '''Rear section''' (square): 94m wide × 16m high * '''Front section''': 72m wide The '''lower level''' is '''rectangular''', while the '''middle and upper levels''' are '''rounder''', creating a hybrid '''keyhole-shaped mound (前方後円形, zenpō-kōenkei)'''. The '''central burial chamber''' is estimated to be a '''[[Vertical pit stone chamber|pit-style stone chamber]]''' based on '''historical records'''. The mound is positioned '''along three natural ridges''', with the '''central ridge typeing the main mound''', while the '''north and south ridges serve as outer embankments'''. A '''moat once surrounded the mound''', but it has since been '''filled in'''. This kofun is '''the largest of its kind in Japan'''. The '''unique construction''', with a '''rectangular lower tier supporting a rounder upper structure''', is believed to be '''original to its design'''. == burial goods & burial Goods == Excavations have uncovered: * '''Copper mirrors (fragments)''' * '''Green jasper arrowheads''' * '''Magatama beads''' * '''Iron swords and blades''' * '''Wheel-shaped stone object (碧玉製車輪石, hekigyoku-sei sharinseki)''' * '''Haniwa clay figures''', including: ** '''[[Cylindrical Haniwa|Cylindrical haniwa]] (円筒埴輪)''' ** '''Fin-shaped haniwa (鰭付円筒埴輪)''' ** '''[[Figural Haniwa|House-shaped haniwa]] (家形埴輪)''' == Current Condition == The '''mound is well preserved''', and due to '''lack of tree cover''', the '''three-tiered structure is clearly visible'''. == Access == * '''20-minute walk from [[Tenri Station]]''' - Located '''500 meters south''' of the '''Tenri University Reference Museum''' * '''Just north''' of '''Tenri Middle School''' == designation1 == === '''National Historic Site of Japan''' === * '''Original Historic Site (1927)''': Nishiyama Kofun was Historic Site1 a '''National Historic Site'''. * '''Expansion (2018)''': The Historic Site was '''expanded''' to include '''Nishinorikura Kofun (西乗鞍古墳)''', renaming the site as the '''Somanochi Kofun Group (杣之内古墳群)'''.Ministry of Education, Science and Culture Announcement No. 19 (February 13, 2018). == References == {{Reflist}} == Additional Resources == * '''On-site intypeation board''' (Tenri City Board of Education) * '''Tenri City Website: Kofun Guide''' == Related Articles == * {{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|12=draft|12=draft}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Nishiyama Kofun}} * [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/1958 '''Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan): Nishiyama Kofun'''] * [http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html '''Tenri City Official Kofun Guide'''] {{draft categories| }} {{citation needed|Nishiyama Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design. == burial goods == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments''' * '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones''' * '''Surface burial goods:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure. == Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館|12=draft|12=draft}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School. == Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927{{国cultural property等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the Historic Site1 area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|12=draft|12=draft}} == External Links == * {{国cultural property等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}} * [http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html Tenri City Kofun Guide] {{otheruses|Nishiyama Kofun in Tenri, Nara|Nishiyama Kofun in Ota, Gunma|Nishiyama Kofun (Ota)}} {{Infobox Kofun | name = Nishiyama Kofun | native_name = 西山古墳 | image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px]]
Mound overview (left: front section, back right: rear section) | location = {{ill|Tenri, Nara|ja|天理市|12=draft|12=draft}}, Nara Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = 34.5925 | coordinates = 135.8433 | region = Japan | type = {{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft|12=draft}} (rectangular keyhole-shaped tumulus) | length = 183m, Height: 13m | burial = {{ill|Tateana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft|12=draft}} (pit-style stone chamber) | built = Early Kofun period (4th century) | person = Possibly a member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏|12=draft|12=draft}} | burial goods = Mirrors, stone arrowheads, iron swords and blades, magatama beads, haniwa clay figures | Historic Site1 = National Historic Site of Japan (Historic Site1 April 8, 1927) }} '''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a '''large [[Zenpō-kōhō-fun|rectangular keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後方墳, zenpō-kōhō-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Tenri, Nara|ja|天理市|12=draft|12=draft}}, Nara Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''{{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|12=draft|12=draft}}''' and is the '''largest kofun of its type in Japan'''. In '''1927 (Showa 2)''', it was '''Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site''' of Japan.{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/1958|title=Nishiyama Kofun - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}} It is also known by the '''alternate name "Nagariyama" (勾山, Magariyama).''' == Overview == The kofun was '''constructed during the early [[Kofun period]] (4th century)''' and is one of the '''earliest tumuli''' in the '''{{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|12=draft|12=draft}}'''. The mound originally had a '''[[Vertical pit stone chamber|pit-style stone chamber]] (竪穴式石室, tateana-shiki sekishitsu)''', but it was likely '''looted in antiquity'''.Izumimori, Ko. *Ancient Tombs of Yamato I* (『大和の古墳I』), Jinbun Shoin, 2003. During '''World War II''', the Japanese Imperial Army '''stationed an anti-aircraft gun battery''' at the site. At that time, stones from the '''burial chamber (originally quarried in Kashiwara, Osaka)''' were reportedly '''removed''' and repurposed.On-site intypeation board by the Tenri City Board of Education. == burial & area == [[File:080515 Nishiyama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|Aerial view of Nishiyama Kofun.
{{National Aerial Photography}}.
[[:File:Tenri-nishiyama_stereo.jpg|Stereo image here]]]] The tumulus is a '''three-tiered, [[Zenpō-kōhō-fun|rectangular keyhole-shaped mound]] (前方後方墳, [[zenpō-kōhō-fun]])''' with the front section '''oriented westward'''. Its area are: * '''Total length''': 183 meters * '''Rear section''' (square): 94m wide × 16m high * '''Front section''': 72m wide The '''lower level''' is '''rectangular''', while the '''middle and upper levels''' are '''rounder''', creating a hybrid '''keyhole-shaped mound (前方後円形, zenpō-kōenkei)'''. The '''central burial chamber''' is estimated to be a '''[[Vertical pit stone chamber|pit-style stone chamber]]''' based on '''historical records'''. The mound is positioned '''along three natural ridges''', with the '''central ridge typeing the main mound''', while the '''north and south ridges serve as outer embankments'''. A '''moat once surrounded the mound''', but it has since been '''filled in'''. This kofun is '''the largest of its kind in Japan'''. The '''unique construction''', with a '''rectangular lower tier supporting a rounder upper structure''', is believed to be '''original to its design'''. == burial goods & burial Goods == Excavations have uncovered: * '''Copper mirrors (fragments)''' * '''Green jasper arrowheads''' * '''Magatama beads''' * '''Iron swords and blades''' * '''Wheel-shaped stone object (碧玉製車輪石, hekigyoku-sei sharinseki)''' * '''Haniwa clay figures''', including: ** '''[[Cylindrical Haniwa|Cylindrical haniwa]] (円筒埴輪)''' ** '''Fin-shaped haniwa (鰭付円筒埴輪)''' ** '''[[Figural Haniwa|House-shaped haniwa]] (家形埴輪)''' == Current Condition == The '''mound is well preserved''', and due to '''lack of tree cover''', the '''three-tiered structure is clearly visible'''. == Access == * '''20-minute walk from The Kofun features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft|12=draft}} at its base to a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft|12=draft}} at its upper levels. The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. So a lot of these pages might not be marked on our wiki as having unknown parameters. But specifically keeping this comment here in case of import, these parameters should be added to [[Template:infobox ancient site]] rather than deleted from this draft or article[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:02, 28 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=I hope this is not too annoying but this article is gonna be placed under [[Category:Pages using infobox ancient site with unknown parameters]] and there is a decent chance these unknown parameters are ones I want added to the main template like burial chamber structure and burial goods. Please do not use any bots that just remove the unknown parameters without looking at them. This was added through [[Special:MassEditRegex]] to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun}} |name = Nishiyama Kofun |image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px|]] |caption = Mound overview (left: anterior, right back: posterior) |location = {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}} {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}} Somanouchi Town |coordinates = {{coord|34|35|33|N|135|50|36|E|region:JP-29_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Nishiyama Kofun}} |type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} |area = Total length: 183m, height: 13m |burial = {{ill|Pit-style stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=竪穴式石室|4=zh|5=豎穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber}} |built = Early Kofun period |Interred = (Theory) A member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏}} |burial goods = Mirror fragments, stone arrowheads, iron sword fragments, magatama, and haniwa |alternate_name = National Historic Site (Historic Site1 April 8, 1927) |map = Japan Nara |type = Zenpō-kōhō-fun-W }} '''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in Somanouchi Town, {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}, Japan. It is Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site and is part of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster}}. == Overview == Constructed during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} (4th century), Nishiyama Kofun is the oldest of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster}}. The Kofun features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} at its base to a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun}} at its upper levels. The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day {{ill|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市}}), was targeted. == area and burial == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * '''Rear mound (posterior):''' 94m width, 16m height * '''Anterior mound:''' 72m width, 13m height The lower tier types a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in. Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design. == burial goods == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments''' * '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones''' * '''Surface burial goods:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure. == Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School. == Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927{{国cultural property等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the Historic Site1 area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster}} == External Links == * {{国cultural property等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}} * [http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html Tenri City Kofun Guide] {{otheruses|Nishiyama Kofun in Tenri, Nara|Nishiyama Kofun in Ota, Gunma|Nishiyama Kofun (Ota)}} {{Infobox Kofun | name = Nishiyama Kofun | native_name = 西山古墳 | image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px]]
Mound overview (left: front section, back right: rear section) | location = {{ill|Tenri, Nara|ja|天理市}}, Nara Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = 34.5925 | coordinates = 135.8433 | region = Japan | type = {{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} (rectangular keyhole-shaped tumulus) | length = 183m, Height: 13m | burial = {{ill|Tateana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=竪穴式石室|4=zh|5=豎穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber}} (pit-style stone chamber) | built = Early Kofun period (4th century) | person = Possibly a member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏}} | burial goods = Mirrors, stone arrowheads, iron swords and blades, magatama beads, haniwa clay figures | Historic Site1 = National Historic Site of Japan (Historic Site1 April 8, 1927) }} '''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a '''large [[Zenpō-kōhō-fun|rectangular keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後方墳, zenpō-kōhō-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Tenri, Nara|ja|天理市}}, Nara Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''{{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster}}''' and is the '''largest kofun of its type in Japan'''. In '''1927 (Showa 2)''', it was '''Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site''' of Japan.{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/1958|title=Nishiyama Kofun - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}} It is also known by the '''alternate name "Nagariyama" (勾山, Magariyama).''' == Overview == The kofun was '''constructed during the early [[Kofun period]] (4th century)''' and is one of the '''earliest tumuli''' in the '''{{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster}}'''. The mound originally had a '''[[Vertical pit stone chamber|pit-style stone chamber]] (竪穴式石室, tateana-shiki sekishitsu)''', but it was likely '''looted in antiquity'''.Izumimori, Ko. *Ancient Tombs of Yamato I* (『大和の古墳I』), Jinbun Shoin, 2003. During '''World War II''', the Japanese Imperial Army '''stationed an anti-aircraft gun battery''' at the site. At that time, stones from the '''burial chamber (originally quarried in Kashiwara, Osaka)''' were reportedly '''removed''' and repurposed.On-site intypeation board by the Tenri City Board of Education. == burial & area == [[File:080515 Nishiyama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|Aerial view of Nishiyama Kofun.
{{National Aerial Photography}}.
[[:File:Tenri-nishiyama_stereo.jpg|Stereo image here]]]] The tumulus is a '''three-tiered, [[Zenpō-kōhō-fun|rectangular keyhole-shaped mound]] (前方後方墳, [[zenpō-kōhō-fun]])''' with the front section '''oriented westward'''. Its area are: * '''Total length''': 183 meters * '''Rear section''' (square): 94m wide × 16m high * '''Front section''': 72m wide The '''lower level''' is '''rectangular''', while the '''middle and upper levels''' are '''rounder''', creating a hybrid '''keyhole-shaped mound (前方後円形, zenpō-kōenkei)'''. The '''central burial chamber''' is estimated to be a '''[[Vertical pit stone chamber|pit-style stone chamber]]''' based on '''historical records'''. The mound is positioned '''along three natural ridges''', with the '''central ridge typeing the main mound''', while the '''north and south ridges serve as outer embankments'''. A '''moat once surrounded the mound''', but it has since been '''filled in'''. This kofun is '''the largest of its kind in Japan'''. The '''unique construction''', with a '''rectangular lower tier supporting a rounder upper structure''', is believed to be '''original to its design'''. == burial goods & burial Goods == Excavations have uncovered: * '''Copper mirrors (fragments)''' * '''Green jasper arrowheads''' * '''Magatama beads''' * '''Iron swords and blades''' * '''Wheel-shaped stone object (碧玉製車輪石, hekigyoku-sei sharinseki)''' * '''Haniwa clay figures''', including: ** '''[[Cylindrical Haniwa|Cylindrical haniwa]] (円筒埴輪)''' ** '''Fin-shaped haniwa (鰭付円筒埴輪)''' ** '''[[Figural Haniwa|House-shaped haniwa]] (家形埴輪)''' == Current Condition == The '''mound is well preserved''', and due to '''lack of tree cover''', the '''three-tiered structure is clearly visible'''. == Access == * '''20-minute walk from [[Tenri Station]]''' - Located '''500 meters south''' of the '''Tenri University Reference Museum''' * '''Just north''' of '''Tenri Middle School''' == designation1 == === '''National Historic Site of Japan''' === * '''Original Historic Site (1927)''': Nishiyama Kofun was Historic Site1 a '''National Historic Site'''. * '''Expansion (2018)''': The Historic Site was '''expanded''' to include '''Nishinorikura Kofun (西乗鞍古墳)''', renaming the site as the '''Somanochi Kofun Group (杣之内古墳群)'''.Ministry of Education, Science and Culture Announcement No. 19 (February 13, 2018). == References == Nishiyama Kofun'''] * [http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html '''Tenri City Official Kofun Guide'''] {{draft categories| }} {{citation needed|Nishiyama Kofun}} {{Kofun {{afc comment|1=See [[Category:Pages using infobox ancient site with unknown parameters]] as this is a member[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 22:44, 22 April 2025 (UTC)}} [[Category:Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]][[Category:Secondary Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]][[Category:Secondary Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]][[Category:Secondary Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] {{afc comment|1=trimming these off. the parameter works as "burial" so no need to use "burial"[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 03:35, 28 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=added parameters Interred_individual and Mausoleum is planned to be added but I messed up in template editing[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:40, 28 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=now we have a 'burial' and 'burial goods' parameter. So a lot of these pages might not be marked on our wiki as having unknown parameters. But specifically keeping this comment here in case of import, these parameters should be added to [[Template:infobox ancient site]] rather than deleted from this draft or article[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:02, 28 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=I hope this is not too annoying but this article is gonna be placed under [[Category:Pages using infobox ancient site with unknown parameters]] and there is a decent chance these unknown parameters are ones I want added to the main template like burial chamber structure and burial goods. Please do not use any bots that just remove the unknown parameters without looking at them. This was added through [[Special:MassEditRegex]] to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun}} |name = Nishiyama Kofun |image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px|]] |caption = Mound overview (left: anterior, right back: posterior) |location = {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}} {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}} Somanouchi Town |coordinates = {{coord|34|35|33|N|135|50|36|E|region:JP-29_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Nishiyama Kofun}} |type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} |area = Total length: 183m, height: 13m |burial = {{ill|Pit-style stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=竪穴式石室|4=zh|5=豎穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber}} |built = Early Kofun period |Interred = (Theory) A member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏}} |burial goods = Mirror fragments, stone arrowheads, iron sword fragments, magatama, and haniwa |alternate_name = National Historic Site (Historic Site1 April 8, 1927) |map = Japan Nara |type = Zenpō-kōhō-fun-W }} '''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in Somanouchi Town, {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}, Japan. It is Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site and is part of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster}}. == Overview == Constructed during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} (4th century), Nishiyama Kofun is the oldest of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster}}. The Kofun features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} at its base to a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun}} at its upper levels. The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day {{ill|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市}}), was targeted. == area and burial == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * '''Rear mound (posterior):''' 94m width, 16m height * '''Anterior mound:''' 72m width, 13m height The lower tier types a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in. Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design. == burial goods == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments''' * '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones''' * '''Surface burial goods:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure. == Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School. == Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927{{国cultural property等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the Historic Site1 area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster}} == External Links == * {{国cultural property等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}} * [http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html Tenri City Kofun Guide] {{otheruses|Nishiyama Kofun in Tenri, Nara|Nishiyama Kofun in Ota, Gunma|Nishiyama Kofun (Ota)}} {{Infobox Kofun | name = Nishiyama Kofun | native_name = 西山古墳 | image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px]]
Mound overview (left: front section, back right: rear section) | location = {{ill|Tenri, Nara|ja|天理市}}, Nara Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = 34.5925 | coordinates = 135.8433 | region = Japan | type = {{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} (rectangular keyhole-shaped tumulus) | length = 183m, Height: 13m | burial = {{ill|Tateana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=竪穴式石室|4=zh|5=豎穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber}} (pit-style stone chamber) | built = Early Kofun period (4th century) | person = Possibly a member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏}} | burial goods = Mirrors, stone arrowheads, iron swords and blades, magatama beads, haniwa clay figures | Historic Site1 = National Historic Site of Japan (Historic Site1 April 8, 1927) }} '''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a '''large [[Zenpō-kōhō-fun|rectangular keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後方墳, zenpō-kōhō-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Tenri, Nara|ja|天理市}}, Nara Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''{{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster}}''' and is the '''largest kofun of its type in Japan'''. In '''1927 (Showa 2)''', it was '''Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site''' of Japan.{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/1958|title=Nishiyama Kofun - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}} It is also known by the '''alternate name "Nagariyama" (勾山, Magariyama).''' == Overview == The kofun was '''constructed during the early [[Kofun period]] (4th century)''' and is one of the '''earliest tumuli''' in the '''{{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster}}'''. The mound originally had a '''[[Vertical pit stone chamber|pit-style stone chamber]] (竪穴式石室, tateana-shiki sekishitsu)''', but it was likely '''looted in antiquity'''.Izumimori, Ko. *Ancient Tombs of Yamato I* (『大和の古墳I』), Jinbun Shoin, 2003. During '''World War II''', the Japanese Imperial Army '''stationed an anti-aircraft gun battery''' at the site. At that time, stones from the '''burial chamber (originally quarried in Kashiwara, Osaka)''' were reportedly '''removed''' and repurposed.On-site intypeation board by the Tenri City Board of Education. == burial & area == [[File:080515 Nishiyama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|Aerial view of Nishiyama Kofun.
{{National Aerial Photography}}.
[[:File:Tenri-nishiyama_stereo.jpg|Stereo image here]]]] The tumulus is a '''three-tiered, [[Zenpō-kōhō-fun|rectangular keyhole-shaped mound]] (前方後方墳, [[zenpō-kōhō-fun]])''' with the front section '''oriented westward'''. Its area are: * '''Total length''': 183 meters * '''Rear section''' (square): 94m wide × 16m high * '''Front section''': 72m wide The '''lower level''' is '''rectangular''', while the '''middle and upper levels''' are '''rounder''', creating a hybrid '''keyhole-shaped mound (前方後円形, zenpō-kōenkei)'''. The '''central burial chamber''' is estimated to be a '''[[Vertical pit stone chamber|pit-style stone chamber]]''' based on '''historical records'''. The mound is positioned '''along three natural ridges''', with the '''central ridge typeing the main mound''', while the '''north and south ridges serve as outer embankments'''. A '''moat once surrounded the mound''', but it has since been '''filled in'''. This kofun is '''the largest of its kind in Japan'''. The '''unique construction''', with a '''rectangular lower tier supporting a rounder upper structure''', is believed to be '''original to its design'''. == burial goods & burial Goods == Excavations have uncovered: * '''Copper mirrors (fragments)''' * '''Green jasper arrowheads''' * '''Magatama beads''' * '''Iron swords and blades''' * '''Wheel-shaped stone object (碧玉製車輪石, hekigyoku-sei sharinseki)''' * '''Haniwa clay figures''', including: ** '''[[Cylindrical Haniwa|Cylindrical haniwa]] (円筒埴輪)''' ** '''Fin-shaped haniwa (鰭付円筒埴輪)''' ** '''[[Figural Haniwa|House-shaped haniwa]] (家形埴輪)''' == Current Condition == The '''mound is well preserved''', and due to '''lack of tree cover''', the '''three-tiered structure is clearly visible'''. == Access == * '''20-minute walk from [[Tenri Station]]''' - Located '''500 meters south''' of the '''Tenri University Reference Museum''' * '''Just north''' of '''Tenri Middle School''' == designation1 == === '''National Historic Site of Japan''' === * '''Original Historic Site (1927)''': Nishiyama Kofun was Historic Site1 a '''National Historic Site'''. * '''Expansion (2018)''': The Historic Site was '''expanded''' to include '''Nishinorikura Kofun (西乗鞍古墳)''', renaming the site as the '''Somanochi Kofun Group (杣之内古墳群)'''.Ministry of Education, Science and Culture Announcement No. 19 (February 13, 2018). == References == Nishiyama Kofun'''] * [http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html '''Tenri City Official Kofun Guide'''] {{draft categories| }} {{citation needed|Nishiyama Kofun}} {{Kofun revision.text:
{{otheruses|奈良県天理市の古墳|群馬県太田市の古墳|西山古墳 (太田市)}} {{日本の古墳 |名称=西山古墳 |画像=[[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px|]]
墳丘全景（左に前方部、右奥に後方部） |所在地=[[奈良県]][[天理市]]杣之内町 |緯度度 = 34|緯度分 = 35|緯度秒 = 33 |経度度 =135|経度分 = 50|経度秒 = 36 |ISO = JP-29 |形状=[[前方後方墳]] |規模=全長183m 高さ13m |埋葬施設=[[竪穴式石室]] |築造年代=古墳時代前期 |被葬者=（一説）[[物部氏]]一族 |出土品=鏡・石鏃・鉄製刀剣類の破片、管玉、埴輪ほか |史跡指定=国の史跡（1927年4月8日指定） |特記事項= |地図 = Japan Nara |アイコン = 前方後方墳-西 }} '''西山古墳'''（にしやまこふん）は、[[奈良県]][[天理市]]杣之内（そまのうち）町の[[天理高等学校]]の敷地内にある[[古墳]]で、1927年（昭和2年）国の[[史跡]]に指定{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}されている。別称はナガリヤマ（勾山[まがりやま]）。 == 概要 == 築造時期は[[古墳時代]]前期（4世紀）と見られており、同古墳が属する[[杣之内古墳群]]の中でも最も古い時期に造られた古墳である。 後方部中心には[[竪穴式石室]]があるが、すでに盗掘を受けているとみられている。 第2次世界大戦中には旧日本軍により対空砲の陣地がおかれ、このさいに竪穴式石室の石材（[[柏原市]]芝山産）が掘り出されたとされる天理教育委員会による現地説明板による。 == 規模・形状 == [[ファイル:080515 Nishiyama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|西山古墳の空中写真。
{{国土航空写真}}
[[:File:Tenri-nishiyama_stereo.jpg|ステレオ写真はこちら]]]] 墳丘は前方部を西に向けた3段構築の[[前方後方墳]]で、全長183メートル、後円部の幅94メートル 高さ16メートル、前方部の幅72メートル。 下段が前方後方形で、中段から上は前方後円形となる特殊な墳形をもつ。下段の後方部は一辺90メートルの正方形で、これに同じ長さの前方部が付いている。中段は前方後円型をしていて、後円丘径72メートル、前方丘全長90メートル。墳頂部は径30メートルが平坦で、前方部方向に7メートル下がって細長い前方部が続き、前方部先端はくびれ部より2メートル高く主軸に直交する横長形となっている。後方部高さは南側で15メートルで、前方部の高さも南側で10メートル。 後方部頂上が盗掘されている。その時の記録から[[竪穴式石室]]であったと推定されている。 緩やかな傾斜地に立地し、三本の尾根の中央部を墳丘に、北と南の尾根を外堤として、自然地形を有効に利用しているため濠幅は一定しないが、全長200メートル以上の双方中方墳とも考えられる。濠は現在埋め立てられているが、階段状の方形の濠階段状の濠は「伝崇神天皇陵」古墳でもみられる。が巡らされていたと考えられる。現状では前方後方形の墳丘と見られるが、地形改変が進んでいることなどを考慮して、双方中方墳の可能性もある泉森皎「西山古墳」文化庁文化財保護部史跡研究会監修『図説　日本の史跡　第3巻　原始3』同朋舎出版　1991年　36ページ。 これは日本にある前方後方墳の中でもっとも規模の大きいものである。墳丘は1段目のみが前方後方墳の形で、その上に[[前方後円墳]]が乗るというきわめて特異な形をしており、当初からこの形であったことは間違いないとみられている『大和の古墳I』泉森皎編 人文書院（2003年）。 == 副葬品・出土品 == 後方部からは、銅鏡片、碧玉製鏃、管玉、鉄剣・鉄刀片が出土している。前方部南側濠内から碧玉製車輪石1が検出されている。傾斜斜面には葺き石が、埴輪片がみられ、円筒埴輪、鰭付（ひれつき）円筒埴輪、家形埴輪が見つかっている。 == 現状 == 墳丘の保存状態は良く、樹木が生えていないため段築をはっきりと観察することができる。 == アクセス == 天理駅より徒歩約20分。[[天理大学附属天理参考館]]の南約500メートル、[[天理中学校]]すぐ北。 == 文化財 == === 国の史跡 === * 西山古墳（史跡「杣之内古墳群」のうち） *: 1927年（昭和2年）4月8日指定。 *: 2018年（平成30年）2月13日、既指定の史跡「西山古墳」に西乗鞍古墳を追加指定、「杣之内古墳群」に名称変更平成30年2月13日文部科学省告示第19号。。 == 脚注 == {{reflist}} == 参考資料 == * 天理市教育委員会設置現地説明板 * 天理市ホームページ 古墳ガイド == 関連項目 == * [[杣之内古墳群]] == 外部リンク == {{Commonscat|Nishiyama Kofun}} * {{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}} *[http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html 天理市ホームページ|古墳ガイド] {{DEFAULTSORT:にしやまこふん}} [[Category:杣之内古墳群]] [[Category:奈良県の古墳]] [[Category:天理市の歴史]] [[Category:奈良県にある国指定の史跡]] [[Category:前方後方墳]]

{{otheruses|奈良県天理市の古墳|群馬県太田市の古墳|西山古墳 (太田市)}} {{日本の古墳 |名称=西山古墳 |画像=[[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px|]]
墳丘全景（左に前方部、右奥に後方部） |所在地=[[奈良県]][[天理市]]杣之内町 |緯度度 = 34|緯度分 = 35|緯度秒 = 33 |経度度 =135|経度分 = 50|経度秒 = 36 |ISO = JP-29 |形状=[[前方後方墳]] |規模=全長183m 高さ13m |埋葬施設=[[竪穴式石室]] |築造年代=古墳時代前期 |被葬者=（一説）[[物部氏]]一族 |出土品=鏡・石鏃・鉄製刀剣類の破片、管玉、埴輪ほか |史跡指定=国の史跡（1927年4月8日指定） |特記事項= |地図 = Japan Nara |アイコン = 前方後方墳-西 }} '''西山古墳'''（にしやまこふん）は、[[奈良県]][[天理市]]杣之内（そまのうち）町の[[天理高等学校]]の敷地内にある[[古墳]]で、1927年（昭和2年）国の[[史跡]]に指定{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}されている。別称はナガリヤマ（勾山[まがりやま]）。 == 概要 == 築造時期は[[古墳時代]]前期（4世紀）と見られており、同古墳が属する[[杣之内古墳群]]の中でも最も古い時期に造られた古墳である。 後方部中心には[[竪穴式石室]]があるが、すでに盗掘を受けているとみられている。 第2次世界大戦中には旧日本軍により対空砲の陣地がおかれ、このさいに竪穴式石室の石材（[[柏原市]]芝山産）が掘り出されたとされる天理教育委員会による現地説明板による。 == 規模・形状 == [[ファイル:080515 Nishiyama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|西山古墳の空中写真。
{{国土航空写真}}
[[:File:Tenri-nishiyama_stereo.jpg|ステレオ写真はこちら]]]] 墳丘は前方部を西に向けた3段構築の[[前方後方墳]]で、全長183メートル、後円部の幅94メートル 高さ16メートル、前方部の幅72メートル。 下段が前方後方形で、中段から上は前方後円形となる特殊な墳形をもつ。下段の後方部は一辺90メートルの正方形で、これに同じ長さの前方部が付いている。中段は前方後円型をしていて、後円丘径72メートル、前方丘全長90メートル。墳頂部は径30メートルが平坦で、前方部方向に7メートル下がって細長い前方部が続き、前方部先端はくびれ部より2メートル高く主軸に直交する横長形となっている。後方部高さは南側で15メートルで、前方部の高さも南側で10メートル。 後方部頂上が盗掘されている。その時の記録から[[竪穴式石室]]であったと推定されている。 緩やかな傾斜地に立地し、三本の尾根の中央部を墳丘に、北と南の尾根を外堤として、自然地形を有効に利用しているため濠幅は一定しないが、全長200メートル以上の双方中方墳とも考えられる。濠は現在埋め立てられているが、階段状の方形の濠階段状の濠は「伝崇神天皇陵」古墳でもみられる。が巡らされていたと考えられる。現状では前方後方形の墳丘と見られるが、地形改変が進んでいることなどを考慮して、双方中方墳の可能性もある泉森皎「西山古墳」文化庁文化財保護部史跡研究会監修『図説　日本の史跡　第3巻　原始3』同朋舎出版　1991年　36ページ。 これは日本にある前方後方墳の中でもっとも規模の大きいものである。墳丘は1段目のみが前方後方墳の形で、その上に[[前方後円墳]]が乗るというきわめて特異な形をしており、当初からこの形であったことは間違いないとみられている『大和の古墳I』泉森皎編 人文書院（2003年）。 == 副葬品・出土品 == 後方部からは、銅鏡片、碧玉製鏃、管玉、鉄剣・鉄刀片が出土している。前方部南側濠内から碧玉製車輪石1が検出されている。傾斜斜面には葺き石が、埴輪片がみられ、円筒埴輪、鰭付（ひれつき）円筒埴輪、家形埴輪が見つかっている。 == 現状 == 墳丘の保存状態は良く、樹木が生えていないため段築をはっきりと観察することができる。 == アクセス == 天理駅より徒歩約20分。[[天理大学附属天理参考館]]の南約500メートル、[[天理中学校]]すぐ北。 == 文化財 == === 国の史跡 === * 西山古墳（史跡「杣之内古墳群」のうち） *: 1927年（昭和2年）4月8日指定。 *: 2018年（平成30年）2月13日、既指定の史跡「西山古墳」に西乗鞍古墳を追加指定、「杣之内古墳群」に名称変更平成30年2月13日文部科学省告示第19号。。 == 脚注 == {{reflist}} == 参考資料 == * 天理市教育委員会設置現地説明板 * 天理市ホームページ 古墳ガイド == 関連項目 == * [[杣之内古墳群]] == 外部リンク == {{Commonscat|Nishiyama Kofun}} * {{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}} *[http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html 天理市ホームページ|古墳ガイド] {{DEFAULTSORT:にしやまこふん}} [[Category:杣之内古墳群]] [[Category:奈良県の古墳]] [[Category:天理市の歴史]] [[Category:奈良県にある国指定の史跡]] [[Category:前方後方墳]]

So a lot of these pages might not be marked on our wiki as having unknown parameters. But specifically keeping this comment here in case of import, these parameters should be added to [[Template:infobox ancient site]] rather than deleted from this draft or article[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:02, 28 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=I hope this is not too annoying but this article is gonna be placed under [[Category:Pages using infobox ancient site with unknown parameters]] and there is a decent chance these unknown parameters are ones I want added to the main template like burial chamber structure and burial goods. Please do not use any bots that just remove the unknown parameters without looking at them. This was added through [[Special:MassEditRegex]] to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun}} |name = Nishiyama Kofun |image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px|]] |caption = Mound overview (left: anterior, right back: posterior) |location = {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}} {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}} Somanouchi Town |coordinates = {{coord|34|35|33|N|135|50|36|E|region:JP-29_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Nishiyama Kofun}} |type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} |area = Total length: 183m, height: 13m |burial = {{ill|Pit-style stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=竪穴式石室|4=zh|5=豎穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber}} |built = Early Kofun period |Interred = (Theory) A member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏}} |burial goods = Mirror fragments, stone arrowheads, iron sword fragments, magatama, and haniwa |alternate_name = National Historic Site (Historic Site1 April 8, 1927) |map = Japan Nara |type = Zenpō-kōhō-fun-W }} '''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in Somanouchi Town, {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}, Japan. It is Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site and is part of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster}}. == Overview == Constructed during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} (4th century), Nishiyama Kofun is the oldest of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster}}. The Kofun features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} at its base to a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun}} at its upper levels. The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day {{ill|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市}}), was targeted. == area and burial == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * '''Rear mound (posterior):''' 94m width, 16m height * '''Anterior mound:''' 72m width, 13m height The lower tier types a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in. Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design. == burial goods == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments''' * '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones''' * '''Surface burial goods:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure. == Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School. == Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927{{国cultural property等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the Historic Site1 area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster}} == External Links == * {{国cultural property等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}} * [http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html Tenri City Kofun Guide] {{otheruses|Nishiyama Kofun in Tenri, Nara|Nishiyama Kofun in Ota, Gunma|Nishiyama Kofun (Ota)}} {{Infobox Kofun | name = Nishiyama Kofun | native_name = 西山古墳 | image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px]]
Mound overview (left: front section, back right: rear section) | location = {{ill|Tenri, Nara|ja|天理市}}, Nara Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = 34.5925 | coordinates = 135.8433 | region = Japan | type = {{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} (rectangular keyhole-shaped tumulus) | length = 183m, Height: 13m | burial = {{ill|Tateana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=竪穴式石室|4=zh|5=豎穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber}} (pit-style stone chamber) | built = Early Kofun period (4th century) | person = Possibly a member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏}} | burial goods = Mirrors, stone arrowheads, iron swords and blades, magatama beads, haniwa clay figures | Historic Site1 = National Historic Site of Japan (Historic Site1 April 8, 1927) }} '''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a '''large [[Zenpō-kōhō-fun|rectangular keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後方墳, zenpō-kōhō-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Tenri, Nara|ja|天理市}}, Nara Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''{{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster}}''' and is the '''largest kofun of its type in Japan'''. In '''1927 (Showa 2)''', it was '''Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site''' of Japan.{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/1958|title=Nishiyama Kofun - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}} It is also known by the '''alternate name "Nagariyama" (勾山, Magariyama).''' == Overview == The kofun was '''constructed during the early [[Kofun period]] (4th century)''' and is one of the '''earliest tumuli''' in the '''{{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster}}'''. The mound originally had a '''[[Vertical pit stone chamber|pit-style stone chamber]] (竪穴式石室, tateana-shiki sekishitsu)''', but it was likely '''looted in antiquity'''.Izumimori, Ko. *Ancient Tombs of Yamato I* (『大和の古墳I』), Jinbun Shoin, 2003. During '''World War II''', the Japanese Imperial Army '''stationed an anti-aircraft gun battery''' at the site. At that time, stones from the '''burial chamber (originally quarried in Kashiwara, Osaka)''' were reportedly '''removed''' and repurposed.On-site intypeation board by the Tenri City Board of Education. == burial & area == [[File:080515 Nishiyama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|Aerial view of Nishiyama Kofun.
{{National Aerial Photography}}.
[[:File:Tenri-nishiyama_stereo.jpg|Stereo image here]]]] The tumulus is a '''three-tiered, [[Zenpō-kōhō-fun|rectangular keyhole-shaped mound]] (前方後方墳, [[zenpō-kōhō-fun]])''' with the front section '''oriented westward'''. Its area are: * '''Total length''': 183 meters * '''Rear section''' (square): 94m wide × 16m high * '''Front section''': 72m wide The '''lower level''' is '''rectangular''', while the '''middle and upper levels''' are '''rounder''', creating a hybrid '''keyhole-shaped mound (前方後円形, zenpō-kōenkei)'''. The '''central burial chamber''' is estimated to be a '''[[Vertical pit stone chamber|pit-style stone chamber]]''' based on '''historical records'''. The mound is positioned '''along three natural ridges''', with the '''central ridge typeing the main mound''', while the '''north and south ridges serve as outer embankments'''. A '''moat once surrounded the mound''', but it has since been '''filled in'''. This kofun is '''the largest of its kind in Japan'''. The '''unique construction''', with a '''rectangular lower tier supporting a rounder upper structure''', is believed to be '''original to its design'''. == burial goods & burial Goods == Excavations have uncovered: * '''Copper mirrors (fragments)''' * '''Green jasper arrowheads''' * '''Magatama beads''' * '''Iron swords and blades''' * '''Wheel-shaped stone object (碧玉製車輪石, hekigyoku-sei sharinseki)''' * '''Haniwa clay figures''', including: ** '''[[Cylindrical Haniwa|Cylindrical haniwa]] (円筒埴輪)''' ** '''Fin-shaped haniwa (鰭付円筒埴輪)''' ** '''[[Figural Haniwa|House-shaped haniwa]] (家形埴輪)''' == Current Condition == The '''mound is well preserved''', and due to '''lack of tree cover''', the '''three-tiered structure is clearly visible'''. == Access == * '''20-minute walk from [[Tenri Station]]''' - Located '''500 meters south''' of the '''Tenri University Reference Museum''' * '''Just north''' of '''Tenri Middle School''' == designation1 == === '''National Historic Site of Japan''' === * '''Original Historic Site (1927)''': Nishiyama Kofun was Historic Site1 a '''National Historic Site'''. * '''Expansion (2018)''': The Historic Site was '''expanded''' to include '''Nishinorikura Kofun (西乗鞍古墳)''', renaming the site as the '''Somanochi Kofun Group (杣之内古墳群)'''.Ministry of Education, Science and Culture Announcement No. 19 (February 13, 2018). == References == The Kofun features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft}} at its base to a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}} at its upper levels. The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day {{ill|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市|12=draft}}), was targeted. == area and burial == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * '''Rear mound (posterior):''' 94m width, 16m height * '''Anterior mound:''' 72m width, 13m height The lower tier types a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in. Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design. == burial goods == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments''' * '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones''' * '''Surface burial goods:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure. == Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館|12=draft}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School. == Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927{{国cultural property等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the Historic Site1 area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|12=draft}} == External Links == * {{国cultural property等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}} * [http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html Tenri City Kofun Guide] {{otheruses|Nishiyama Kofun in Tenri, Nara|Nishiyama Kofun in Ota, Gunma|Nishiyama Kofun (Ota)}} {{Infobox Kofun | name = Nishiyama Kofun | native_name = 西山古墳 | image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px]]

It is part of the '''{{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|12=draft}}''' and is the '''largest kofun of its type in Japan'''. In '''1927 (Showa 2)''', it was '''Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site''' of Japan.{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/1958|title=Nishiyama Kofun - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}} It is also known by the '''alternate name "Nagariyama" (勾山, Magariyama).''' == Overview == The kofun was '''constructed during the early [[Kofun period]] (4th century)''' and is one of the '''earliest tumuli''' in the '''{{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|12=draft}}'''. The mound originally had a '''[[Vertical pit stone chamber|pit-style stone chamber]] (竪穴式石室, tateana-shiki sekishitsu)''', but it was likely '''looted in antiquity'''.Izumimori, Ko. *Ancient Tombs of Yamato I* (『大和の古墳I』), Jinbun Shoin, 2003. During '''World War II''', the Japanese Imperial Army '''stationed an anti-aircraft gun battery''' at the site. At that time, stones from the '''burial chamber (originally quarried in Kashiwara, Osaka)''' were reportedly '''removed''' and repurposed.On-site intypeation board by the Tenri City Board of Education. == burial & area == [[File:080515 Nishiyama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|Aerial view of Nishiyama Kofun.
{{National Aerial Photography}}.
[[:File:Tenri-nishiyama_stereo.jpg|Stereo image here]]]] The tumulus is a '''three-tiered, [[Zenpō-kōhō-fun|rectangular keyhole-shaped mound]] (前方後方墳, [[zenpō-kōhō-fun]])''' with the front section '''oriented westward'''. Its area are: * '''Total length''': 183 meters * '''Rear section''' (square): 94m wide × 16m high * '''Front section''': 72m wide The '''lower level''' is '''rectangular''', while the '''middle and upper levels''' are '''rounder''', creating a hybrid '''keyhole-shaped mound (前方後円形, zenpō-kōenkei)'''. The '''central burial chamber''' is estimated to be a '''[[Vertical pit stone chamber|pit-style stone chamber]]''' based on '''historical records'''. The mound is positioned '''along three natural ridges''', with the '''central ridge typeing the main mound''', while the '''north and south ridges serve as outer embankments'''. A '''moat once surrounded the mound''', but it has since been '''filled in'''. This kofun is '''the largest of its kind in Japan'''. The '''unique construction''', with a '''rectangular lower tier supporting a rounder upper structure''', is believed to be '''original to its design'''. == burial goods & burial Goods == Excavations have uncovered: * '''Copper mirrors (fragments)''' * '''Green jasper arrowheads''' * '''Magatama beads''' * '''Iron swords and blades''' * '''Wheel-shaped stone object (碧玉製車輪石, hekigyoku-sei sharinseki)''' * '''Haniwa clay figures''', including: ** '''[[Cylindrical Haniwa|Cylindrical haniwa]] (円筒埴輪)''' ** '''Fin-shaped haniwa (鰭付円筒埴輪)''' ** '''[[Figural Haniwa|House-shaped haniwa]] (家形埴輪)''' == Current Condition == The '''mound is well preserved''', and due to '''lack of tree cover''', the '''three-tiered structure is clearly visible'''. == Access == * '''20-minute walk from Please do not use any bots that just remove the unknown parameters without looking at them. This was added through [[Special:MassEditRegex]] to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft}} |name = Nishiyama Kofun |image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px|]] |caption = Mound overview (left: anterior, right back: posterior) |location = {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県|qq=draft}} {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市|qq=draft}} Somanouchi Town |coordinates = {{coord|34|35|33|N|135|50|36|E|region:JP-29_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Nishiyama Kofun}} |type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft}} |area = Total length: 183m, height: 13m |burial = {{ill|Pit-style stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=竪穴式石室|4=zh|5=豎穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft}} |built = Early Kofun period |Interred = (Theory) A member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏|qq=draft}} |burial goods = Mirror fragments, stone arrowheads, iron sword fragments, magatama, and haniwa |alternate_name = National Historic Site (Historic Site1 April 8, 1927) |map = Japan Nara |type = Zenpō-kōhō-fun-W }} '''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|qq=draft}} located in Somanouchi Town, {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県|qq=draft}}, Japan. It is Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site and is part of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|qq=draft}}. == Overview == Constructed during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft}} (4th century), Nishiyama Kofun is the oldest of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|qq=draft}}. The Kofun features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft}} at its base to a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft}} at its upper levels. The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day {{ill|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市|qq=draft}}), was targeted. == area and burial == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * '''Rear mound (posterior):''' 94m width, 16m height * '''Anterior mound:''' 72m width, 13m height The lower tier types a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in. Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design. == burial goods == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments''' * '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones''' * '''Surface burial goods:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure. == Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館|qq=draft}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School. == Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927{{国cultural property等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the Historic Site1 area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|qq=draft}} == External Links == * {{国cultural property等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}} * [http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html Tenri City Kofun Guide] {{otheruses|Nishiyama Kofun in Tenri, Nara|Nishiyama Kofun in Ota, Gunma|Nishiyama Kofun (Ota)}} {{Infobox Kofun | name = Nishiyama Kofun | native_name = 西山古墳 | image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px]]
Mound overview (left: front section, back right: rear section) | location = {{ill|Tenri, Nara|ja|天理市|qq=draft}}, Nara Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = 34.5925 | coordinates = 135.8433 | region = Japan | type = {{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft}} (rectangular keyhole-shaped tumulus) | length = 183m, Height: 13m | burial = {{ill|Tateana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=竪穴式石室|4=zh|5=豎穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft}} (pit-style stone chamber) | built = Early Kofun period (4th century) | person = Possibly a member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏|qq=draft}} | burial goods = Mirrors, stone arrowheads, iron swords and blades, magatama beads, haniwa clay figures | Historic Site1 = National Historic Site of Japan (Historic Site1 April 8, 1927) }} '''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a '''large [[Zenpō-kōhō-fun|rectangular keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後方墳, zenpō-kōhō-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Tenri, Nara|ja|天理市|qq=draft}}, Nara Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''{{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|qq=draft}}''' and is the '''largest kofun of its type in Japan'''. In '''1927 (Showa 2)''', it was '''Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site''' of Japan.{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/1958|title=Nishiyama Kofun - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}} It is also known by the '''alternate name "Nagariyama" (勾山, Magariyama).''' == Overview == The kofun was '''constructed during the early [[Kofun period]] (4th century)''' and is one of the '''earliest tumuli''' in the '''{{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|qq=draft}}'''. The mound originally had a '''[[Vertical pit stone chamber|pit-style stone chamber]] (竪穴式石室, tateana-shiki sekishitsu)''', but it was likely '''looted in antiquity'''.Izumimori, Ko. *Ancient Tombs of Yamato I* (『大和の古墳I』), Jinbun Shoin, 2003. During '''World War II''', the Japanese Imperial Army '''stationed an anti-aircraft gun battery''' at the site. At that time, stones from the '''burial chamber (originally quarried in Kashiwara, Osaka)''' were reportedly '''removed''' and repurposed.On-site intypeation board by the Tenri City Board of Education. == burial & area == [[File:080515 Nishiyama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|Aerial view of Nishiyama Kofun.
{{National Aerial Photography}}.
[[:File:Tenri-nishiyama_stereo.jpg|Stereo image here]]]] The tumulus is a '''three-tiered, [[Zenpō-kōhō-fun|rectangular keyhole-shaped mound]] (前方後方墳, [[zenpō-kōhō-fun]])''' with the front section '''oriented westward'''. Its area are: * '''Total length''': 183 meters * '''Rear section''' (square): 94m wide × 16m high * '''Front section''': 72m wide The '''lower level''' is '''rectangular''', while the '''middle and upper levels''' are '''rounder''', creating a hybrid '''keyhole-shaped mound (前方後円形, zenpō-kōenkei)'''. The '''central burial chamber''' is estimated to be a '''[[Vertical pit stone chamber|pit-style stone chamber]]''' based on '''historical records'''. The mound is positioned '''along three natural ridges''', with the '''central ridge typeing the main mound''', while the '''north and south ridges serve as outer embankments'''. A '''moat once surrounded the mound''', but it has since been '''filled in'''. This kofun is '''the largest of its kind in Japan'''. The '''unique construction''', with a '''rectangular lower tier supporting a rounder upper structure''', is believed to be '''original to its design'''. == burial goods & burial Goods == Excavations have uncovered: * '''Copper mirrors (fragments)''' * '''Green jasper arrowheads''' * '''Magatama beads''' * '''Iron swords and blades''' * '''Wheel-shaped stone object (碧玉製車輪石, hekigyoku-sei sharinseki)''' * '''Haniwa clay figures''', including: ** '''[[Cylindrical Haniwa|Cylindrical haniwa]] (円筒埴輪)''' ** '''Fin-shaped haniwa (鰭付円筒埴輪)''' ** '''[[Figural Haniwa|House-shaped haniwa]] (家形埴輪)''' == Current Condition == The '''mound is well preserved''', and due to '''lack of tree cover''', the '''three-tiered structure is clearly visible'''. == Access == * '''20-minute walk from [[Tenri Station]]''' - Located '''500 meters south''' of the '''Tenri University Reference Museum''' * '''Just north''' of '''Tenri Middle School''' == designation1 == === '''National Historic Site of Japan''' === * '''Original Historic Site (1927)''': Nishiyama Kofun was Historic Site1 a '''National Historic Site'''. * '''Expansion (2018)''': The Historic Site was '''expanded''' to include '''Nishinorikura Kofun (西乗鞍古墳)''', renaming the site as the '''Somanochi Kofun Group (杣之内古墳群)'''.Ministry of Education, Science and Culture Announcement No. 19 (February 13, 2018). == References == {{Reflist}} == Additional Resources == * '''On-site intypeation board''' (Tenri City Board of Education) * '''Tenri City Website: Kofun Guide''' == Related Articles == * {{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|qq=draft}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Nishiyama Kofun}} * [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/1958 '''Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan): Nishiyama Kofun'''] * [http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html '''Tenri City Official Kofun Guide'''] {{citation needed|Nishiyama Kofun}} {{Kofun navbar}}
