Its area are: * '''Total length''': 183 meters * '''Rear section''' (square): 94m wide × 16m high * '''Front section''': 72m wide The '''lower level''' is '''rectangular''', while the '''middle and upper levels''' are '''rounder''', creating a hybrid '''keyhole-shaped mound (前方後円形, zenpō-kōenkei)'''. The '''central burial chamber''' is estimated to be a '''[[Vertical pit stone chamber|pit-style stone chamber]]''' based on '''historical records'''. The mound is positioned '''along three natural ridges''', with the '''central ridge typeing the main mound''', while the '''north and south ridges serve as outer embankments'''. A '''moat once surrounded the mound''', but it has since been '''filled in'''. This kofun is '''the largest of its kind in Japan'''. The '''unique construction''', with a '''rectangular lower tier supporting a rounder upper structure''', is believed to be '''original to its design'''. == burial goods & burial Goods == Excavations have uncovered: * '''Copper mirrors (fragments)''' * '''Green jasper arrowheads''' * '''Magatama beads''' * '''Iron swords and blades''' * '''Wheel-shaped stone object (碧玉製車輪石, hekigyoku-sei sharinseki)''' * '''Haniwa clay figures''', including: ** '''[[Cylindrical Haniwa|Cylindrical haniwa]] (円筒埴輪)''' ** '''Fin-shaped haniwa (鰭付円筒埴輪)''' ** '''[[Figural Haniwa|House-shaped haniwa]] (家形埴輪)''' == Current Condition == The '''mound is well preserved''', and due to '''lack of tree cover''', the '''three-tiered structure is clearly visible'''. == Access == * '''20-minute walk from [[Tenri Station]]''' - Located '''500 meters south''' of the '''Tenri University Reference Museum''' * '''Just north''' of '''Tenri Middle School''' == designation1 == === '''National Historic Site of Japan''' === * '''Original Historic Site (1927)''': Nishiyama Kofun was Historic Site1 a '''National Historic Site'''. * '''Expansion (2018)''': The Historic Site was '''expanded''' to include {{coord|34|35|33|N|135|50|36|E|region:JP-29_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Nishiyama Kofun}} |type = {{ill|Zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpō-kōhō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=}} |area = Total length: 183m, height: 13m |burial = {{ill|Pit-style stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=竪穴式石室|4=zh|5=豎穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Pit-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} |built = Early Kofun period |Interred = (Theory) A member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mononobe clan|qq=}} |burial goods = Mirror fragments, stone arrowheads, iron sword fragments, magatama, and haniwa |alternate_name = National Historic Site (Historic Site1 April 8, 1927) |map = Japan Nara |type = Zenpō-kōhō-fun-W }} '''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun|qq=}} located in Somanouchi Town, {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenri|qq=}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nara Prefecture|qq=}}, Japan. It is Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site and is part of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Somanouchi Kofun cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Somanouchi Kofun cluster|qq=}}. == Overview == Constructed during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun period|qq=}} (4th century), Nishiyama Kofun is the oldest of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Somanouchi Kofun cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Somanouchi Kofun cluster|qq=}}. The Kofun features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=}} at its base to a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōen-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|qq=}} at its upper levels. The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day {{ill|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kashiwara|qq=}}), was targeted. == area and burial == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * '''Rear mound (posterior):''' 94m width, 16m height * '''Anterior mound:''' 72m width, 13m height The lower tier types a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōen-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|qq=}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in. Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design. == burial goods == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments''' * '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones''' * '''Surface burial goods:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure. == Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenri University Sankokan Museum|qq=}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School. == Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927{{国cultural property等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the Historic Site1 area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Somanouchi Kofun cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Somanouchi Kofun cluster|qq=}} == External Links == * {{国cultural property等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}} * [http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html Tenri City Kofun Guide] {{otheruses|Nishiyama Kofun in Tenri, Nara|Nishiyama Kofun in Ota, Gunma|Nishiyama Kofun (Ota)}} {{Infobox Kofun | name = Nishiyama Kofun | native_name = 西山古墳 | image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px]]
Mound overview (left: front section, back right: rear section) | location = {{ill|Tenri, Nara|ja|天理市|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenri, Nara|qq=}}, Nara Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = 34.5925 | coordinates = 135.8433 | region = Japan | type = {{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoho-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=}} (rectangular keyhole-shaped tumulus) | length = 183m, Height: 13m | burial = {{ill|Tateana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=竪穴式石室|4=zh|5=豎穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tateana-shiki sekishitsu|13=User:Immanuelle/Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} (pit-style stone chamber) | built = Early Kofun period (4th century) | person = Possibly a member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mononobe clan|qq=}} | burial goods = Mirrors, stone arrowheads, iron swords and blades, magatama beads, haniwa clay figures | Historic Site1 = National Historic Site of Japan (Historic Site1 April 8, 1927) }} '''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a '''large [[Zenpō-kōhō-fun|rectangular keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後方墳, zenpō-kōhō-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Tenri, Nara|ja|天理市|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenri, Nara|qq=}}, Nara Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''{{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Somanochi Kofun Group|13=User:Immanuelle/Somanouchi Kofun cluster|qq=}}''' and is the '''largest kofun of its type in Japan'''. In '''1927 (Showa 2)''', it was '''Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site''' of Japan.{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/1958|title=Nishiyama Kofun - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}} It is also known by the '''alternate name "Nagariyama" (勾山, Magariyama).''' == Overview == The kofun was '''constructed during the early [[Kofun period]] (4th century)''' and is one of the '''earliest tumuli''' in the '''{{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Somanochi Kofun Group|13=User:Immanuelle/Somanouchi Kofun cluster|qq=}}'''. The mound originally had a '''[[Vertical pit stone chamber|pit-style stone chamber]] (竪穴式石室, tateana-shiki sekishitsu)''', but it was likely '''looted in antiquity'''.Izumimori, Ko. *Ancient Tombs of Yamato I* (『大和の古墳I』), Jinbun Shoin, 2003. During '''World War II''', the Japanese Imperial Army '''stationed an anti-aircraft gun battery''' at the site. At that time, stones from the '''burial chamber (originally quarried in Kashiwara, Osaka)''' were reportedly '''removed''' and repurposed.On-site intypeation board by the Tenri City Board of Education. == burial & area == [[File:080515 Nishiyama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|Aerial view of Nishiyama Kofun.
{{National Aerial Photography}}.
[[:File:Tenri-nishiyama_stereo.jpg|Stereo image here]]]] The tumulus is a '''three-tiered, [[Zenpō-kōhō-fun|rectangular keyhole-shaped mound]] (前方後方墳, [[zenpō-kōhō-fun]])''' with the front section '''oriented westward'''. Its area are: * '''Total length''': 183 meters * '''Rear section''' (square): 94m wide × 16m high * '''Front section''': 72m wide The '''lower level''' is '''rectangular''', while the '''middle and upper levels''' are '''rounder''', creating a hybrid '''keyhole-shaped mound (前方後円形, zenpō-kōenkei)'''. The '''central burial chamber''' is estimated to be a '''[[Vertical pit stone chamber|pit-style stone chamber]]''' based on '''historical records'''. The mound is positioned '''along three natural ridges''', with the '''central ridge typeing the main mound''', while the '''north and south ridges serve as outer embankments'''. A '''moat once surrounded the mound''', but it has since been '''filled in'''. This kofun is '''the largest of its kind in Japan'''. The '''unique construction''', with a '''rectangular lower tier supporting a rounder upper structure''', is believed to be '''original to its design'''. == burial goods & burial Goods == Excavations have uncovered: * '''Copper mirrors (fragments)''' * '''Green jasper arrowheads''' * '''Magatama beads''' * '''Iron swords and blades''' * '''Wheel-shaped stone object (碧玉製車輪石, hekigyoku-sei sharinseki)''' * '''Haniwa clay figures''', including: ** '''[[Cylindrical Haniwa|Cylindrical haniwa]] (円筒埴輪)''' ** '''Fin-shaped haniwa (鰭付円筒埴輪)''' ** '''[[Figural Haniwa|House-shaped haniwa]] (家形埴輪)''' == Current Condition == The '''mound is well preserved''', and due to '''lack of tree cover''', the '''three-tiered structure is clearly visible'''. == Access == * '''20-minute walk from {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun|qq=}} located in Somanouchi Town, {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenri|qq=}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nara Prefecture|qq=}}, Japan. It is Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site and is part of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Somanouchi Kofun cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Somanouchi Kofun cluster|qq=}}. == Overview == Constructed during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun period|qq=}} (4th century), Nishiyama Kofun is the oldest of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Somanouchi Kofun cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Somanouchi Kofun cluster|qq=}}. The Kofun features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=}} at its base to a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōen-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|qq=}} at its upper levels. The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day {{ill|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kashiwara|qq=}}), was targeted. == area and burial == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * '''Rear mound (posterior):''' 94m width, 16m height * '''Anterior mound:''' 72m width, 13m height The lower tier types a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōen-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|qq=}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in. Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design. == burial goods == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments''' * '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones''' * '''Surface burial goods:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure. == Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenri University Sankokan Museum|qq=}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School. == Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927{{国cultural property等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the Historic Site1 area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Somanouchi Kofun cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Somanouchi Kofun cluster|qq=}} == External Links == * {{国cultural property等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}} * [http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html Tenri City Kofun Guide] {{otheruses|Nishiyama Kofun in Tenri, Nara|Nishiyama Kofun in Ota, Gunma|Nishiyama Kofun (Ota)}} {{Infobox Kofun | name = Nishiyama Kofun | native_name = 西山古墳 | image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px]]
Mound overview (left: front section, back right: rear section) | location = {{ill|Tenri, Nara|ja|天理市|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenri, Nara|qq=}}, Nara Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = 34.5925 | coordinates = 135.8433 | region = Japan | type = {{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoho-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=}} (rectangular keyhole-shaped tumulus) | length = 183m, Height: 13m | burial = {{ill|Tateana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=竪穴式石室|4=zh|5=豎穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tateana-shiki sekishitsu|13=User:Immanuelle/Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} (pit-style stone chamber) | built = Early Kofun period (4th century) | person = Possibly a member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mononobe clan|qq=}} | burial goods = Mirrors, stone arrowheads, iron swords and blades, magatama beads, haniwa clay figures | Historic Site1 = National Historic Site of Japan (Historic Site1 April 8, 1927) }} '''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a '''large [[Zenpō-kōhō-fun|rectangular keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後方墳, zenpō-kōhō-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Tenri, Nara|ja|天理市|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenri, Nara|qq=}}, Nara Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''{{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Somanochi Kofun Group|13=User:Immanuelle/Somanouchi Kofun cluster|qq=}}''' and is the '''largest kofun of its type in Japan'''. In '''1927 (Showa 2)''', it was '''Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site''' of Japan.{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/1958|title=Nishiyama Kofun - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}} It is also known by the '''alternate name "Nagariyama" (勾山, Magariyama).''' == Overview == The kofun was '''constructed during the early [[Kofun period]] (4th century)''' and is one of the '''earliest tumuli''' in the '''{{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Somanochi Kofun Group|13=User:Immanuelle/Somanouchi Kofun cluster|qq=}}'''. The mound originally had a '''[[Vertical pit stone chamber|pit-style stone chamber]] (竪穴式石室, tateana-shiki sekishitsu)''', but it was likely '''looted in antiquity'''.Izumimori, Ko. *Ancient Tombs of Yamato I* (『大和の古墳I』), Jinbun Shoin, 2003. During '''World War II''', the Japanese Imperial Army '''stationed an anti-aircraft gun battery''' at the site. At that time, stones from the '''burial chamber (originally quarried in Kashiwara, Osaka)''' were reportedly '''removed''' and repurposed.On-site intypeation board by the Tenri City Board of Education. == burial & area == [[File:080515 Nishiyama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|Aerial view of Nishiyama Kofun.
{{National Aerial Photography}}.
[[:File:Tenri-nishiyama_stereo.jpg|Stereo image here]]]] The tumulus is a '''three-tiered, [[Zenpō-kōhō-fun|rectangular keyhole-shaped mound]] (前方後方墳, [[zenpō-kōhō-fun]])''' with the front section '''oriented westward'''. Its area are: * '''Total length''': 183 meters * '''Rear section''' (square): 94m wide × 16m high * '''Front section''': 72m wide The '''lower level''' is '''rectangular''', while the '''middle and upper levels''' are '''rounder''', creating a hybrid '''keyhole-shaped mound (前方後円形, zenpō-kōenkei)'''. The '''central burial chamber''' is estimated to be a '''[[Vertical pit stone chamber|pit-style stone chamber]]''' based on '''historical records'''. The mound is positioned '''along three natural ridges''', with the '''central ridge typeing the main mound''', while the '''north and south ridges serve as outer embankments'''. A '''moat once surrounded the mound''', but it has since been '''filled in'''. This kofun is '''the largest of its kind in Japan'''. The '''unique construction''', with a '''rectangular lower tier supporting a rounder upper structure''', is believed to be '''original to its design'''. == burial goods & burial Goods == Excavations have uncovered: * '''Copper mirrors (fragments)''' * '''Green jasper arrowheads''' * '''Magatama beads''' * '''Iron swords and blades''' * '''Wheel-shaped stone object (碧玉製車輪石, hekigyoku-sei sharinseki)''' * '''Haniwa clay figures''', including: ** '''[[Cylindrical Haniwa|Cylindrical haniwa]] (円筒埴輪)''' ** '''Fin-shaped haniwa (鰭付円筒埴輪)''' ** '''[[Figural Haniwa|House-shaped haniwa]] (家形埴輪)''' == Current Condition == The '''mound is well preserved''', and due to '''lack of tree cover''', the '''three-tiered structure is clearly visible'''. == Access == * '''20-minute walk from [[Tenri Station]]''' - Located '''500 meters south''' of the '''Tenri University Reference Museum''' * '''Just north''' of '''Tenri Middle School''' == designation1 == === '''National Historic Site of Japan''' === * '''Original Historic Site (1927)''': Nishiyama Kofun was Historic Site1 a '''National Historic Site'''. * '''Expansion (2018)''': The Historic Site was '''expanded''' to include '''Nishinorikura Kofun (西乗鞍古墳)''', renaming the site as the '''Somanochi Kofun Group (杣之内古墳群)'''.Ministry of Education, Science and Culture Announcement No. 19 (February 13, 2018). == References == It is part of the '''{{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Somanochi Kofun Group|13=User:Immanuelle/Somanouchi Kofun cluster|qq=}}''' and is the '''largest kofun of its type in Japan'''. In '''1927 (Showa 2)''', it was '''Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site''' of Japan.{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/1958|title=Nishiyama Kofun - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}} It is also known by the '''alternate name "Nagariyama" (勾山, Magariyama).''' == Overview == The kofun was '''constructed during the early [[Kofun period]] (4th century)''' and is one of the '''earliest tumuli''' in the '''{{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Somanochi Kofun Group|13=User:Immanuelle/Somanouchi Kofun cluster|qq=}}'''. Its area are: * '''Total length''': 183 meters * '''Rear section''' (square): 94m wide × 16m high * '''Front section''': 72m wide The '''lower level''' is '''rectangular''', while the '''middle and upper levels''' are '''rounder''', creating a hybrid '''keyhole-shaped mound (前方後円形, zenpō-kōenkei)'''. The '''central burial chamber''' is estimated to be a '''[[Vertical pit stone chamber|pit-style stone chamber]]''' based on '''historical records'''. The mound is positioned '''along three natural ridges''', with the '''central ridge typeing the main mound''', while the '''north and south ridges serve as outer embankments'''. A '''moat once surrounded the mound''', but it has since been '''filled in'''. This kofun is '''the largest of its kind in Japan'''. The '''unique construction''', with a '''rectangular lower tier supporting a rounder upper structure''', is believed to be '''original to its design'''. == burial goods & burial Goods == Excavations sharinseki)''' * '''Haniwa clay figures''', including: ** '''[[Cylindrical Haniwa|Cylindrical haniwa]] (円筒埴輪)''' ** '''Fin-shaped haniwa (鰭付円筒埴輪)''' ** '''[[Figural Haniwa|House-shaped haniwa]] (家形埴輪)''' == Current Condition == The '''mound is well preserved''', and due to '''lack of tree cover''', the '''three-tiered structure is clearly visible'''. == Access == * '''20-minute walk from Site (Historic Site1 April 8, 1927) |map = Japan Nara |type = Zenpō-kōhō-fun-W }} '''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun|qq=}} located in Somanouchi Town, {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenri|qq=}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nara Prefecture|qq=}}, Japan. It is Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site and is part of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Somanouchi Kofun cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Somanouchi Kofun cluster|qq=}}. == Overview == Constructed during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun period|qq=}} (4th century), Nishiyama Kofun is the oldest of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Somanouchi Kofun cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Somanouchi Kofun cluster|qq=}}. The Kofun features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=}} at its base to a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōen-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|qq=}} at its upper levels. The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day {{ill|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kashiwara|qq=}}), was targeted. == area and burial == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * '''Rear mound (posterior):''' 94m width, 16m height * '''Anterior mound:''' 72m width, 13m height The lower tier types a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōen-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|qq=}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in. Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design. == burial goods == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments''' * '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones''' * '''Surface burial goods:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure. == Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenri University Sankokan Museum|qq=}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School. == Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927{{国cultural property等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the Historic Site1 area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Somanouchi Kofun cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Somanouchi Kofun cluster|qq=}} == External Links == * {{国cultural property等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}} * [http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html Tenri City Kofun Guide] {{otheruses|Nishiyama Kofun in Tenri, Nara|Nishiyama Kofun in Ota, Gunma|Nishiyama Kofun (Ota)}} {{Infobox Kofun | name = Nishiyama Kofun | native_name = 西山古墳 | image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px]]

{{ill|Pit-style stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=竪穴式石室|4=zh|5=豎穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Pit-style stone Site (Historic Site1 April 8, 1927) |map = Japan Nara |type = Zenpō-kōhō-fun-W }} '''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun|qq=}} located in Somanouchi Town, {{ill|Tenri|ja|天理市|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenri|qq=}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nara Prefecture|qq=}}, Japan. It is Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site and is part of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Somanouchi Kofun cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Somanouchi Kofun cluster|qq=}}. == Overview == Constructed during the early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun period|qq=}} (4th century), Nishiyama Kofun is the oldest of the {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Somanouchi Kofun cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Somanouchi Kofun cluster|qq=}}. The Kofun features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=}} at its base to a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōen-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|qq=}} at its upper levels. The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day {{ill|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kashiwara|qq=}}), was targeted. == area and burial == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * '''Rear mound (posterior):''' 94m width, 16m height * '''Anterior mound:''' 72m width, 13m height The lower tier types a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōen-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|qq=}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in. Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design. == burial goods == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments''' * '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones''' * '''Surface burial goods:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure. == Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenri University Sankokan Museum|qq=}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School. == Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927{{国cultural property等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the Historic Site1 area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Somanouchi Kofun cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Somanouchi Kofun cluster|qq=}} == External Links == * {{国cultural property等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}} * [http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html Tenri City Kofun Guide] {{otheruses|Nishiyama Kofun in Tenri, Nara|Nishiyama Kofun in Ota, Gunma|Nishiyama Kofun (Ota)}} {{Infobox Kofun | name = Nishiyama Kofun | native_name = 西山古墳 | image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px]]
Mound overview (left: front section, back right: rear section) | location = {{ill|Tenri, Nara|ja|天理市|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenri, Nara|qq=}}, Nara Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = 34.5925 | coordinates = 135.8433 | region = Japan | type = {{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoho-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=}} (rectangular keyhole-shaped tumulus) | length = 183m, Height: 13m | burial = {{ill|Tateana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=竪穴式石室|4=zh|5=豎穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tateana-shiki sekishitsu|13=User:Immanuelle/Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} (pit-style stone chamber) | built = Early Kofun period (4th century) | person = Possibly a member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mononobe clan|qq=}} | burial goods = Mirrors, stone arrowheads, iron swords and blades, magatama beads, haniwa clay figures | Historic Site1 = National Historic Site of Japan (Historic Site1 April 8, 1927) }} '''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a '''large [[Zenpō-kōhō-fun|rectangular keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後方墳, zenpō-kōhō-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Tenri, Nara|ja|天理市|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenri, Nara|qq=}}, Nara Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''{{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Somanochi Kofun Group|13=User:Immanuelle/Somanouchi Kofun cluster|qq=}}''' and is the '''largest kofun of its type in Japan'''. In '''1927 (Showa 2)''', it was '''Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site''' of Japan.{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/1958|title=Nishiyama Kofun - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}} It is also known by the '''alternate name "Nagariyama" (勾山, Magariyama).''' == Overview == The kofun was '''constructed during the early [[Kofun period]] (4th century)''' and is one of the '''earliest tumuli''' in the '''{{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Somanochi Kofun Group|13=User:Immanuelle/Somanouchi Kofun cluster|qq=}}'''. The mound originally had a '''[[Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|pit-style stone chamber]] (竪穴式石室, tateana-shiki sekishitsu)''', but it was likely '''looted in antiquity'''.Izumimori, Ko. *Ancient Tombs of Yamato I* (『大和の古墳I』), Jinbun Shoin, 2003. During '''World War II''', the Japanese Imperial Army '''stationed an anti-aircraft gun battery''' at the site. At that time, stones from the '''burial chamber (originally quarried in Kashiwara, Osaka)''' were reportedly '''removed''' and repurposed.On-site intypeation board by the Tenri City Board of Education. == burial & area == [[File:080515 Nishiyama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|Aerial view of Nishiyama Kofun.
{{National Aerial Photography}}.
[[:File:Tenri-nishiyama_stereo.jpg|Stereo image here]]]] The tumulus is a '''three-tiered, [[Zenpō-kōhō-fun|rectangular keyhole-shaped mound]] (前方後方墳, [[zenpō-kōhō-fun]])''' with the front section '''oriented westward'''. Its area are: * '''Total length''': 183 meters * '''Rear section''' (square): 94m wide × 16m high * '''Front section''': 72m wide The '''lower level''' is '''rectangular''', while the '''middle and upper levels''' are '''rounder''', creating a hybrid '''keyhole-shaped mound (前方後円形, zenpō-kōenkei)'''. The '''central burial chamber''' is estimated to be a '''[[Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|pit-style stone chamber]]''' based on '''historical records'''. The mound is positioned '''along three natural ridges''', with the '''central ridge typeing the main mound''', while the '''north and south ridges serve as outer embankments'''. A '''moat once surrounded the mound''', but it has since been '''filled in'''. This kofun is '''the largest of its kind in Japan'''. The '''unique construction''', with a '''rectangular lower tier supporting a rounder upper structure''', is believed to be '''original to its design'''. == burial goods & burial Goods == Excavations have uncovered: * '''Copper mirrors (fragments)''' * '''Green jasper arrowheads''' * '''Magatama beads''' * '''Iron swords and blades''' * '''Wheel-shaped stone object (碧玉製車輪石, hekigyoku-sei sharinseki)''' * '''Haniwa clay figures''', including: ** '''[[Cylindrical Haniwa|Cylindrical haniwa]] (円筒埴輪)''' ** '''Fin-shaped haniwa (鰭付円筒埴輪)''' ** '''[[Figural Haniwa|House-shaped haniwa]] (家形埴輪)''' == Current Condition == The '''mound is well preserved''', and due to '''lack of tree cover''', the '''three-tiered structure is clearly visible'''. == Access == * '''20-minute walk from [[Tenri Station]]''' - Located '''500 meters south''' of the '''Tenri University Reference Museum''' * '''Just north''' of '''Tenri Middle School''' == designation1 == === '''National Historic Site of Japan''' === * '''Original Historic Site (1927)''': Nishiyama Kofun was Historic Site1 a '''National Historic Site'''. * '''Expansion (2018)''': The Historic Site was '''expanded''' to include '''Nishinorikura Kofun (西乗鞍古墳)''', renaming the site as the '''Somanochi Kofun Group (杣之内古墳群)'''.Ministry of Education, Science and Culture Announcement No. 19 (February 13, 2018). == References == {{Reflist}} == Additional Resources == * '''On-site intypeation board''' (Tenri City Board of Education) * '''Tenri City Website: Kofun Guide''' == Related Articles == * {{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Somanochi Kofun Group|13=User:Immanuelle/Somanouchi Kofun cluster|qq=}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Nishiyama The Kofun features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=}} at its base to a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|comement=second one attempting to fix this error|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōen-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|qq=}} at its upper levels. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|comement=second one attempting to fix this error|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōen-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|qq=}} with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in. Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design. == burial goods == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments''' * '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones''' * '''Surface burial goods:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure. == Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the {{ill|Tenri University Sankokan Museum|ja|天理大学附属天理参考館|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenri University Sankokan Museum|qq=}} and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School. == Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927{{国cultural property等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the Historic Site1 area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Somanouchi Kofun cluster|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Somanouchi Kofun cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Somanouchi Kofun cluster|qq=}} == External Links == * {{国cultural property等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}} * [http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html Tenri City Kofun Guide] {{otheruses|Nishiyama Kofun in Tenri, Nara|Nishiyama Kofun in Ota, Gunma|Nishiyama Kofun (Ota)}} {{Infobox Kofun | name = Nishiyama Kofun | native_name = 西山古墳 | image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px]]
Mound overview (left: front section, back right: rear section) | location = {{ill|Tenri, Nara|ja|天理市|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenri, Nara|qq=}}, Nara Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = 34.5925 | coordinates = 135.8433 | region = Japan | type = {{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoho-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=}} (rectangular keyhole-shaped tumulus) | length = 183m, Height: 13m | burial = {{ill|Tateana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=竪穴式石室|4=zh|5=豎穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tateana-shiki sekishitsu|13=User:Immanuelle/Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} (pit-style stone chamber) | built = Early Kofun period (4th century) | person = Possibly a member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mononobe clan|qq=}} | burial goods = Mirrors, stone arrowheads, iron swords and blades, magatama beads, haniwa clay figures | Historic Site1 = National Historic Site of Japan (Historic Site1 April 8, 1927) }} '''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a '''large [[Zenpō-kōhō-fun|rectangular keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後方墳, zenpō-kōhō-fun)''' located in '''{{ill|Tenri, Nara|ja|天理市|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenri, Nara|qq=}}, Nara Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''{{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Somanochi Kofun Group|13=User:Immanuelle/Somanouchi Kofun cluster|qq=}}''' and is the '''largest kofun of its type in Japan'''. In '''1927 (Showa 2)''', it was '''Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site''' of Japan.{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/1958|title=Nishiyama Kofun - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}} It is also known by the '''alternate name "Nagariyama" (勾山, Magariyama).''' == Overview == The kofun was '''constructed during the early [[Kofun period]] (4th century)''' and is one of the '''earliest tumuli''' in the '''{{ill|Somanochi Kofun Group|ja|杣之内古墳群|1=Somanouchi Kofun cluster|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Somanochi Kofun Group|13=User:Immanuelle/Somanouchi Kofun cluster|qq=}}'''. The mound originally had a '''[[Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|pit-style stone chamber]] (竪穴式石室, tateana-shiki sekishitsu)''', but it was likely '''looted in antiquity'''.Izumimori, Ko. *Ancient Tombs of Yamato I* (『大和の古墳I』), Jinbun Shoin, 2003. During '''World War II''', the Japanese Imperial Army '''stationed an anti-aircraft gun battery''' at the site. At that time, stones from the '''burial chamber (originally quarried in Kashiwara, Osaka)''' were reportedly '''removed''' and repurposed.On-site intypeation board by the Tenri City Board of Education. == burial & area == [[File:080515 Nishiyama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|Aerial view of Nishiyama Kofun.
{{National Aerial Photography}}.
[[:File:Tenri-nishiyama_stereo.jpg|Stereo image here]]]] The tumulus is a '''three-tiered, [[Zenpō-kōhō-fun|rectangular keyhole-shaped mound]] (前方後方墳, [[zenpō-kōhō-fun]])''' with the front section '''oriented westward'''. Its area are: * '''Total length''': 183 meters * '''Rear section''' (square): 94m wide × 16m high * '''Front section''': 72m wide The '''lower level''' is '''rectangular''', while the '''middle and upper levels''' are '''rounder''', creating a hybrid '''keyhole-shaped mound (前方後円形, zenpō-kōenkei)'''. The '''central burial chamber''' is estimated to be a '''[[Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|pit-style stone chamber]]''' based on '''historical records'''. The mound is positioned '''along three natural ridges''', with the '''central ridge typeing the main mound''', while the '''north and south ridges serve as outer embankments'''. A '''moat once surrounded the mound''', but it has since been '''filled in'''. This kofun is '''the largest of its kind in Japan'''. The '''unique construction''', with a '''rectangular lower tier supporting a rounder upper structure''', is believed to be '''original to its design'''. == burial goods & burial Goods == Excavations have uncovered: * '''Copper mirrors (fragments)''' * '''Green jasper arrowheads''' * '''Magatama beads''' * '''Iron swords and blades''' * '''Wheel-shaped stone object (碧玉製車輪石, hekigyoku-sei sharinseki)''' * '''Haniwa clay figures''', including: ** '''[[Cylindrical Haniwa|Cylindrical haniwa]] (円筒埴輪)''' ** '''Fin-shaped haniwa (鰭付円筒埴輪)''' ** '''[[Figural Haniwa|House-shaped haniwa]] (家形埴輪)''' == Current Condition == The '''mound is well preserved''', and due to '''lack of tree cover''', the '''three-tiered structure is clearly visible'''. == Access == * '''20-minute walk from [[Tenri Station]]''' - Located '''500 meters south''' of the '''Tenri University Reference Museum''' * '''Just north''' of '''Tenri Middle School''' == designation1 == === '''National Historic Site of Japan''' === * '''Original Historic Site (1927)''': Nishiyama Kofun was Historic Site1 a '''National Historic Site'''. * '''Expansion (2018)''': The Historic Site was '''expanded''' to include '''Nishinorikura Kofun (西乗鞍古墳)''', renaming the site as the '''Somanochi Kofun Group (杣之内古墳群)'''.Ministry of Education, Science and Culture Announcement No. 19 (February 13, 2018). == References == The mound originally had a '''[[Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|pit-style stone chamber]] (竪穴式石室, tateana-shiki sekishitsu)''', but it was likely '''looted in antiquity'''.Izumimori, Ko. *Ancient Tombs of Yamato I* (『大和の古墳I』), Jinbun Shoin, 2003. During '''World War II''', the Japanese Imperial Army '''stationed an anti-aircraft gun battery''' at the site. At that time, stones from the '''burial chamber (originally quarried in Kashiwara, Osaka)''' were reportedly '''removed''' and repurposed.On-site intypeation board by the Tenri City Board of Education. == burial & area == [[File:080515 Nishiyama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|Aerial view of Nishiyama Kofun.
{{National Aerial Photography}}.
[[:File:Tenri-nishiyama_stereo.jpg|Stereo image here]]]] The tumulus is a '''three-tiered, [[Zenpō-kōhō-fun|rectangular keyhole-shaped mound]] (前方後方墳, [[zenpō-kōhō-fun]])''' with the front section '''oriented westward'''. Its area are: * '''Total length''': 183 meters * '''Rear section''' (square): 94m wide × 16m high * '''Front section''': 72m wide The '''lower level''' is '''rectangular''', while the '''middle and upper levels''' are '''rounder''', creating a hybrid '''keyhole-shaped mound (前方後円形, zenpō-kōenkei)'''. The '''central burial chamber''' is estimated to be a '''[[Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|pit-style stone chamber]]''' based on '''historical records'''. The mound is positioned '''along three natural ridges''', with the '''central ridge typeing the main mound''', while the '''north and south ridges serve as outer embankments'''. A '''moat once surrounded the mound''', but it has since been '''filled in'''. This kofun is '''the largest of its kind in Japan'''. The '''unique construction''', with a '''rectangular lower tier supporting a rounder upper structure''', is believed to be '''original to its design'''. == burial goods & burial Goods == Excavations have uncovered: * '''Copper mirrors (fragments)''' * '''Green jasper arrowheads''' * '''Magatama beads''' * '''Iron swords and blades''' * '''Wheel-shaped stone object (碧玉製車輪石, hekigyoku-sei sharinseki)''' * '''Haniwa clay figures''', including: ** '''[[Cylindrical Haniwa|Cylindrical haniwa]] (円筒埴輪)''' ** '''Fin-shaped haniwa (鰭付円筒埴輪)''' ** '''[[Figural Haniwa|House-shaped haniwa]] (家形埴輪)''' == Current Condition == The '''mound is well preserved''', and due to '''lack of tree cover''', the '''three-tiered structure is clearly visible'''. == Access == * '''20-minute walk from [[Tenri Station]]''' - Located '''500 meters south''' of the '''Tenri University Reference Museum''' * '''Just north''' of '''Tenri Middle School''' == designation1 == === '''National Historic Site of Japan''' === * '''Original Historic Site (1927)''': Nishiyama Kofun was Historic Site1 a '''National Historic Site'''. * '''Expansion (2018)''': The Historic Site was '''expanded''' to include '''Nishinorikura Kofun (西乗鞍古墳)''', renaming the site as the '''Somanochi Kofun Group (杣之内古墳群)'''.Ministry of Education, Science and Culture Announcement No. 19 (February 13, 2018). == References == stone arrowheads, iron sword fragments, magatama, and haniwa |alternate_name = National Historic Site (Historic Site1 April 8, 1927) |map = Japan Nara |type = Zenpō-kōhō-fun-W }} '''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in Somanouchi Town, [[:en:Tenri, Nara|Tenri]], [[:en:Nara Prefecture|Nara Prefecture]], Japan. It is Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site and is part of the [[:en:Somanouchi Kofun cluster|Somanouchi Kofun cluster]]. == Overview == Constructed during the early [[:en:Kofun period|Kofun period]] (4th century), Nishiyama Kofun is the oldest of the [[:en:Somanouchi Kofun cluster|Somanouchi Kofun cluster]]. The Kofun features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=}} at its base to a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] at its upper levels. The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day [[:en:Kashiwara|Kashiwara]]), was targeted. == area and burial == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * '''Rear mound (posterior):''' 94m width, 16m height * '''Anterior mound:''' 72m width, 13m height The lower tier types a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in. Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design. == burial goods == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments''' * '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones''' * '''Surface burial goods:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure. == Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the [[:en:Tenri University Sankōkan Museum|Tenri University Sankokan Museum]] and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School. == Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927{{国cultural property等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the Historic Site1 area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * [[:en:Somanouchi Kofun cluster|Somanouchi Kofun cluster]] == External Links == * {{国cultural property等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}} * [http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html Tenri City Kofun Guide] {{otheruses|Nishiyama Kofun in Tenri, Nara|Nishiyama Kofun in Ota, Gunma|Nishiyama Kofun (Ota)}} {{Infobox Kofun | name = Nishiyama Kofun | native_name = 西山古墳 | image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px]]

The Kofun features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=}} at its base to a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] at its upper levels. The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day [[:en:Kashiwara|Kashiwara]]), was targeted. == area and burial == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * '''Rear mound (posterior):''' 94m width, 16m height * '''Anterior mound:''' 72m width, 13m height The lower tier types a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in. Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design. == burial goods == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments''' * '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones''' * '''Surface burial goods:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure. == Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the [[:en:Tenri University Sankōkan Museum|Tenri University Sankokan Museum]] and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School. == Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927{{国cultural property等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the Historic Site1 area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * [[:en:Somanouchi Kofun cluster|Somanouchi Kofun cluster]] == External Links == * {{国cultural property等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}} * [http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html Tenri City Kofun Guide] {{otheruses|Nishiyama Kofun in Tenri, Nara|Nishiyama Kofun in Ota, Gunma|Nishiyama Kofun (Ota)}} {{Infobox Kofun | name = Nishiyama Kofun | native_name = 西山古墳 | image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px]]
Mound overview (left: front section, back right: rear section) | location = [[:en:Tenri, Nara|Tenri, Nara]], Nara Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = 34.5925 | coordinates = 135.8433 | region = Japan | type = {{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoho-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=}} (rectangular keyhole-shaped tumulus) | length = 183m, Height: 13m | burial = {{ill|Tateana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=竪穴式石室|4=zh|5=豎穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tateana-shiki sekishitsu|13=User:Immanuelle/Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} (pit-style stone chamber) | built = Early Kofun period (4th century) | person = Possibly a member of the [[:en:Mononobe clan|Mononobe clan]] | burial goods = Mirrors, stone arrowheads, iron swords and blades, magatama beads, haniwa clay figures | Historic Site1 = National Historic Site of Japan (Historic Site1 April 8, 1927) }} '''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a '''large [[Zenpō-kōhō-fun|rectangular keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後方墳, zenpō-kōhō-fun)''' located in '''[[:en:Tenri, Nara|Tenri, Nara]], Nara Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''[[:en:Somanouchi Kofun cluster|Somanouchi Kofun cluster]]''' and is the '''largest kofun of its type in Japan'''. In '''1927 (Showa 2)''', it was '''Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site''' of Japan.{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/1958|title=Nishiyama Kofun - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}} It is also known by the '''alternate name "Nagariyama" (勾山, Magariyama).''' == Overview == The kofun was '''constructed during the early [[Kofun period]] (4th century)''' and is one of the '''earliest tumuli''' in the '''[[:en:Somanouchi Kofun cluster|Somanouchi Kofun cluster]]'''. The mound originally had a '''[[Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|pit-style stone chamber]] (竪穴式石室, tateana-shiki sekishitsu)''', but it was likely '''looted in antiquity'''.Izumimori, Ko. *Ancient Tombs of Yamato I* (『大和の古墳I』), Jinbun Shoin, 2003. During '''World War II''', the Japanese Imperial Army '''stationed an anti-aircraft gun battery''' at the site. At that time, stones from the '''burial chamber (originally quarried in Kashiwara, Osaka)''' were reportedly '''removed''' and repurposed.On-site intypeation board by the Tenri City Board of Education. == burial & area == [[File:080515 Nishiyama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|Aerial view of Nishiyama Kofun.
{{National Aerial Photography}}.
[[:File:Tenri-nishiyama_stereo.jpg|Stereo image here]]]] The tumulus is a '''three-tiered, [[Zenpō-kōhō-fun|rectangular keyhole-shaped mound]] (前方後方墳, [[zenpō-kōhō-fun]])''' with the front section '''oriented westward'''. Its area are: * '''Total length''': 183 meters * '''Rear section''' (square): 94m wide × 16m high * '''Front section''': 72m wide The '''lower level''' is '''rectangular''', while the '''middle and upper levels''' are '''rounder''', creating a hybrid '''keyhole-shaped mound (前方後円形, zenpō-kōenkei)'''. The '''central burial chamber''' is estimated to be a '''[[Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|pit-style stone chamber]]''' based on '''historical records'''. The mound is positioned '''along three natural ridges''', with the '''central ridge typeing the main mound''', while the '''north and south ridges serve as outer embankments'''. A '''moat once surrounded the mound''', but it has since been '''filled in'''. This kofun is '''the largest of its kind in Japan'''. The '''unique construction''', with a '''rectangular lower tier supporting a rounder upper structure''', is believed to be '''original to its design'''. == burial goods & burial Goods == Excavations have uncovered: * '''Copper mirrors (fragments)''' * '''Green jasper arrowheads''' * '''Magatama beads''' * '''Iron swords and blades''' * '''Wheel-shaped stone object (碧玉製車輪石, hekigyoku-sei sharinseki)''' * '''Haniwa clay figures''', including: ** '''[[Cylindrical Haniwa|Cylindrical haniwa]] (円筒埴輪)''' ** '''Fin-shaped haniwa (鰭付円筒埴輪)''' ** '''[[Figural Haniwa|House-shaped haniwa]] (家形埴輪)''' == Current Condition == The '''mound is well preserved''', and due to '''lack of tree cover''', the '''three-tiered structure is clearly visible'''. == Access == * '''20-minute walk from [[Tenri Station]]''' - Located '''500 meters south''' of the '''Tenri University Reference Museum''' * '''Just north''' of '''Tenri Middle School''' == designation1 == === '''National Historic Site of stone arrowheads, iron sword fragments, magatama, and haniwa |alternate_name = National Historic Site (Historic Site1 April 8, 1927) |map = Japan Nara |type = Zenpō-kōhō-fun-W }} '''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in Somanouchi Town, [[:en:Tenri, Nara|Tenri]], [[:en:Nara Prefecture|Nara Prefecture]], Japan. It is Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site and is part of the [[:en:Somanouchi Kofun cluster|Somanouchi Kofun cluster]]. == Overview == Constructed during the early [[:en:Kofun period|Kofun period]] (4th century), Nishiyama Kofun is the oldest of the [[:en:Somanouchi Kofun cluster|Somanouchi Kofun cluster]]. The Kofun features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=}} at its base to a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] at its upper levels. The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day [[:en:Kashiwara|Kashiwara]]), was targeted. == area and burial == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * '''Rear mound (posterior):''' 94m width, 16m height * '''Anterior mound:''' 72m width, 13m height The lower tier types a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in. Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan. Its combination of construction styles is believed to be intentional, reflecting a transitional phase in kofun design. == burial goods == Excavations have yielded: * '''Posterior mound:''' ** ''' Mirror fragments''' ** '''Greenstone arrowheads''' ** '''Magatama beads''' ** '''Iron sword fragments''' * '''Moat (south side):''' ** ''' Greenstone wheel stones''' * '''Surface burial goods:''' ** ''' Stone paving (fukiishi)''' ** '''Haniwa fragments (cylindrical, finned, house-shaped)''' == Current State == The tumulus is well-preserved, with no significant vegetation on its surface, allowing clear observation of its tiered structure. == Access == * 20 minutes on foot from Tenri Station. * Located 500 meters south of the [[:en:Tenri University Sankōkan Museum|Tenri University Sankokan Museum]] and adjacent to Tenri Junior High School. == Cultural Significance == === National Historic Site === * Designated on April 8, 1927{{国cultural property等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}}. * In 2018, Nishinorikura Kofun was added to the Historic Site1 area, renaming the site "Somanouchi Kofun Group."Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 19, February 13, 2018. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * [[:en:Somanouchi Kofun cluster|Somanouchi Kofun cluster]] == External Links == * {{国cultural property等データベース|401|1958|西山古墳}} * [http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html Tenri City Kofun Guide] {{otheruses|Nishiyama Kofun in Tenri, Nara|Nishiyama Kofun in Ota, Gunma|Nishiyama Kofun (Ota)}} {{Infobox Kofun | name = Nishiyama Kofun | native_name = 西山古墳 | image = [[File:Nishiyama Kofun, zenkei-1.jpg|280px]]
Mound overview (left: front section, back right: rear section) | location = [[:en:Tenri, Nara|Tenri, Nara]], Nara Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = 34.5925 | coordinates = 135.8433 | region = Japan | type = {{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoho-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=}} (rectangular keyhole-shaped tumulus) | length = 183m, Height: 13m | burial = {{ill|Tateana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=竪穴式石室|4=zh|5=豎穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tateana-shiki sekishitsu|13=User:Immanuelle/Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} (pit-style stone chamber) | built = Early Kofun period (4th century) | person = Possibly a member of the [[:en:Mononobe clan|Mononobe clan]] | burial goods = Mirrors, stone arrowheads, iron swords and blades, magatama beads, haniwa clay figures | Historic Site1 = National Historic Site of Japan (Historic Site1 April 8, 1927) }} '''Nishiyama Kofun''' (西山古墳) is a '''large [[Zenpō-kōhō-fun|rectangular keyhole-shaped tumulus]] (前方後方墳, zenpō-kōhō-fun)''' located in '''[[:en:Tenri, Nara|Tenri, Nara]], Nara Prefecture, Japan'''. It is part of the '''[[:en:Somanouchi Kofun cluster|Somanouchi Kofun cluster]]''' and is the '''largest kofun of its type in Japan'''. In '''1927 (Showa 2)''', it was '''Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site''' of Japan.{{Cite web|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/1958|title=Nishiyama Kofun - National Historic Site|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|access-date=2024-01-30}} It is also known by the '''alternate name "Nagariyama" (勾山, Magariyama).''' == Overview == The kofun was '''constructed during the early [[Kofun period]] (4th century)''' and is one of the '''earliest tumuli''' in the '''[[:en:Somanouchi Kofun cluster|Somanouchi Kofun cluster]]'''. The mound originally had a '''[[Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|pit-style stone chamber]] (竪穴式石室, tateana-shiki sekishitsu)''', but it was likely '''looted in antiquity'''.Izumimori, Ko. *Ancient Tombs of Yamato I* (『大和の古墳I』), Jinbun Shoin, 2003. During '''World War II''', the Japanese Imperial Army '''stationed an anti-aircraft gun battery''' at the site. At that time, stones from the '''burial chamber (originally quarried in Kashiwara, Osaka)''' were reportedly '''removed''' and repurposed.On-site intypeation board by the Tenri City Board of Education. == burial & area == [[File:080515 Nishiyama Kofun aerial.jpg|thumb|250px|Aerial view of Nishiyama Kofun.
{{National Aerial Photography}}.
[[:File:Tenri-nishiyama_stereo.jpg|Stereo image here]]]] The tumulus is a '''three-tiered, [[Zenpō-kōhō-fun|rectangular keyhole-shaped mound]] (前方後方墳, [[zenpō-kōhō-fun]])''' with the front section '''oriented westward'''. Its area are: * '''Total length''': 183 meters * '''Rear section''' (square): 94m wide × 16m high * '''Front section''': 72m wide The '''lower level''' is '''rectangular''', while the '''middle and upper levels''' are '''rounder''', creating a hybrid '''keyhole-shaped mound (前方後円形, zenpō-kōenkei)'''. The '''central burial chamber''' is estimated to be a '''[[Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|pit-style stone chamber]]''' based on '''historical records'''. The mound is positioned '''along three natural ridges''', with the '''central ridge typeing the main mound''', while the '''north and south ridges serve as outer embankments'''. A '''moat once surrounded the mound''', but it has since been '''filled in'''. This kofun is '''the largest of its kind in Japan'''. The '''unique construction''', with a '''rectangular lower tier supporting a rounder upper structure''', is believed to be '''original to its design'''. == burial goods & burial Goods == Excavations have uncovered: * '''Copper mirrors (fragments)''' * '''Green jasper arrowheads''' * '''Magatama beads''' * '''Iron swords and blades''' * '''Wheel-shaped stone object (碧玉製車輪石, hekigyoku-sei sharinseki)''' * '''Haniwa clay figures''', including: ** '''[[Cylindrical Haniwa|Cylindrical haniwa]] (円筒埴輪)''' ** '''Fin-shaped haniwa (鰭付円筒埴輪)''' ** '''[[Figural Haniwa|House-shaped haniwa]] (家形埴輪)''' == Current Condition == The '''mound is well preserved''', and due to '''lack of tree cover''', the '''three-tiered structure is clearly visible'''. == Access == * '''20-minute walk from [[Tenri Station]]''' - Located '''500 meters south''' of the '''Tenri University Reference Museum''' * '''Just north''' of '''Tenri Middle School''' == designation1 == === '''National Historic Site of Japan''' === * '''Original Historic Site (1927)''': Nishiyama Kofun was Historic Site1 a '''National Historic Site'''. * '''Expansion (2018)''': The Historic Site was '''expanded''' to include '''Nishinorikura Kofun (西乗鞍古墳)''', renaming the site as the '''Somanochi Kofun Group (杣之内古墳群)'''.Ministry of Education, Science and Culture Announcement No. 19 (February 13, 2018). == References == cluster|Somanouchi Kofun cluster]] == External Links == {{Commonscat|Nishiyama Kofun}} * [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/1958 '''Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan): Nishiyama Kofun'''] * [http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/kanko/kohun_guide/kohun/index.html '''Tenri City Official Kofun Guide'''] {{Kofun navbar}} {{translated page|ja|西山古墳|version=96134985|comment=Imported full Its area are: * '''Total length''': 183 meters * '''Rear section''' (square): 94m wide × 16m high * '''Front section''': 72m wide The '''lower level''' is '''rectangular''', while the '''middle and upper levels''' are '''rounder''', creating a hybrid '''keyhole-shaped mound (前方後円形, zenpō-kōenkei)'''. A '''moat once surrounded the mound''', but it has since been '''filled in'''. This kofun is '''the largest of its kind in Japan'''. (西山古墳) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in Somanouchi Town, [[:en:Tenri, Nara|Tenri]], [[:en:Nara Prefecture|Nara Prefecture]], Japan. It is Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site and is part of the [[:en:Somanouchi Kofun cluster|Somanouchi Kofun cluster]]. == Overview == Constructed during the early [[:en:Kofun period|Kofun period]] (4th century), Nishiyama Kofun is the oldest of the [[:en:Somanouchi Kofun cluster|Somanouchi Kofun cluster]]. The Kofun features a unique combination of construction styles, transitioning from a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=}} at its base to a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] at its upper levels. The tomb was partially disturbed during WWII when it was repurposed for anti-aircraft defense. Evidence of looting suggests that its burial chamber, constructed from stone sourced from Kashiwabara (present-day [[:en:Kashiwara|Kashiwara]]), was targeted. == area and burial == The tumulus measures 183 meters in length and features a three-tiered construction: * '''Rear mound (posterior):''' 94m width, 16m height * '''Anterior mound:''' 72m width, 13m height The lower tier types a classic {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=}} with a square posterior mound (90m sides) and a matching anterior mound. The middle and upper tiers, however, resemble a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] with a circular posterior section (72m diameter) and a narrower anterior projection. The posterior mound height reaches 15 meters, while the anterior mound height is 10 meters. Surrounding the tumulus was a stepped moat system, now mostly filled in. Nishiyama Kofun is the largest example of its type in Japan.
